name: Accent color
definition: The one saturated colour an interface spends sparingly on the things it wants clicked, so its rarity is what makes it read as important.
useWhen: the one colour reserved for the primary action
notes: The CSS accent-color property (which tints checkboxes and range inputs) is a distinct enough sense that it may deserve its own tail entry.

name: Access key
definition: A single letter, usually shown underlined, that jumps straight to a menu or control once the access modifier is held.
useWhen: the underlined letter that reaches a menu item
notes: Windows calls it an access key, general HCI literature calls it a mnemonic; keep both as aliases.

name: Accessibility annotation
definition: Notes attached to a design file that spell out the things a mockup cannot show: heading levels, focus order, names, roles, live regions, and alt text.
useWhen: handing a design over without losing the semantics

name: Accessibility grouping
definition: Collapsing a cluster of elements, an icon plus a label plus a value, into one thing assistive technology stops at, instead of three stops that mean nothing apart.
useWhen: a card reads as five fragments instead of one item

name: Accessibility overlay
definition: A third party script bolted onto a site with a promise of automatic compliance, usually a floating widget of font and contrast toggles that fixes nothing underneath.
useWhen: someone proposes buying a widget instead of fixing
notes: Contested term with a strong consensus against the products; the entry should carry that consensus rather than stay neutral.

name: Accessibility trait
definition: The platform flag on a native view that says what it is and how it behaves, the mobile counterpart to a role plus a state, and the thing a custom control has to set by hand.
useWhen: a custom native control announces as plain text

sources.title: Deque: What iOS traits actually do
Mobile A11y: iOS UIKit accessibility traits

name: Accessibility tree
definition: The parallel tree a browser derives from the DOM, holding the role, name, state, and value that assistive technology actually reads.
useWhen: talking about what AT sees rather than what renders

name: Accessible authentication
definition: A sign-in route that never requires a cognitive function test such as recalling a password or solving a puzzle without offering an alternative.
useWhen: a login demands memory or puzzle solving

name: Accessible description
definition: Supplementary text announced after a control's name, carrying hint or error detail without becoming part of the name itself.
useWhen: extra detail that should follow the name, not replace it

sources.title: APG: Providing Accessible Names and Descriptions

name: Accessible name
definition: The string assistive technology announces for a control, computed from label, aria-labelledby, aria-label, or its own content in a fixed order of precedence.
useWhen: asking what a control is actually called out loud

sources.title: APG: Providing Accessible Names and Descriptions

name: Achievement badge
definition: A collectible marker awarded for a milestone and displayed on a profile, often shown greyed out before it is earned so the set is visible.
useWhen: the collectible award shown on a profile
notes: badge already exists on the site as the small count or status marker; this is the gamification sense and needs a contrastWith edge, not a merge.

name: Acid graphics
definition: A 2020s rave revival style of chrome and liquid 3D objects, warped and stretched lettering, clashing saturated color on near black, smileys, globes, and wireframe motifs.
useWhen: chrome, warped type, and rave motifs used ironically

sources.title: AIGA Eye on Design: Acid graphics are the new psychedelia

notes: Rooted in 1990s acid house flyers rather than 1960s psychedelia, and carries irony where the 60s style carried optimism.

name: Action list
definition: A vertical list of commands with icons, descriptions and dividers, the shared body used inside menus, panels and side sheets.
useWhen: a list of commands reused inside several surfaces
notes: Primer's split of ActionList (the body) from ActionMenu (the trigger and popover) is the clearest statement of why this is its own component.

name: Active descendant
definition: A focus technique where DOM focus stays on a container or input and aria-activedescendant names which child is active, used when focus must not move.
useWhen: the typing field must keep focus while a list moves

name: Activity feed
definition: A reverse chronological list of things that happened, each entry naming an actor, a verb, and an object, grouped when many are alike.
useWhen: the running list of who did what, most recent first

name: Adaptive layout
definition: A layout that switches between a few discrete arrangements chosen per size class, rather than flowing continuously as the window changes.
useWhen: distinguishing snapping between layouts from fluid reflow
notes: The adaptive versus responsive distinction is the whole entry; treat it as a contrastWith pair.

name: Additive animation
definition: Composing an animation on top of whatever is already animating the same property instead of replacing it, so a second nudge adds to the first rather than restarting it.
useWhen: a repeated trigger should stack rather than snap back to the start

sources.title: CSS-Tricks: additive animation with the Web Animations API

notes: Deep vocabulary, but it is the reason a rapidly retriggered nudge or shake reads as one motion instead of a stutter.

name: Address autocomplete
definition: Replacing a set of address fields with one lookup that suggests full addresses after a few characters and fills the rest on selection.
useWhen: typing a postcode fills in the whole address

name: Affordance
definition: What an element makes possible for the person using it, such as a surface that can be pushed, dragged, or scrolled.
useWhen: naming what an element allows a person to do

name: Afrofuturism
definition: A style that pictures technology through the African diaspora, combining cosmic imagery, textile and mask pattern, gold and indigo, and geometric ornament used structurally.
useWhen: a future told through African diaspora imagery
notes: Cultural movement first and a visual style second, so a term page has to say that rather than reduce it to pattern and palette.

name: All caps
definition: Text set entirely in capitals, which reads slower than mixed case because the word's outline shape disappears.
useWhen: short labels that must shout, never sentences

sources.title: Title case vs sentence case in UI

name: Alpha channel
definition: The transparency component carried inside a colour value itself, which lets a border or fill blend with whatever surface it lands on instead of assuming one.
useWhen: a colour that must blend with an unknown background

name: Alpha compositing
definition: The arithmetic that combines a translucent layer with what is beneath it, and the reason two stacked 50 percent layers do not add up to fully opaque.
useWhen: predicting the result of stacking translucent layers
notes: Premultiplied versus straight alpha is a strong candidate for its own tail entry if canonicalize wants the split.

name: Alt text
definition: The text alternative that stands in for an image, written to serve the same purpose in the same context rather than to describe every detail.
useWhen: writing what an image says when it cannot be seen

name: Analogous colors
definition: A palette built from hues that neighbour each other on the wheel, giving a calm scheme with no colour fighting another for attention.
useWhen: a quiet palette of neighbouring hues

name: Anchor positioning
definition: A CSS mechanism that tethers one element to another, sizing and placing it against its anchor and trying fallback positions when the default one would overflow.
useWhen: pinning one element to another without JavaScript
notes: The platform answer to what floating-ui does in script. position-try-fallbacks is the vocabulary designers actually need: what happens when the tooltip hits the edge.

name: Anti-design
definition: A deliberately awkward style that breaks layout, type, and color conventions so the interface reads as a statement rather than as a polished product.
useWhen: the rule breaking is the message

sources.title: Envato: Minimalism vs. Maximalism: Battle of the Divisive Design Styles

notes: Frequently conflated with brutalism; the discrimination is intent (statement) versus method (exposed structure).

name: Anticipation
definition: A small move in the opposite direction just before the main one, borrowed from character animation to telegraph what is about to happen.
useWhen: an action needs a wind-up so it does not start cold

sources.title: IxDF: UI Animation, applying Disney's 12 principles to UI

notes: One of the twelve Disney principles that survives translation to UI. GSAP's ScrollTrigger anticipatePin is an unrelated use of the same word.

name: APCA
definition: A perceptual contrast algorithm proposed for WCAG 3 that scores a text and background pair as an Lc value and takes font size and weight into account.
useWhen: scoring contrast in a way that accounts for text size and weight

sources.title: Radix Colors: understanding the scale (quotes Lc 60 and Lc 90)

notes: Tail gold: Radix guarantees its step 11 and 12 text against step 2 in Lc, not in WCAG ratio.

name: Aperture
definition: The partly enclosed opening in a letter such as the gap at the bottom of a lowercase e or the mouth of a c.
useWhen: explaining why one sans feels more legible at small sizes

name: App shell
definition: The persistent frame of an application, its header, navigation and footer, that stays put while only the content region swaps as you move around.
useWhen: naming the part of the app that never reloads

sources.title: Instant Loading Web Apps with an Application Shell Architecture

notes: Two senses in the wild: the visual frame (design vocabulary) and the cached HTML/CSS/JS bundle (PWA performance vocabulary). Define the visual sense, mention the second.

name: App shortcut
definition: A short menu of app actions hung off the app icon itself, opened by a long press or a secondary click before the app is even running.
useWhen: a frequent action should skip the app launch

sources.title: Apple HIG: Home Screen quick actions

notes: HIG itself ties Dock menus and Home Screen quick actions together as one idea, so they are merged here. Not to be confused with the separate HIG App Shortcuts page, which is about App Intents and Siri.

name: App silhouette
definition: The recognisable outline of an app's chrome, which bars and panes it has and where they sit, used to classify one app's layout against another's.
useWhen: classifying an app by the shape of its chrome
notes: Windows names four: top navigation, menu bar, left navigation, tab view. A good vocabulary word for the thing designers point at when they say an app looks like Settings.

name: Applied filters
definition: A row of removable tokens above the results showing every filter currently in force, with a control to clear them all at once.
useWhen: the removable tags showing which filters are on
notes: chip already exists on the site; this is the pattern that uses chips, so it needs a contrastWith edge rather than a merge.

name: Aqua
definition: Apple's early Mac OS X look of glossy blue gel buttons, pinstripes, gumdrop window controls, and a pulsing default button.
useWhen: candy-gel Mac controls from the 2000s
notes: Introduced January 2000, shipped in Mac OS X 10.0; flattened out from OS X Yosemite in 2014.

name: Arc motion
definition: Moving an element along a curved path rather than a straight line, so a change of position reads as natural rather than mechanical.
useWhen: an element travels in two axes at once

sources.title: IxDF: UI Animation, applying Disney's 12 principles to UI

name: ARIA notify
definition: A proposed API for speaking a message directly to assistive technology, without the live region trick of mutating hidden text and hoping the timing works out.
useWhen: an announcement has no element it belongs to
notes: Proposal stage. Worth a record because live-region workarounds are usually explained by contrast with it.

name: Art Deco
definition: A 1920s luxury style of strict symmetry, stepped and fanned geometry, strong vertical emphasis, metallic gold on deep color, and high contrast display capitals.
useWhen: symmetrical geometric luxury, gold on deep color

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions
Big Human: 12 graphic design styles, a complete guide for 2026

notes: Reaches interfaces mainly through display type, borders, and frame ornament rather than through control design.

name: Art Nouveau
definition: A turn of the century style of whiplash curves, botanical line ornament, muted jewel tones, and lettering drawn to fit the frame rather than set on a grid.
useWhen: botanical line ornament and curved frames

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions

notes: Reaches the screen mostly as ornament and border art; its lettering is the direct ancestor of the psychedelic poster style.

name: Ascender
definition: The part of a lowercase letter such as b, d, or h that rises above the x-height.
useWhen: naming the strokes that reach above lowercase height

name: Aspect ratio box
definition: A container that holds a fixed width to height proportion whatever its size, so media reserves its space before it loads.
useWhen: reserving the right shaped hole before an image arrives

name: Asymmetric easing
definition: Giving a state change and its reverse different curves or durations, usually a quick confident exit and a slower entrance, so the two directions do not feel identical.
useWhen: opening and closing should not be mirror images
notes: Sits between easing and motion-token: the token sets say the same thing with named accelerate and decelerate curves.

name: Atomic live region
definition: A live region setting that makes assistive technology re-read the whole region when any part of it changes, instead of only the changed fragment.
useWhen: a partial update would be read out of context

name: Attract mode
definition: A self-playing loop an idle screen falls into to demonstrate itself, inherited from arcade cabinets and reused by kiosks and product demos.
useWhen: an unattended screen should demonstrate itself

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: The site's own stage uses this word, which makes the entry self-demonstrating. Could sit in pattern instead of motion.

name: Attribute editor
definition: A repeating row of key and value fields with add and remove controls, used for tags, headers and other open ended pairs.
useWhen: a form section that repeats a row of fields
notes: Focus management after removing a row is the accessibility detail worth demonstrating.

name: Audio control
definition: A way to stop sound that started on its own, because autoplaying audio drowns out the screen reader voice a reader depends on to find the control that stops it.
useWhen: anything makes noise before the reader asked

name: Audio description
definition: A narration track describing visual information the soundtrack leaves out, fitted into the gaps between dialogue.
useWhen: the picture carries information the audio does not

name: Auditory icon
definition: A recorded everyday sound standing for an event, so a crumple means delete by resembling the act rather than by convention learned in the interface.
useWhen: the sound that reports an event by resembling it
notes: Coined by Bill Gaver in 1986; VERIFY before asserting. Wikipedia covers both this and earcon on the Earcon page, so both terms share the source. Round-mate contrast pair with earcon, and the demos must not look alike.

name: Aurora UI
definition: A style whose background is built from heavily blurred color blobs that glow and drift like the northern lights behind the content.
useWhen: the background is soft glowing bands of color

sources.title: Hype4 Academy: Aurora UI, new visual trend for 2021
Superdesign: Aurora UI: The CSS Gradient Recipe, Real Examples, and When It Breaks

notes: Coined by Michal Malewicz in 2020/2021. Distinguish from mesh gradient: aurora is the dark, often animated northern-lights case.

name: Autosave
definition: Persisting the reader's work continuously without a save action, usually with a quiet status line reporting when the last save happened.
useWhen: work is kept without anyone pressing save

name: Back to top
definition: A control that appears after the reader has scrolled some distance and returns them to the top of the page in one action.
useWhen: the button that appears partway down to send you back up
notes: iframe demo: the trigger threshold is a property of the document scroller.

name: Baseline
definition: The invisible line that most letters sit on, and the line every other vertical type metric is measured from.
useWhen: aligning text with an icon or another line of text
notes: Anchor term for the whole metrics cluster.

name: Baseline grid
definition: A set of evenly spaced horizontal lines that every line of text sits on, so type in adjacent columns lines up across the page.
useWhen: text in neighbouring columns must line up
notes: Cross category candidate with typography (it sits next to leading, already on the site). Kept in layout because it governs the page, not the face.

name: Bauhaus style
definition: A style reduced to primary red, yellow, and blue on off-white, elementary circles, triangles, and squares, and undecorated sans serif type, following form follows function.
useWhen: primary colors and elementary shapes doing the work

sources.title: Digital Heroes: Bauhaus web design, form follows function revival
Inkbot Design: 20 iconic graphic design styles

notes: Ancestor of swiss-style and of flat-design; the three are often conflated in trend writing, and the primary palette is what separates this one.

name: Bevel and emboss
definition: Light and dark edges drawn along a shape's border so it reads as raised or carved, the depth trick behind classic desktop buttons.
useWhen: a raised edge drawn from a light and a dark border
notes: CSS still ships border-style: outset/inset/ridge/groove for exactly this; a good specimen shows all four.

name: Bidirectional text
definition: Text mixing a right-to-left script with left-to-right runs such as numbers or Latin words, where each run keeps its own direction.
useWhen: Arabic or Hebrew text containing Latin or digits
notes: Arguably layout or accessibility; recorded as typography because the subject is how text sets.

name: Biophilic design
definition: A style that borrows from the natural world on purpose, using earthy greens and clays, organic silhouettes, botanical imagery, and slow ambient motion to make a screen feel less mechanical.
useWhen: nature borrowed deliberately for calm, not decoration

sources.title: Silphium Design: Understanding biophilia in digital design

notes: Biomimetic is folded in as an alias but is not strictly a synonym: biophilia is about evoking nature, biomimicry about copying how nature works.

name: Blend mode
definition: A formula for combining a layer's colour with the colour behind it, such as multiply or screen or overlay, instead of simply covering it.
useWhen: combining layers by a formula rather than by covering
notes: The isolation property (stopping a blend at a stacking context) is a plausible separate tail entry.

name: Organic blob
definition: A soft irregular shape with no straight edges, used as a background accent or image mask to soften a strictly rectangular layout.
useWhen: an amoeba shape softening a rectangular grid
notes: Made in CSS with eight-value border-radius, or with an SVG path.

name: Bottom sheet
definition: A surface anchored to the bottom edge that slides up over the content, often draggable between a peeked and an expanded height.
useWhen: a panel that rises from the bottom edge
notes: The site already has drawer, so this record must argue the edge and the drag, not just the overlay. Vaul row needs a probe.

name: Bounce
definition: Motion that arrives, rebounds, and arrives again in decreasing amounts, reading as an object landing on a surface.
useWhen: an arrival should read as landing, with weight

name: Box
definition: A bordered container, optionally titled, that groups logically related controls so the grouping is drawn rather than implied by spacing alone.
useWhen: grouping controls with a visible boundary
notes: Overlaps fieldset in the component sweep: a box is the visual grouping device, a fieldset is the form semantics. Windows calls it a group box, SwiftUI a GroupBox.

name: Braille display
definition: A refreshable braille row that renders the same accessibility tree as speech, with abbreviated role names authors can override.
useWhen: output is a braille line, not synthesized speech

name: Brand color
definition: The colour an organisation owns in a customer's memory, carried into a product as the seed for its palette rather than used directly on every surface.
useWhen: the colour the company owns, before it becomes UI tokens

name: Breakout
definition: A track wider than the reading column but narrower than the viewport, used for figures and code that need more room than prose.
useWhen: a figure that needs more width than the text

sources.title: Layout Breakouts with CSS Grid, Ryan Mulligan

notes: Usually implemented as a named grid track set (full, breakout, content). The named track diagram is the demo.

name: Breakpoint
definition: A viewport width at which a layout is allowed to change shape, defined once so every screen in a system reflows at the same places.
useWhen: the widths where the layout is allowed to change

implementations.name: Breakpoints (xs, sm, md, lg, xl, xxl)

notes: iframe because the subject is the viewport itself; a shadow root cannot make media queries fire.

name: Broken grid
definition: A composition that sets up a grid and then deliberately violates it, overlapping and offsetting elements to create tension.
useWhen: breaking the grid on purpose, not by accident
notes: Round two folded in "asymmetric grid" from the uiterms glossary, where it means columns of deliberately uneven width; canonicalize may want to split that sense out from overlapping and offsetting.

name: Browse mode
definition: The screen reader mode that intercepts keystrokes for reading and navigation, as opposed to focus or forms mode where keys reach the page.
useWhen: explaining why a key press never reached your widget

sources.title: Accessibility Developer Guide: Browse and focus modes
Tink: Understanding screen reader interaction modes

notes: Tail gold. Absorbs 'virtual cursor' as an alias rather than a separate entry.

name: Brutalist web design
definition: A raw style that leaves the document showing: system or monospace type, default link blue, hard borders, and no decoration beyond structure.
useWhen: the page looks like unstyled HTML on purpose

sources.title: Superdesign: Brutalist Web Design: CSS Recipe, Live Examples and Trend Data

notes: Distinct from neubrutalism: brutalism deletes decoration, neubrutalism adds thick outlines and hard shadows.

name: Bubble toolbar
definition: A small formatting bar that appears floating over a text selection and disappears when the selection is dropped.
useWhen: the toolbar appears over the text you just selected
notes: Named by editor libraries (Tiptap BubbleMenu, ProseMirror) rather than by design systems, so implementations need a dedicated probe.

name: Bulk actions
definition: Selecting several rows and applying one command to all of them, usually through a bar that appears once a selection exists and reports its count.
useWhen: picking many rows and acting on them at once

name: Busy state
definition: Marking a region as still loading so assistive technology waits for the finished result instead of reading each row as it streams in.
useWhen: a region updates in pieces and each piece speaks

name: Button versus link
definition: The rule that decides which element to use: a link goes somewhere, a button does something, and the choice sets the keyboard, the cursor, and the announced role.
useWhen: a control looks like a button but navigates

name: Bypassing pattern
definition: A scanning shape where readers deliberately skip the opening words of each line because every line in a list starts the same way.
useWhen: arguing against repeated leading words in lists

sources.title: F-Shaped Pattern of Reading on the Web, NN/g

notes: The evidence behind front loading list items with the word that differs.

name: Calendar
definition: A month grid of dates that can be read, navigated and selected from, whether standing alone or living inside a date field.
useWhen: a month laid out as a grid of days
notes: Keyboard support is a grid, not a list, which is the interesting half of the entry.

name: Canonical layout
definition: One of a small set of proven multi pane arrangements a platform recommends, such as list detail, supporting pane and feed, instead of a new layout per screen.
useWhen: reaching for a proven arrangement, not a new one
notes: The parent term for list-detail, supporting-pane and feed-layout, which round one captured individually. Material moved the page from canonical-examples to canonical-layouts; both paths appear in search.

name: Cap height
definition: The height of a capital letter measured from the baseline, and the edge designers usually mean when they say text should line up flush.
useWhen: aligning a heading optically instead of by its box

name: CAPTCHA
definition: A challenge placed in a form to sort people from scripts, from distorted text to a single checkbox that watches how you got there.
useWhen: the challenge that proves you are a person
notes: accessibility.json already holds accessible-authentication, which is where the WCAG argument against CAPTCHAs lives. Keep the two linked.

name: Captions
definition: Synchronised text for a video's audio, including speaker changes and meaningful sound, distinct from subtitles which only translate dialogue.
useWhen: text that carries the sound of a video, not a translation
notes: Slug avoids colliding with a typography 'caption' (figure caption); canonicalize should keep both apart.

name: Card flip
definition: Rotating a card about its own axis to show a second face on the back, with the hidden face pre-rotated and its backface hidden so only one side is ever visible.
useWhen: one surface carries two faces and both are the same object

sources.title: David DeSandro: card flip, intro to CSS 3D transforms
Auroratide: a (more) realistic card flip animation

notes: Not to be confused with the existing flip-animation entry, which records the FLIP technique (First Last Invert Play). Two unrelated meanings of one word, and the collision is itself worth writing about.

name: Card grid
definition: Content laid out as equal width cards flowing across a responsive grid and wrapping to new rows as space allows.
useWhen: many peers of the same kind, browsed by scanning
notes: Contrast set with masonry (already on the site) and bento-grid (already on the site): even rows versus ragged versus deliberately unequal cells.

name: Caret
definition: The blinking marker showing where typed text will be inserted, moved by clicking, by arrow keys, or by dragging on touch.
useWhen: the text insertion marker, not the mouse pointer
notes: Name collision worth calling out: caret also names the small triangle glyph on a dropdown trigger.

name: Cascader
definition: A select whose options open level by level, each choice narrowing the next, used for country then state then city style data.
useWhen: choosing down a hierarchy one level at a time
notes: Miller columns is the older name from the Finder column view and deserves a mention in the article.

name: Cassette futurism
definition: The analog future of late 1970s science fiction: beige and putty plastic, chunky toggles and rocker switches, amber or green CRT readouts, and monochrome bitmap type.
useWhen: a future built from 1970s and 80s analog hardware
notes: Distinguished from synthwave and vaporwave by materiality: worn utilitarian hardware rather than neon and gradients.

name: Categorical palette
definition: A data palette of distinct hues at roughly equal visual weight, used for groups that have no order so no colour reads as larger than another.
useWhen: colouring unordered groups without implying rank

name: Ch unit
definition: A CSS length equal to the advance width of the digit zero in the current font, used to set column widths in characters rather than pixels.
useWhen: setting a column width in characters, not pixels

name: Change of context
definition: A shift big enough to disorient a reader, a new page, a new window, a moved focus, a rearranged form, and the rule that it should follow a request rather than a keystroke.
useWhen: naming the surprise a select or focus event should not cause

name: Character key shortcuts
definition: Single letter shortcuts that fire without a modifier, which must be switchable off or remappable because speech input and screen readers trigger them by accident.
useWhen: a bare letter key does something on the page

name: Chart
definition: A drawing of data in which position, length, angle or colour carries the numbers, chosen so the comparison a reader needs is the easiest one to see.
useWhen: numbers are easier compared by eye than by reading
notes: Round one caught sparkline and gauge but not the head term above them. The article should carry the encoding choice (position beats angle beats area) rather than a chart type list.

name: Chat bubble
definition: A rounded container for one message in a conversation, aligned and coloured by who sent it, often with a tail toward the sender's side.
useWhen: one message in a conversation view
notes: Newly standard vocabulary: several systems added chat components in 2024 and 2025 for assistant interfaces.

name: Check answers
definition: A review screen listing everything the reader entered, with a change link beside each answer, shown before the submission is final.
useWhen: a summary screen lets you review and edit before submitting

name: Chevron
definition: The small angle bracket used as a directional marker: down means this opens, right means this goes deeper, in breadcrumbs it means next level.
useWhen: naming the little angle arrow on a control
notes: Collides with typography's caret (the text insertion point) and with the CSS caret-color property, which typography.json already covers.

name: Chorded shortcut
definition: A shortcut whose keys are held down together like a chord, in contrast to one typed as a sequence of separate presses.
useWhen: keys pressed together rather than one after another

name: Motion choreography
definition: The plan for how several animating elements relate in time and space, deciding what leads, what follows, and what stays still.
useWhen: more than one thing moves and the order matters
notes: The site's own attract mode uses 'choreography' as a code term; the dictionary sense here is the design-system one.

name: Chroma
definition: Colourfulness measured in absolute terms rather than as a percentage of the maximum, so a light pastel and a dark ink can be compared on one scale.
useWhen: comparing colourfulness across colours of different lightness
notes: The word that separates OKLCH from HSL: chroma is unbounded and hue dependent, saturation is a percentage.

name: Chrome
definition: The parts of a window or app that frame content rather than being content: title bars, toolbars, tab strips and address bars.
useWhen: separating the frame from the thing being framed
notes: Predates the browser named Chrome, which is exactly why people are confused by it. This site's own SPEC uses chrome in this sense.

name: Chunking
definition: Breaking content into small labelled pieces, short paragraphs, lists, and headings, so a reader can hold one piece at a time instead of the whole wall.
useWhen: a dense block has to be read by anyone tired

sources.title: W3C: Keep Text Succinct (cognitive accessibility design pattern)

notes: Overlaps typography and content design; filed here because the cited pattern is cognitive accessibility guidance.

name: Claymorphism
definition: A soft style where controls look inflated from clay: pastel fills, very large corner radii, an inner highlight, and a tinted drop shadow.
useWhen: puffy pastel surfaces that look moulded

sources.title: Wow-How: 4 Main Types of Morphism in UI Design

name: Click-through
definition: A click that both focuses an inactive surface and reaches the control underneath, instead of being spent activating the window first.
useWhen: the first click also does the thing, or does not

sources.title: LWN: Focus follows mouse or click to focus?

notes: Also used in CSS sense (pointer-events: none makes an overlay click-through). Two meanings worth disambiguating in the article.

name: Cloning
definition: Spawning a new element visibly out of an existing one so the reader can see where it came from, rather than having it arrive from nowhere.
useWhen: a new object must be traceable to the thing that made it

sources.title: UX Magazine: creating usability with motion, the UX in Motion Manifesto
The 12 principles of UX in motion

notes: Close to origin-aware-animation and container-transform; the distinction is that the source stays put and a copy leaves it. Merge candidate.

name: Close button
definition: The small dismiss control in the corner of a dialog, banner or panel, drawn as an X and named Close rather than X.
useWhen: the little X that dismisses a surface
notes: Small enough that most systems ship it as its own component, which is the argument for it being a term.

name: Cluster
definition: A layout primitive that lays items of differing widths out like words in a paragraph, wrapping to new lines with even gaps in both directions.
useWhen: tags or buttons of mixed widths that must wrap neatly

name: Coach mark
definition: A temporary message anchored to a control that teaches what it does, often chained into a numbered sequence across a screen.
useWhen: a teaching bubble pointing at a control
notes: The multi step tour built from these is arguably a pattern; this record is the single bubble.

name: Code editor
definition: A text area specialised for code, with a gutter of line numbers, syntax colouring and a caret that understands indentation.
useWhen: an editing surface built for code
notes: layout.json already holds gutter in the CSS grid sense; the editor gutter is a different sense of the same word and the merge step should notice.

name: Cognitive load
definition: The mental effort an interface demands, split between the work the task really needs and the work the design added by way of clutter, jargon, and avoidable steps.
useWhen: a screen is correct but exhausting to use

sources.title: W3C WAI: Cognitive Accessibility at W3C

notes: Sits on the border with the pattern category; nothing in the other files claims it, so it is filed here with its cognitive accessibility framing.

name: Collapsing toolbar
definition: A header that shrinks as the page scrolls, trading its large title and image for a compact bar that stays available.
useWhen: a header must stay reachable without keeping its height
notes: Cross-category candidate with component; relates directly to the existing app-bar entry.

name: Color alias
definition: A second name pointing at an existing scale so one palette can answer to several meanings, letting yellow serve as both warning and pending without duplication.
useWhen: one scale answering to more than one meaning
notes: Merge candidate with semantic-color and primitive-color-token; the three describe one layered system from different angles.

name: Color banding
definition: The visible stripes that appear across a gradient when a display or file cannot render enough intermediate steps to keep the transition smooth.
useWhen: a gradient breaking into visible stripes
notes: Tail gold and highly demoable: one wide, low-contrast gradient shows it immediately.

name: Color font
definition: A font whose glyphs carry their own colors, gradients, or layers, with a palette the page can override rather than a single ink.
useWhen: type that carries its own colors

name: Color gamut
definition: The set of colours a space or a display can actually produce, which is why a value that is legal in one notation can be impossible on a given screen.
useWhen: asking whether a colour can be shown at all

name: Color harmonization
definition: Nudging an outside colour's hue toward the current scheme so a fixed brand or status colour sits inside a generated palette without looking imported.
useWhen: making a fixed outside colour belong to a generated scheme
notes: Tail gold: the answer to 'my warning orange clashes with the generated theme'.

name: Color harmony
definition: A rule for choosing colours by their positions on the wheel, such as complementary or analogous or triadic, so a palette holds together by construction.
useWhen: choosing a palette by a geometric rule rather than by eye

sources.title: The Ultimate Color Glossary For UI Designers

name: Color interpolation
definition: The rule for what happens between two colours in a gradient or transition, including which space the blend runs in and which way around the hue wheel it travels.
useWhen: controlling the path a blend takes between two colours
notes: Tail gold: names why blue to yellow goes through grey in sRGB but not in OKLCH.

name: color-mix()
definition: A CSS function that blends two colours by a chosen percentage in a chosen colour space, so hover and disabled variants are derived rather than hand-picked.
useWhen: deriving a variant from a colour instead of picking one

sources.title: CSS Color Module Level 5 vocabulary in css-color-4

name: Color picker
definition: A control for choosing a colour, usually pairing a saturation and lightness field with a hue slider, an alpha slider and a text field for a value.
useWhen: letting a person choose an arbitrary colour
notes: Cross-category: component, not color. Likely a duplicate of a record from the component sweep.

name: Color role
definition: A named job in the interface, such as surface or outline or on-primary, that components style themselves against instead of reaching for a palette value.
useWhen: the job a colour does, as the thing components reference
notes: Strong merge candidate with the existing semantic-color stub; role is the system's word, semantic colour is the community's.

name: Color scheme
definition: The declaration that a page or element supports light or dark rendering, which also tells the browser which palette to use for scrollbars and form controls.
useWhen: telling the browser which themes your page supports
notes: Demo is arguably document scope, since the visible effect includes the document scrollbar and UA form widgets.

name: Color space
definition: A coordinate system for describing colour, where the choice of axes decides whether arithmetic like mixing or stepping a ramp matches what the eye sees.
useWhen: naming the coordinate system a colour value is written in
notes: Colour space versus colour model is a live distinction worth the disambiguation prose.

name: Color stop
definition: A colour pinned at a position along a gradient, with an optional hint between two stops that moves the halfway point of the transition off centre.
useWhen: pinning a colour at a point along a gradient
notes: Interpolation hint is genuine tail vocabulary and could be split out.

name: Color temperature
definition: Whether a colour reads warm (toward red and orange) or cool (toward blue), the axis designers use to bias a neutral grey without changing its lightness.
useWhen: biasing a palette warm or cool

name: Color theme
definition: A complete named set of colour values a product can swap in whole, so light, dark, high contrast and per-tenant branding are the same mechanism.
useWhen: a whole palette swapped as one named set

name: Color token
definition: A named colour decision stored once and referenced everywhere, so retheming is a change to the value rather than an edit at every place it is used.
useWhen: a colour stored as a name so it can be repointed

name: Color vision deficiency
definition: Reduced ability to tell certain hues apart, most often red from green, which makes hue alone an unreliable way to carry meaning for roughly one man in twelve.
useWhen: checking a palette against reduced hue discrimination
notes: Cross-category: recorded as accessibility, surfaced by the colour sweep.

name: Color well
definition: The small filled square that shows the current colour and opens a colour picker when pressed.
useWhen: the little colour square that opens a picker
notes: AppKit's NSColorWell is where the name comes from. color.json already holds color-picker and swatch, so this record is only the trigger.

name: Color wheel
definition: A circular arrangement of hues that makes relationships between colours geometric, so a scheme becomes a shape drawn across the circle.
useWhen: picking colours by their angular relationship to each other

name: Column drop
definition: A responsive pattern where full height columns peel off one at a time and stack below as the viewport narrows, keeping source order.
useWhen: columns that stack one by one as space runs out

name: Column offset
definition: Pushing a column away from the grid's start so it begins on a later line, leaving deliberate empty tracks rather than an element to fill them.
useWhen: starting a column part way across the grid
notes: Push and pull are the older float era names for the same move, and they also reordered columns, which is why source order and visual order came apart.

name: Column resizer
definition: The invisible strip on a column border that widens or narrows the column when dragged, and often fits the column to its content on double click.
useWhen: dragging a column border to change its width
notes: A good demo for hit slop: the visible line is one pixel and the target is eight.

name: Commitment pattern
definition: The rare scanning shape where a motivated reader fixates on nearly every word, the only pattern that behaves like actual reading.
useWhen: the one case where readers read every word

sources.title: Text Scanning Patterns: Eyetracking Evidence, NN/g

notes: Useful as the counterexample: it is what designers assume happens and almost never does.

name: Common region
definition: The grouping principle that anything inside a shared boundary reads as one group, strong enough to beat how far apart the items actually are.
useWhen: when a container has to beat the spacing

sources.title: The Principle of Common Region: Containers Create Groupings, NN/g

notes: Pairs with proximity as a contrast set, and explains why cards work and why too many boxes stop working.

name: Comparison prevention
definition: Structuring plans or products so their features and prices cannot be lined up, forcing a decision that no side-by-side reading would support.
useWhen: the plans are built so you cannot compare them

name: Comparison table
definition: A table whose columns are options and whose rows are features, read across to decide between plans or products.
useWhen: deciding between options feature by feature
notes: The hard part is the mobile reading, where the columns have to become cards or the header has to stick sideways.

name: Complementary colors
definition: Two hues sitting opposite each other on the colour wheel, the pairing that produces the strongest contrast and the loudest accent.
useWhen: the loudest possible pairing of two hues
notes: Split-complementary is recorded here as an alias; canonicalize may promote it to its own entry.

name: Complication
definition: A slot on a watch face filled with one live figure from an app, sized to be read in the second a wrist is raised.
useWhen: one number has to survive being glanced at on a watch
notes: Borrowed from watchmaking, where a complication is any function beyond telling the time. watchOS 9 organises them into families (circular, inline and others) with recommended layouts.

name: Compositor-only animation
definition: An animation limited to properties the compositor can handle alone, usually transform and opacity, so it keeps running even when the main thread is busy.
useWhen: motion must stay smooth under load

sources.title: MDN: animation performance and frame rate

name: Compound grid
definition: Two or more grids of different column counts overlaid in one layout, so a page can carry several rhythms while still sharing one structure.
useWhen: one page needing two different column rhythms

sources.title: Five simple steps to designing grid systems, part 4, Mark Boulton
Mark Boulton on grids and responsive web design, Creative Bloq

notes: Swiss theory from the 1960s that desktop publishing made impractical and CSS grid made easy again. Good tail term with a strong demo.

name: Confetti burst
definition: A short particle celebration thrown across the screen to mark a completion, decorative by design and the first thing reduced motion should drop.
useWhen: a milestone deserves a moment of celebration

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

name: Confirmation page
definition: The screen that closes a transaction, stating plainly that it succeeded, giving a reference the reader can quote, and saying what happens next.
useWhen: the screen that says it worked and what happens next

name: Confirmshaming
definition: Wording the decline option so that choosing it is an admission of something embarrassing, making refusal feel like a confession rather than a choice.
useWhen: the no button is written to make you feel bad

aliases.name: no thanks, I hate saving money

name: Conformance level
definition: The A, AA, or AAA tier a success criterion sits in, and the tier a product claims, which is what people mean when they say a design is "AA".
useWhen: someone says the target is AA and you need the tiers

implementations.name: WCAG AA across all standard themes

name: Conic gradient
definition: A gradient whose colours sweep around a centre point like a clock hand rather than along a line, the shape behind pie charts, colour wheels and progress rings.
useWhen: colours sweeping around a centre instead of across a line

name: Consistent help
definition: Keeping the same help route, a contact link, a chat launcher, a self-help pane, in the same relative place on every page so a stuck reader can find it again.
useWhen: placing the help affordance so it never moves
notes: WCAG 2.2 addition (3.2.6). The demo can show two pages of one flow with the help control anchored versus wandering.

name: Consistent identification
definition: Calling the same function by the same name and icon everywhere in a product, so a reader who learned it once does not have to relearn it per screen.
useWhen: the same action has three names across screens

name: Constructivism
definition: A 1920s poster language of diagonal bars and blocks, red and black on off-white, photomontage, and heavy sans capitals set on a strong angle.
useWhen: diagonal red and black bars driving the composition

sources.title: daisyUI trends: UI design styles catalog
Inkbot Design: 20 iconic graphic design styles

notes: Reaches interfaces through hero sections and posters rather than controls; the diagonal is what separates it from De Stijl and Bauhaus.

name: Container
definition: A wrapper that caps how wide content can get and adds the side padding that keeps it off the viewport edges.
useWhen: the element that decides how wide the page can be
notes: Name collides with container-query's "container". Disambiguate: this is the width capping wrapper, that is the query containment root.

name: Container color
definition: A muted companion to an accent, light enough to fill a chip or a card behind ordinary text, so an accent can shade a region without shouting.
useWhen: a soft fill in the accent hue rather than the solid accent

name: Container query
definition: A rule that responds to the size of a component's own container rather than the viewport, so one component adapts anywhere it is placed.
useWhen: a component that must adapt to its slot, not the screen
notes: Style queries and scroll-state queries are the same at-rule extended; mention them as siblings rather than separate entries.

name: Container transform
definition: Material's transition in which a container grows or shrinks into another one, its contents crossfading inside, so a card visibly becomes the screen it opened.
useWhen: a small surface opens into the larger one it belongs to

sources.title: Building beautiful transitions with Material Motion for Android

notes: One of Material's four named transition patterns (container transform, shared axis, fade through, fade).

name: Containing block
definition: The box an element's percentages and offsets are measured against, which is not always its parent and changes with positioning.
useWhen: asking what 100% is actually 100% of

sources.title: CSS Flexible Box Layout Module Level 1

name: Content choreography
definition: Deciding how blocks of content reorder and regroup as a layout reflows, so hierarchy survives the collapse from several columns into one.
useWhen: deciding what order stacked blocks land in

sources.title: How To Maintain Hierarchy Through Content Choreography, Smashing Magazine

notes: Trent Walton, 2011. Names the failure round one already has the mechanics for: stacking columns destroys hierarchy unless someone chooses the new order.

name: Shelf
definition: A horizontally scrolling row of cards, one row per category, stacked down the page so each row is browsed sideways.
useWhen: many categories, each with too many items to stack
notes: Prime long tail term: people describe it ("the Netflix rows") long before they can name it. Every Layout's "Reel" is the closest thing to a canonical name.

name: Contextual alternates
definition: Substitute letterforms a font swaps in automatically based on the neighbouring characters, so joins and repeats look natural.
useWhen: a script font changes shape depending on its neighbours

sources.title: Syntax for OpenType features in CSS (Adobe Fonts)

name: Contrast ratio
definition: A number from 1:1 to 21:1 describing how far apart two colours sit in relative luminance, used to decide whether text on a background is readable.
useWhen: measuring whether two colours are far enough apart to read
notes: Head term. Cross-category with accessibility; kept in color because the demo is two swatches and a number.

name: Cookie consent banner
definition: A notice asking permission to store non-essential cookies before the reader has done anything, offering accept, reject, and a route to per-purpose choices.
useWhen: the consent notice that greets you before you read anything
notes: banner already exists on the site as the component. This is the flow, and it is where several deceptive design terms live in the wild.

name: Corporate Memphis
definition: The flat vector illustration style of bright, faceless people with long bendy limbs and small torsos that spread across tech marketing from 2017.
useWhen: flat faceless people with long bendy limbs

sources.title: Webflow: Blue people and long limbs: How one illustration style took over the corporate world

notes: Named after the Memphis Group but visually unrelated to it; Alegria (Facebook, 2017) is the origin point.

name: Count-up animation
definition: Animating a number toward its value instead of setting it, often with digits rolling like an odometer so the change is legible.
useWhen: a number changing should be noticed and read

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: Search intent is strong ('rolling number animation') and no system owns the name; verify implementations in a later pass.

name: Countdown timer
definition: A running clock attached to an offer or a held resource, showing how long remains and what will happen when it reaches zero.
useWhen: a clock ticking down beside an offer or a held seat

name: Counter
definition: The fully enclosed white space inside a letter such as o, b, or the upper bowl of an a.
useWhen: describing the hole inside a letterform

name: Cover
definition: A layout primitive that fills at least the viewport height, centring a principal element vertically with optional header and footer pinned above and below.
useWhen: a full height panel with something centred in it

name: Crossfade
definition: A transition in which one element fades out while the other fades in over the same span, so both are partly visible at the midpoint.
useWhen: swapping content of the same shape in place

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: Merge candidate with dissolve; kept apart because dissolve is the single-element case and crossfade is the two-element case.

name: Cubic bezier
definition: The four-control-point curve that describes how a value moves between its start and end, the default way CSS spells an easing.
useWhen: an easing has to be written down exactly
notes: Sub-entry to the existing easing term; the standard curve family names (sine, quad, cubic, quart, quint, expo, circ, back, elastic, bounce, each in, out, in-out) belong as aliases on easing.

name: Curb cut effect
definition: The pattern where something built for a disabled minority turns out to serve everyone, the way dropped kerbs serve prams and captions serve noisy rooms.
useWhen: justifying accessibility work to a sceptical room

aliases.name: solve for one extend to many

name: Current page indicator
definition: The marking of which item in a navigation set is the one you are on, exposed with aria-current so it survives without the colour cue.
useWhen: showing which nav item is the page you are on

name: currentColor
definition: A CSS keyword meaning the element's own text colour, letting borders, icons and fills inherit whatever colour the surrounding text happens to be.
useWhen: an icon or border that should follow the text colour
notes: Tail gold for icon systems: one keyword is why an SVG picks up a button's text colour.

name: Cursor follower
definition: A dot or ring that trails the pointer with a lag and often swells over links, replacing or augmenting the native cursor as a piece of brand motion.
useWhen: the pointer itself is part of the site's personality

sources.title: Webflow: a guide to custom cursors
HubSpot: how to use custom animated cursors

notes: An accessibility hazard as much as a vocabulary item: hiding the native cursor costs pointer visibility. The stage already draws its own ghost cursor, so a demo of this must not fight it.

name: Cursor pagination
definition: Paging that moves by a pointer into the result set rather than a page number, so newly inserted rows never shift what the next page contains.
useWhen: the list only offers next and previous, never page numbers
notes: Names the reason a feed shows only Next and Previous. Sits on the boundary between data access and UI vocabulary.

name: Cyberpunk UI
definition: A dystopian sci-fi interface style: near-black surfaces, one or two toxic neon accents, monospace all-caps labels, clipped corners, and scanline or glitch noise laid over the top.
useWhen: dark dystopian surfaces with toxic neon accents

sources.title: stellae.design: Cyberpunk UI, dark themes, neon accents and terminal aesthetics
daisyUI trends: Cyberpunk UI design style

notes: Reads as a bundle: it is mostly dark-mode plus neon-glow plus terminal-aesthetic plus scanlines, so canonicalize may prefer it as a collection page.

name: Damping
definition: The friction term in a spring that decides how quickly oscillation dies out, from a loose wobble to a critically damped move with no bounce at all.
useWhen: tuning how much wobble a spring is allowed

sources.title: Spring Animations in Pure CSS with linear()

notes: Merge candidate with spring-animation if the taxonomy prefers one entry for the whole spring model.

name: Dark mode
definition: A second palette built on dark surfaces with light foregrounds, derived from the light one by rebalancing lightness and saturation rather than by inverting it.
useWhen: the dark counterpart of a palette, not an inversion of it
notes: Head term. The interesting content is the rules that make a dark palette not an inversion: reduced saturation, no pure white text.

name: Dark pattern
definition: An interface arranged to make the reader do something they did not intend and would not have chosen, by exploiting how attention and defaults work.
useWhen: the interface is designed against the person using it

sources.title: Deceptive Design: Types of deceptive pattern

notes: Harry Brignull coined dark pattern in 2010 and now prefers deceptive pattern; the rename is the article. Parent term for the whole family below.

name: Dashboard grid
definition: A grid of tiles, each holding one metric, chart or list, that a reader can often resize and rearrange.
useWhen: many independent readouts on one screen

name: Data grid
definition: A spreadsheet-like table where individual cells take focus and can be edited, navigated cell by cell with the arrow keys.
useWhen: a table you move around cell by cell

implementations.name: Grid (Interactive Tabular Data and Layout Containers)

notes: Data table vs data grid is a real discrimination (row focus vs cell focus) that almost every product blurs. TanStack row needs a probe.

name: Date picker
definition: A field that opens a small calendar so a date can be chosen by looking at the month rather than typing it.
useWhen: choosing a date where the day of week matters
notes: GOV.UK deliberately ships three separate text boxes instead of a calendar, which is a real disagreement worth quoting.

name: Date range picker
definition: A calendar that takes a start and an end date in one pass, highlighting the span between them as you move.
useWhen: the answer is a span of days, not one day

name: De Stijl
definition: A style built only from black rules, rectangular fields, and the three primaries on white, arranged asymmetrically with no curves and no diagonals.
useWhen: black rules and primary rectangles, nothing else

sources.title: Creative Market: Design trend report, De Stijl design

notes: Often invoked as the ancestor of card and grid layout; useful on the site as the contrast case for a modular grid.

name: Dead zone
definition: A range of input near the resting position that is deliberately ignored, so tiny unintended movement produces no response at all.
useWhen: input near zero is ignored on purpose

sources.title: Apple Developer: Explore game input in visionOS

notes: Game and tool UI vocabulary that has quietly moved into touch UI as the word for ignored micro-movement.

name: Debounce
definition: Waiting until input has stopped for a set moment before reacting, so a burst of keystrokes or clicks produces one response instead of many.
useWhen: waiting for input to settle before responding

sources.title: NN/g: Timing guidelines for exposing hidden content

notes: Recorded as felt behaviour rather than as a coding utility; the demo should show the search field that waits.

name: Deck
definition: The short summary line set between a headline and the body, larger than body text and written to sell the article.
useWhen: the summary line under a headline

name: Deconstructed pancake
definition: A row of equal cards that wraps to fewer per line as space runs out, with the last line left aligned at its natural size rather than stretched to fill.
useWhen: a wrapping row whose last line should not stretch
notes: The named contrast to the RAM technique: flex basis with wrapping versus auto-fit tracks. Worth one demo showing both side by side.

name: Decorative image
definition: An image that carries no information and is given an empty alt attribute so assistive technology skips it entirely.
useWhen: the picture adds nothing a reader would miss

name: Deformable UI
definition: A style where controls behave like soft matter, squashing under a press and springing back past rest, so the surface reads as jelly, clay, or inflated plastic rather than paint.
useWhen: controls that squash and spring like soft material

sources.title: UI Style Guide: Tactile Digital / Deformable UI
Buzzvel: The human touch returns, design trends for 2026

notes: Half aesthetic and half motion: the look is claymorphism, the term is really about the spring response on press. Candidate for a motion cross-reference.

name: Delay
definition: The wait between an animation being triggered and starting to move, the unit stagger is built from and the reason a hover effect reads as either twitchy or considered.
useWhen: motion should start after something else, not with it
notes: The missing sibling of the existing site terms duration and easing. Canonicalize may prefer to fold it into duration rather than ship a third timing atom.

name: Density
definition: How much content a system packs into a given area, tuned as a named setting so the same components can run comfortable or compact.
useWhen: the same UI, tighter, for expert users

name: Density independent pixel
definition: A virtual unit of length that stays the same physical size across screen densities, so one number can describe a layout on every device.
useWhen: why sizes are written in dp, pt or CSS px

sources.title: Support different pixel densities, Android Developers

notes: One idea under four names: dp on Android, pt on Apple platforms, effective pixel on Windows, CSS pixel on the web. Android's sp is the text variant that follows the user's font size.

name: Descender
definition: The part of a letter such as g, j, p, or y that drops below the baseline.
useWhen: naming the strokes that hang below the baseline

name: Description list
definition: Paired labels and values laid out as a list of facts about one thing, rather than as a table of many things.
useWhen: labelled facts about a single record
notes: Six systems, six names, one thing: a strong candidate for the naming table this site is for.

name: Detent
definition: A position a control settles into and resists leaving, so a continuous drag or turn lands on discrete values that can be felt rather than read.
useWhen: the position a control sticks at as you drag past it
notes: Load-bearing in 13 places across 9 published articles (knob, bottom-sheet, grabber, rotate-gesture, spring-animation, haptic-feedback, tick-marks, modal-presentation, cassette-futurism) with no definition anywhere on site. ALIAS FENCE: do not claim 'notch', it belongs to display-cutout.

name: Device posture
definition: The physical fold state of a foldable device, such as flat, book or tabletop, which a layout can respond to alongside plain size.
useWhen: a layout that responds to how the device is folded

name: Did you mean
definition: Offering a corrected spelling for a query that returned little or nothing, either as a suggestion to accept or as a substitution the reader can undo.
useWhen: search offers a corrected spelling of your query
notes: The forgiving reading of it (auto-substitute plus a way back) is the interesting half.

name: Diegetic interface
definition: An interface that exists inside the fiction it serves, so the character can see and use it too, rather than being drawn on top of the world for the player alone.
useWhen: the readout belongs to the world, not the screen

sources.title: Types of UI in gaming: diegetic, non-diegetic, spatial and meta
Nasty Rodent: Diegetic vs non-diegetic UI, the four-type framework

notes: Cross-category: recorded as pattern, surfaced by an aesthetic sweep. From the 2009 Fagerholt and Lorentzon thesis, whose four types are fiction against geometry; the other three names are listed as aliases only because they come as a set.

name: Digital collage
definition: A composition assembled from cut-out photography, torn paper edges, scanned texture, and type set at odd angles, so the page reads as pasted up rather than laid out.
useWhen: imagery cut out and pasted rather than placed

sources.title: Linearity: Everything designers need to know about digital collage
Envato: Trend deep dive, collage art

notes: The torn edge and the visible scan texture are what sell it; without them it reads as ordinary image composition.

name: Dimensionality
definition: Giving interface objects a believable place in depth by folding, layering or flipping them, so a reader can tell where something went and where it will come back from.
useWhen: objects need somewhere to come from and return to

sources.title: UX Magazine: creating usability with motion, the UX in Motion Manifesto
The 12 principles of UX in motion

notes: Easy to confuse with the existing directionality entry: that one is about which way, this one is about how many dimensions the interface pretends to have.

name: Direct manipulation
definition: Acting on an object by handling the object itself, dragging, resizing, or typing into it, rather than describing the change in a separate control.
useWhen: you change the thing by grabbing the thing

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Direct Manipulation instead of contextless menus

notes: Ben Shneiderman's term from 1982; the history is worth a paragraph.

name: Directionality
definition: The rule that every movement carries a direction, and that using it consistently tells the reader how the parts of an interface relate.
useWhen: motion should say where a view sits relative to another

name: Disguised ad
definition: An advertisement styled to look like a control or an item of content, so the click it collects was aimed at something else entirely.
useWhen: the download button that is actually an advert

name: Display cutout
definition: The camera housing that intrudes into the screen rectangle, which a layout has to route content around rather than under.
useWhen: naming the hole the layout must dodge

sources.title: Using safe-area-inset to build mobile-safe layouts, Polypane

name: Dissolve
definition: A fade that carries the eye from one image or state to another without any movement, inherited from film editing vocabulary.
useWhen: the change should register without implying direction

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: Merge candidate with crossfade.

name: Dithering
definition: Adding fine noise to a gradient or image so the eye averages neighbouring pixels into the missing intermediate colours, hiding the bands.
useWhen: removing banding by adding fine noise

name: Diverging palette
definition: A data palette built from two sequential scales meeting at a neutral midpoint, used when values run above and below a meaningful zero.
useWhen: values that run above and below a midpoint

name: Dock
definition: A persistent strip of application icons anchored to a screen edge, holding launchers, running apps and pinned items in one row.
useWhen: the persistent row of app icons at a screen edge
notes: The magnification effect on hover is what most people picture, and it is a good demo. Cross platform naming: dock on macOS, taskbar on Windows, shelf on ChromeOS.

name: Dock magnification
definition: Scaling each item in a row by how close the pointer is to it, so the hovered item swells, its neighbours ramp down, and the row reads as bulging under the cursor.
useWhen: a dense row of icons needs a hovered target enlarged in place

sources.title: O'Reilly, jQuery 1.4 Animation: resizing elements and the fisheye menu

notes: New systemId buildui. A layout-shift trap by construction: the honest version reserves the row's full magnified height so the page below never moves (SPEC §5).

name: Dolly and zoom
definition: Borrowing the camera's vocabulary: dolly moves the viewer through the scene, zoom scales the scene itself, and the interface reads as travelling rather than rearranging.
useWhen: the reader should feel moved through the interface

sources.title: UX Magazine: creating usability with motion, the UX in Motion Manifesto
School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: The film loan that explains zoom-transition and ken-burns-effect; keep only if the taxonomy wants the camera metaphor named as such.

name: Dot grid background
definition: A faint repeating field of dots or ruled squares behind content, borrowed from graph paper and canvas tools to suggest an editable surface rather than a page.
useWhen: a faint grid or dot field behind the content
notes: Usually one repeating gradient or an SVG tile, masked with a radial fade so it does not compete with the text; the interactive versions light cells under the pointer.

name: Double click
definition: Two clicks inside a short interval on the same spot, treated as one gesture that opens, edits, or selects a word rather than activating twice.
useWhen: two clicks that mean something a single click does not
notes: Double-click to select a word and triple-click to select a paragraph belong here as aliases unless canonicalize splits them out.

name: Double tap
definition: Two taps in quick succession on the same spot, conventionally used to zoom in on content or to zoom back out when already zoomed.
useWhen: two quick taps that mean zoom, not activate

name: Drag and drop
definition: Picking up an object, moving it under continuous pointer or finger contact, and releasing it over a target that accepts it.
useWhen: moving an object onto a target by holding it the whole way

sources.title: MDN: HTML Drag and Drop API

name: Drag autoscroll
definition: Scrolling a container automatically when a drag is held near its edge, so an item can be moved somewhere currently off screen.
useWhen: a drag needs to reach past the visible area

name: Drag handle
definition: The small gripped area, often drawn as rows of dots or lines, that marks where an item may be picked up and dragged.
useWhen: the part of an item that says grab me here
notes: Cross-category: it is a component, but it is discovered through interaction searches. This is the literal what is the word for the little grip dots query.

name: Drag preview
definition: The semi-transparent copy of the dragged item that follows the pointer, sometimes collapsed into a stack when several items move at once.
useWhen: the ghost of the item that follows your cursor

name: Drag threshold
definition: The small distance a pointer must travel while pressed before the gesture counts as a drag, so a shaky click is not mistaken for one.
useWhen: deciding when a press turns into a drag

name: Drag to reorder
definition: Changing the order of a list by dragging an item to a new position, with the remaining items shifting to show where it will land.
useWhen: you rearrange a list by dragging its rows
notes: The keyboard equivalent (move up, move down, or grab and arrow) is the accessibility half of this term.

name: Dragging alternative
definition: A second, non-dragging route to anything a drag can do, such as arrow keys or a move-to menu on a sortable list.
useWhen: a drag is the only way to perform an action

name: Drill-down navigation
definition: Going deeper into a hierarchy one level at a time inside the same panel, each level replacing the last and offering a way back up.
useWhen: a hierarchy is too deep to show all at once
notes: The mobile settings pattern, and the one a narrow sidebar falls back to. The state question worth writing about is whether the panel you came from keeps its scroll and form state when you go back.

name: Drip pricing
definition: Advertising a low headline price and adding mandatory fees one screen at a time, so the true total only appears once the buyer is committed.
useWhen: fees keep appearing as you move through checkout

name: Drop cap
definition: An oversized opening letter set into the first lines of a paragraph, marking where the reading starts.
useWhen: marking where an article begins

sources.title: How to Use Drop Caps effectively

name: Drop indicator
definition: The line or highlighted gap drawn during a drag to show exactly where the item will land if it is released now.
useWhen: the line that shows where the dragged item will land
notes: Strong long-tail candidate: people search for the name of the blue line.

name: Drop zone
definition: The region that will accept a dragged item, usually highlighted while a compatible drag is in flight so the destination is unmistakable.
useWhen: the area that says a drag can land here

sources.title: MDN: HTML Drag and Drop API

name: Duotone
definition: An image rendered in two colours instead of full colour, mapping its shadows to one hue and its highlights to another so photography joins the brand palette.
useWhen: forcing photography into two brand colours

name: Dwell activation
definition: Committing an action by keeping a pointer or gaze still on a target for a set time, for input methods that have no click of their own.
useWhen: holding still is the only way to click

sources.title: NN/g: Timing guidelines for exposing hidden content

notes: Cross-category candidate with accessibility: it is a primary input method for people who cannot click.

name: Dynamic Type
definition: A platform feature that scales interface text to a size the reader chose in system settings, with layouts expected to reflow around it.
useWhen: the reader, not the designer, picks the text size
notes: Cross-category: equally an accessibility term. Recorded as typography since the subject is type sizing.

name: E-ink aesthetic
definition: A paper-like style built for or borrowed from electronic ink: near-white ground, pure black text, hairline rules, no shadows or gradients, and paged navigation instead of smooth scrolling.
useWhen: an interface styled like reflective ink on paper

sources.title: Intent: How to design for e-ink devices
CHI 2026: A Dedicated E-Paper Design System for Mobile Phones

notes: On real e-paper the constraints are physical (slow refresh, ghosting, no backlight); as a style on ordinary screens it keeps only the look.

name: Earcon
definition: A brief synthesized sound standing for an event, abstract by design, so a rising figure means success only because the interface taught you it does.
useWhen: the abstract tone that reports an event
notes: The term was coined by D.A. Sumikawa in 1985 (a deliberate pun: icon reads as eye-con, so the ear gets one too) and structured families of tones were formalized by Blattner, Sumikawa and Greenberg in 1989. VERIFY these attributions against the source before asserting them. Round-mate contrast pair with auditory-icon: abstract and learned versus recorded and resembling.

name: Edge swipe
definition: A swipe that begins off the screen edge and travels inward, reserved by the system for navigation such as going back or revealing a drawer.
useWhen: a gesture that starts at the bezel, not on a control
notes: Relates to drawer, which already exists on the site; edge swipe is the gesture, drawer is the surface.

name: Edge to edge
definition: Drawing an app behind the system bars so content reaches the physical screen edges, with insets applied only to what must stay tappable.
useWhen: content under the bars, controls kept clear of them
notes: Cross platform naming clash: Android says edge-to-edge, Apple says full screen with safe area insets, the web says viewport-fit=cover.

name: Editorial web design
definition: A style that borrows print magazine craft for the screen: a visible column grid, display type at poster scale, pull quotes, rules, and captioned images set into the text.
useWhen: a page styled like a magazine spread rather than a template

sources.title: Wix: The biggest web design trends of 2026

notes: Overlaps the layout record magazine-layout, which owns the grid mechanics; this entry is the visual style. Merge candidate at canonicalize.

name: 8 point grid
definition: A spacing convention where every size and gap is a multiple of eight, so values stay whole numbers at every common screen density.
useWhen: picking a base unit for a whole system

name: Elevation overlay
definition: The older dark theme technique of laying white over a surface at an opacity that rises with elevation, because shadows are nearly invisible on dark backgrounds.
useWhen: raising a dark surface where a shadow would not show
notes: Superseded by surface tint in Material 3; the entry should say so, since both words are still in circulation.

name: Em dash
definition: The longest common dash, about the width of the letter m, used to set off an abrupt break or aside in a sentence.
useWhen: naming the longest dash on the keyboard
notes: Awkward but necessary: the site bans the character in its own prose (SPEC 2.4) while still owing readers the definition. Author with care.

name: Em
definition: A relative unit equal to the current font size, historically the width of the square the letter m was cast on.
useWhen: sizing something relative to the text it sits in
notes: rem is close enough that it may deserve its own entry during canonicalize.

name: Emergency exit button
definition: A control that leaves the current page immediately for an unrelated site and tries to clear it from history, for readers who may be watched.
useWhen: leaving a page fast and without a trace
notes: Triggered by pressing Shift three times as well as by the button. Rare, specific and genuinely important, which is the best kind of tail entry.

name: Emoji picker
definition: A searchable grid of emoji organised by category, with recent choices remembered and skin tone chosen once.
useWhen: choosing an emoji from a searchable grid

name: Emoji presentation
definition: Whether a character that can be either a symbol or an emoji renders as flat text or as a color emoji, selected by a variation selector or by CSS.
useWhen: a symbol turns into an emoji you did not want

name: Emphasis level
definition: A hierarchy expressed by lowering the opacity of one foreground colour rather than by choosing different colours, giving high, medium and disabled text one source.
useWhen: ranking text by opacity instead of by separate colours
notes: Material 3 moved to explicit on-surface-variant roles instead; the entry should note the opacity approach can quietly fail contrast.

name: En dash
definition: A dash about the width of the letter n, used for ranges of numbers and for connections between two things.
useWhen: writing a range of numbers or dates

name: Endowed progress
definition: Starting a progress meter part filled, so the reader feels they are continuing something already begun rather than starting from nothing.
useWhen: the progress bar starts at 20 percent before you did anything

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Upfront Progress instead of starting with a blank

name: Entrance animation
definition: The motion an element plays as it arrives, running from a starting style that only exists before the element was ever rendered.
useWhen: something new appears and should not just pop in
notes: Could be merged with exit-animation into one 'enter and exit' entry, but the two have different hard problems and different APIs.

name: Error identification
definition: Naming the field that failed and saying what went wrong in text, rather than only outlining the input in red.
useWhen: telling a reader which field failed and why

name: Error summary
definition: A block at the top of a failed form listing every problem as links that move focus to the field that caused it.
useWhen: one list at the top links to each broken field

sources.title: GOV.UK Design System: Recover from validation errors
