notes: Could land in accessibility instead; the focus-management behaviour is the whole point of it.

name: Escape gesture
definition: The screen reader equivalent of the Escape key, a two finger scrub that dismisses a sheet or steps back a level and that a custom overlay has to answer for itself.
useWhen: a custom sheet ignores the platform dismiss gesture

sources.title: Apple: Supporting Accessibility (View Controller Programming Guide)

name: Exit animation
definition: The motion an element plays on its way out, which requires deferring its removal from the layout until the animation has finished.
useWhen: something is being removed and should not blink out

name: Expandable row
definition: A table row that opens to reveal a detail panel beneath it, keeping the row in place instead of navigating away.
useWhen: row detail that opens in place under the row

name: Expanded state
definition: The open or closed state of a disclosure, exposed with aria-expanded on the control that owns it rather than on the panel it reveals.
useWhen: the trigger must say whether its panel is open

name: Explore by touch
definition: The touch screen reader mode where dragging a finger reads whatever is under it and activation takes a second, deliberate tap, so nothing fires by accident.
useWhen: designing touch targets a finger has to find blind

sources.title: Android Accessibility Help: Navigate your device with TalkBack

name: Express checkout
definition: A row of one-tap payment buttons placed above the normal form, which fetch address and payment details from a wallet the buyer already has.
useWhen: the wallet buttons above the checkout form

name: Eyebrow
definition: A short line of text above a heading that says what category or series the content belongs to.
useWhen: labelling what kind of thing a heading is
notes: Material's older overline style is the closest design-system equivalent; kept as an alias.

name: Eyedropper
definition: A tool that turns the cursor into a sampler so a colour can be picked from anywhere on screen, usually with a magnified preview of the pixel under it.
useWhen: sampling a colour from pixels rather than typing a value
notes: Cross-category: recorded as component, surfaced by the colour sweep. Merge with the component file's color-picker entry if one exists.

name: F pattern
definition: The scanning shape eye tracking finds on text heavy pages: two horizontal sweeps across the top, then a vertical run down the left edge.
useWhen: predicting how a text heavy page gets skimmed
notes: Fact check the article against the original NN/g 2006 eye tracking study, not the many blog restatements.

name: Faceted filter
definition: A panel of grouped checkboxes and ranges that narrows a result set, each option usually showing how many results it would leave.
useWhen: narrowing results by category with counts
notes: The count beside each option is the part that makes it faceted rather than just a list of checkboxes.

name: Faceted search
definition: Narrowing results by ticking values from several independent attribute groups, with counts showing how many results each value would leave.
useWhen: filters grouped by attribute, each showing result counts

sources.title: A List Apart: Design Patterns: Faceted Navigation

name: Fade
definition: A change in opacity used to bring an element in or take it out, the cheapest transition and the one that implies no spatial relationship.
useWhen: an element appears or leaves without moving

name: Fade through
definition: Material's transition for unrelated views: the outgoing view fades out completely before the incoming one fades in while scaling up slightly.
useWhen: two views have no spatial or hierarchical relationship
notes: Contrasts precisely with crossfade, where the two views overlap in opacity; the discrimination is the point of the entry.

name: Fake scarcity
definition: Claiming limited supply that is not real, with stock counts or demand messages generated to pressure a decision rather than report a fact.
useWhen: only three left, and the number is invented

name: Fake social proof
definition: Manufacturing evidence that other people approve, through invented reviews, testimonials, or live activity messages nobody actually generated.
useWhen: someone in Leeds just bought this, and nobody did

name: Fake urgency
definition: Presenting a deadline that does not exist, usually a timer that resets on reload, so the reader hurries a decision they had time to make.
useWhen: the countdown resets when you refresh the page

name: Fallback font
definition: The typeface actually used when the preferred one is missing or has not loaded, either for the whole run of text or for characters it lacks.
useWhen: naming what shows up when the real font does not

sources.title: Framework tools for font fallbacks (Chrome for Developers)
Creating Perfect Font Fallbacks in CSS

name: False bottom
definition: A page that looks finished at a point where content actually continues, so the reader stops scrolling and never sees the rest.
useWhen: the page looks like it ended but has not

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Suggesting Continuity instead of false bottoms

notes: Excellent long-tail entry: readers know the problem and not the word.

name: Faux bold
definition: A bold or italic the browser fakes by smearing or shearing the regular weight, because the real style was never loaded.
useWhen: your bold looks wrong and blurry

name: Feature gate
definition: Showing a locked feature in place, with its real position in the interface, so the reader sees what upgrading would unlock rather than a hidden absence.
useWhen: a locked feature stays visible with an upgrade badge

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Exposing Options instead of hiding them

name: Feature spotlight
definition: A one-time announcement pointing at something newly added, shown in place next to the feature and dismissed for good once acknowledged.
useWhen: the one-time New badge pointing at a change

name: Feed layout
definition: A scrolling column or adaptive grid of equivalent items built for browsing, where no item outranks another by position alone.
useWhen: endless peers you skim rather than navigate

name: Feedforward
definition: What an interface says about the result of an act before it is taken, the half of the loop that sits ahead of the action rather than after it.
useWhen: telling someone what will happen before they act

sources.title: But how, Donald, tell us how? (DIS 2002)
Crossing the bridge over Norman's gulf of execution (CHI 2013)

notes: Djajadiningrat, Overbeeke and Wensveen (DIS 2002); Vermeulen et al. (CHI 2013). The neighbourhood is DENSE: affordance appears in 47 term files and signifier in 9, so the article must earn its place by discriminating hard. Affordance is what you CAN do, signifier is where and how you do it, feedforward is what WILL HAPPEN if you do. Verify the second source URL resolves before shipping it.

name: Fictional user interface
definition: The screen graphics style invented for film, television, and games: dense readouts, targeting reticles, wireframe globes, and animated telemetry that look computational without computing anything.
useWhen: interface art made to be watched rather than used

sources.title: Reel Deal Film School: Creating Fantasy User Interfaces (FUIs)
Kit FUI: user interfaces from movies, TV and video games

notes: The F is expanded as fictional, fantasy, futuristic, film, or fake depending on who is writing; fictional is the least contested. HUD is the in-world subset.

name: Fieldset
definition: A group of related form controls sharing one question, with a legend that acts as the label for the whole group.
useWhen: several controls answering one question
notes: The legend is the part that matters and the part everyone omits, which is the article.

name: Figure
definition: An image, table or code block bound to its caption so the two travel together and can be referred to from the running text.
useWhen: a visual needs a caption that belongs to it

name: File attachment
definition: A row or card standing in for a file, showing its type, name and size, with the one action that file supports: download, open or remove.
useWhen: a file has to be represented rather than uploaded
notes: Deliberately split from file-upload: that term is the drop target, this one is the representation of a file that already exists.

name: File upload
definition: A control that takes files, by opening the system picker from a button or by accepting a drop into a marked area.
useWhen: the form takes files rather than text
notes: interaction.json already holds drop-zone as the target region; this record is the whole control.

name: Fill mode
definition: Whether an animation's first or last keyframe styles apply outside its running window, which decides if an element snaps back when it finishes or stays where it landed.
useWhen: an animation ends and the element must not jump back
notes: Round one flagged it as felt behaviour rather than syntax: the word names what a reader sees when an animation ends and the element snaps back to where it started.

name: Filmstrip
definition: A scrollable row of thumbnails beside a larger view, where picking one changes what the large view shows.
useWhen: a thumbnail rail that drives a big preview

name: First-line indent
definition: Indenting the opening line of a paragraph so the start of each paragraph is visible without a blank line between them.
useWhen: marking new paragraphs without adding space

name: First rule of ARIA
definition: The maxim that no ARIA is better than bad ARIA: if a native element does the job, use it rather than pinning a role onto a div and reimplementing the behaviour.
useWhen: someone proposes a role instead of an element

aliases.name: no ARIA is better than bad ARIA

sources.title: W3C: Using ARIA, rules of ARIA use
Primer: The first rule of ARIA

name: First run experience
definition: Everything shown only on the very first open, from a welcome sequence to seeded sample content, and never shown to that person again.
useWhen: what happens only the very first time you open it
notes: FRE and FTUE are widely used inside product teams and almost never written down, which makes this a strong dictionary entry.

name: Fisheye view
definition: A focus plus context display that magnifies whatever has attention and progressively compresses everything further away, like a lens dragged along a list.
useWhen: magnifying one item without hiding the rest

sources.title: A Review of Overview+Detail, Zooming, and Focus+Context Interfaces, Cockburn, Karlson and Bederson

notes: The motion sweep already has dock magnification, which is one instance of this. Keep fisheye-view as the general display technique and let canonicalize decide the parent.

name: Fitts's law
definition: The rule that the time to hit a target grows with its distance and shrinks with its size, which is why screen edges and corners are so easy to reach.
useWhen: arguing about how big or how near a control should be

sources.title: Smashing Magazine: Accessible target sizes cheatsheet

name: Flash of inaccurate color theme
definition: The moment a page paints in the wrong theme before the stored preference is applied, showing a light flash to a reader who chose dark.
useWhen: the wrong theme showing for a frame on page load

sources.title: Avoiding Flash of Inaccurate Theme Color

notes: Tail gold with a real community acronym. Demo is document scope (first paint of a whole document), hence iframe.

name: Flashing content
definition: Content that flashes more than three times per second in a large enough area, restricted because it can trigger seizures.
useWhen: judging whether a flash rate is dangerous

aliases.name: general flash and red flash thresholds

sources.title: WCAG 2.2: Three Flashes or Below Threshold

notes: demo: none on purpose. Building a specimen that flashes would be the harm the term names.

name: Flat design
definition: A style that strips away depth cues, using solid fills, sharp edges, and bold color instead of shadow, gradient, bevel, or texture.
useWhen: no depth cues at all, only color and shape

sources.title: NN/g: Flat Design: Its Origins, Its Problems, and Why Flat 2.0 Is Better for Users
CareerFoundry: Flat Design: A Complete Beginner's Guide

notes: Datable: emerged around 2011, mainstreamed by Windows Metro and iOS 7.

name: Flat 2.0
definition: Flat design with the depth cues put back in small doses: soft shadow, subtle gradient, and hover feedback that show what can actually be clicked.
useWhen: flat surfaces, but affordance restored with light shadow

sources.title: NN/g: Flat Design: Its Origins, Its Problems, and Why Flat 2.0 Is Better for Users
UXPin: The 7-Minute Guide to Flat Design 2.0

notes: NN/g owns this coinage; 99designs and others say semi-flat for the same thing. Merge candidate with flat-design if the taxonomy prefers one entry with a history section.

name: Fling
definition: The fastest of the drag family: contact is released while still moving, so the content keeps travelling and the action cannot be dragged back.
useWhen: a throw that releases mid-motion and cannot be taken back

sources.title: Material Design: Gestures (drag, swipe, or fling)

notes: Material distinguishes drag, swipe and fling purely by velocity and whether contact is kept; Apple's word for the same thing is flick.

name: FLIP
definition: A technique that measures an element's first and last positions, inverts the difference with a transform, then plays it off, so layout changes animate on the compositor.
useWhen: a layout change must animate without animating layout properties

sources.title: Josh Comeau: the FLIP technique for list animations

notes: Merge candidate with layout-animation: FLIP is the mechanism, layout animation is the feature name libraries ship it under.

name: Float animation
definition: A slow continuous up and down drift on an idle element so a static composition keeps breathing without asking for attention.
useWhen: a hero illustration should not look frozen
notes: Ambient motion: nothing triggers it and nothing ends it, which is exactly what reduced motion should switch off.

name: Fluid grid
definition: A grid whose columns and gutters are expressed as proportions rather than fixed pixels, so the whole composition stretches and shrinks with its container.
useWhen: columns measured in proportions, not pixels

sources.title: Responsive Web Design, A List Apart

notes: Historically the counterpart of the fixed width layout. Worth saying that fr units and minmax made the arithmetic disappear.

name: Fluid space scale
definition: A spacing ramp whose every step interpolates between a minimum and a maximum viewport, so gaps grow smoothly with the screen instead of jumping at breakpoints.
useWhen: spacing that scales with the screen, not in steps
notes: The spacing counterpart of fluid-typography, which the typography sweep already has. Utopia's T-shirt names and one-up pairs are the vocabulary in use.

name: Fluid typography
definition: Type sizes that scale continuously with the viewport between a minimum and a maximum, rather than jumping at breakpoints.
useWhen: sizing text across screens without breakpoints

sources.title: Creating a Fluid Type Scale (Modern CSS)

name: Focal point
definition: The one element a composition is built around, given enough size, contrast or isolation that the eye lands there before anywhere else.
useWhen: naming the thing the eye should hit first

sources.title: Design Principles: Compositional, Symmetrical And Asymmetrical Balance, Smashing Magazine

notes: The demo writes itself: one layout with two competing focal points, one with a single clear one.

name: Focus appearance
definition: The size and contrast a focus indicator must reach to count as visible: enough area around the control, enough change against both the control and its background.
useWhen: judging whether a focus ring is strong enough

name: Focus delegation
definition: A shadow root option that forwards focus from the host into the first focusable element inside it, so clicking the padding of a custom element does not leave focus nowhere.
useWhen: a custom element swallows clicks near its edges

sources.title: Frontend Masters: Shadow DOM focus delegation

notes: Directly relevant to this project: every specimen in shadow mode is a host whose focus behaviour this decides.

name: Focus follows mouse
definition: A focus model in which whatever the pointer is over receives keyboard input, without any click to claim it first.
useWhen: keyboard input goes where the pointer is pointing

sources.title: LWN: Focus follows mouse or click to focus?

notes: Click to focus is the opposite model and is recorded here as an alias; canonicalize may prefer it as a contrasting stub.

name: Focus management
definition: Deliberately moving keyboard focus after a state change so the reader lands on the new content instead of at the top of the document.
useWhen: deciding where focus goes when the UI changes
notes: Merge candidate with the existing focus-trap entry; focus management is the umbrella, focus trap is one case.

name: Focus not obscured
definition: The requirement that a focused control is not completely hidden by sticky headers, footers, cookie bars, or chat widgets when it receives focus.
useWhen: the sticky header swallows the focused control

sources.title: W3C F110: sticky footer or header hiding focused elements

name: Focus order
definition: The sequence keyboard focus follows through a page, which should match reading order instead of source quirks or positive tabindex values.
useWhen: the path Tab takes through a whole page
notes: iframe: the subject is the document's own focus order, which a shadow root cannot honestly stage.

name: Focus plus context
definition: A layout that keeps one region in full detail inside its own surroundings, shrinking or dimming the context instead of moving it into a second pane.
useWhen: detail and its surroundings in one view

sources.title: A Review of Overview+Detail, Zooming, and Focus+Context Interfaces, Cockburn, Karlson and Bederson

notes: Useful because it names what expanding a row in place does, as against opening a detail pane.

name: Focus ring
definition: The visible outline drawn around the element that currently holds keyboard focus, showing where the next keypress will land.
useWhen: marking where keyboard focus is sitting right now
notes: Head term. The stage already draws annotation rings, so the demo must not confuse its own ring with the specimen's.

name: Focus visible
definition: A focus style shown only when focus arrived by keyboard or another non-pointer route, so a mouse click does not leave a ring behind.
useWhen: showing the ring to keyboard users but not to clickers

name: Focusable disabled
definition: A control styled as unavailable but left in the tab order with aria-disabled, so a reader can find it and learn why it is off.
useWhen: a disabled control still needs to be discoverable
notes: Tail gold: the trade-off between the native disabled attribute and aria-disabled has no popular name.

name: Focusable scroll region
definition: Giving a scrollable box its own tab stop so a keyboard user can scroll it, which matters whenever the content inside holds no focusable element of its own.
useWhen: a code block or log pane scrolls but cannot be reached

sources.title: Deque: Scrollable region must have keyboard access

name: FOFT
definition: A loading strategy that shows the roman weight as soon as it arrives and lets the remaining styles swap in afterwards, so the swap happens in stages.
useWhen: staging a font swap instead of taking it all at once

name: FOIT
definition: The blank period when a browser hides text entirely rather than show it in a fallback face while the web font loads.
useWhen: the text is missing, not just wrong, on load

sources.title: Ensure text remains visible during webfont load (Lighthouse)

name: Follow-through
definition: Parts of a composition that keep moving briefly after the main element stops, and start slightly after it starts, so a group does not move as one rigid block.
useWhen: a group should move like connected parts, not one slab

sources.title: IxDF: UI Animation, applying Disney's 12 principles to UI

notes: Close to stagger (already on the site) but distinct: stagger offsets identical animations, follow-through is one motion dragging its dependents.

name: Hinting
definition: Instructions inside a font that nudge its outlines onto the pixel grid at small sizes so stems stay crisp and even.
useWhen: explaining why type looks fuzzy at small sizes

name: Font metric override
definition: Reshaping a fallback font's size and vertical metrics in CSS so it occupies the same space as the web font and the swap shifts nothing.
useWhen: killing the layout jump when a web font lands

sources.title: Framework tools for font fallbacks (Chrome for Developers)
Creating Perfect Font Fallbacks in CSS

notes: Sits between typography and performance; the layout-shift angle may pull it toward a future performance cluster.

name: Font pairing
definition: Choosing two or more typefaces that work together, usually one expressive and one neutral, with enough contrast to read as a deliberate choice.
useWhen: deciding which two typefaces to run together

sources.title: Three secrets to font pairing (Adobe Design)

name: Font smoothing
definition: How a device softens the edges of letterforms, either by shading whole pixels grey or by lighting a pixel's coloured subpixels separately.
useWhen: your type looks heavier on one platform than another

sources.title: What's the deal with WebKit Font Smoothing?

name: Font stack
definition: The ordered list of typefaces a rule names, each tried in turn until one is available, ending in a generic family.
useWhen: listing which fonts to try and in what order

sources.title: Creating Perfect Font Fallbacks in CSS

name: Font subsetting
definition: Shipping only the characters a page actually needs, cutting the font file down and letting the browser fetch ranges on demand.
useWhen: cutting a font file down to what the page uses

name: Font weight
definition: How thick a typeface's strokes are, named in steps from thin to black and numbered from 100 to 900 on the web.
useWhen: naming how heavy the strokes are

name: Force touch
definition: A press whose depth is part of the input, letting a harder press mean something different from a light one on a pressure sensing surface.
useWhen: press depth carries meaning, not just contact
notes: Largely retired on current hardware, but still the word people reach for; keep as a historical tail entry.

name: Forced colors mode
definition: An operating system mode that replaces a page's palette with a small user-chosen set of system colours, overriding almost everything an author specified.
useWhen: the OS is imposing its own palette on your interface

sources.title: Styling for Windows high contrast with forced colors

notes: Cross-category with accessibility; kept in color because the subject is the palette substitution itself.

name: Forced continuity
definition: Turning a free trial into a paid subscription automatically, with the card taken up front and no reminder before the first real charge.
useWhen: a free trial quietly becomes a paid plan

name: Forgiving format
definition: Accepting whatever shape the reader types and normalising it afterwards, instead of rejecting input that differs only in spacing or punctuation.
useWhen: the field takes the card number however you type it

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Forgiving Inputs instead of being strict with data

name: Form
definition: A grouping of controls a reader fills in and submits together, carrying the labels, validation and submit affordance for the whole set.
useWhen: a set of inputs is submitted as one unit
notes: Head term above the whole input family. Has to earn its keep against the more specific field terms, so lean on submit semantics, grouping and the validation contract rather than on styling.

name: FOUT
definition: The visible swap when a page first paints text in a fallback face and then re-renders it once the web font arrives.
useWhen: the text visibly changes font on load

name: Frame rate
definition: How many frames a second the interface actually draws, the budget every animation spends: 60fps leaves about 16ms per frame and a 120Hz display halves it.
useWhen: motion has to be judged in milliseconds per frame

sources.title: MDN: animation performance and frame rate

notes: Jank already records the symptom; this records the unit. Merge candidate if the taxonomy wants one performance word.

name: Friend spam
definition: Asking for access to a contact list under one pretext and using it to send invitations that appear to come from the reader.
useWhen: the app mails your contacts as if you had
notes: One of Brignull's original twelve. The honest version (invite friends) and the deceptive version share a shape, which is the article.

name: Frozen column
definition: A table column held against the edge while the rest scrolls sideways, so the row's identifying value stays readable.
useWhen: a wide table where you lose track of the row

sources.title: Data Grid column pinning, MUI X

notes: Four names for one feature (pinned, sticky, frozen, locked) makes it a strong alias magnet for search.

name: Frutiger Aero
definition: The mid 2000s look of glossy gradients, bubbles, water, bright skies, and clean humanist type, retroactively named after the typeface and Windows Aero.
useWhen: glossy optimistic 2000s tech imagery
notes: Term coined retroactively by Sofi Lee in 2017, popular from 2022. Covers roughly 2004 to 2013, ended by flat design and iOS 7.

name: Frutiger Metro
definition: The flat vector cousin of Frutiger Aero: gradient color blocks, bloom and glow, silhouetted figures, swooshes and abstract flourishes, without the glossy water and grass.
useWhen: gradient vector blocks with bloom and swooshes
notes: Vectordelia is the wiki name and Frutiger Metro the popular one; both cover the mid 2000s to early 2010s vector poster look, not Microsoft Metro.

name: Full bleed
definition: An element that breaks past the content column to span the whole viewport width while its neighbours stay constrained.
useWhen: one band that runs edge to edge inside a narrow page

sources.title: CSS Grid full-bleed layout tutorial, Josh W. Comeau

notes: Borrowed from print, where a full bleed image runs off the trimmed edge of the paper. Say so.

name: Functional need
definition: A statement of the gap between what a person can do and what a design demands, used by the WCAG 3 draft in place of sorting people into disability categories.
useWhen: framing a barrier without naming a diagnosis
notes: WCAG 3 draft vocabulary, still moving. Worth a record because audits already use the phrase.

name: Gamut mapping
definition: Converting a colour that falls outside a display's range into the nearest one inside it, usually by lowering chroma in OKLCH rather than clipping each channel.
useWhen: bringing an impossible colour into a display's range
notes: Tail gold: clipping darkens a bright colour, mapping does not, and that difference is visible in a demo.

name: Gauge
definition: A dial style readout showing one value on an arc between a minimum and a maximum, borrowed from instrument panels.
useWhen: a value read off an arc like a dial
notes: SwiftUI ships Gauge as a first class control, which is the strongest claim on the name.

name: Generative UI
definition: An interface whose parts are chosen or composed by a model at runtime, so a request is answered with a built form, chart, or panel instead of a paragraph of text.
useWhen: the model assembles the screen, not just the words

sources.title: CopilotKit: Generative UI, understanding agent-powered interfaces
Builder.io: Designing generative UI in an agent-native world

notes: Cross-category: recorded as pattern, surfaced by an aesthetic sweep. Generative UI is the settled engineering name; AI-native UI is the trend-article name for the same thing.

name: Ghost click
definition: A stray click the browser emits after a touch has already been handled, landing on whatever moved under the finger in the meantime.
useWhen: one touch produces a second, unwanted activation

sources.title: FastClick: polyfill to remove click delays
Chrome for Developers: 300ms tap delay, gone away

name: Glitch aesthetic
definition: A look that fakes signal failure with color channel offset, torn scan bands, and jitter, used for emphasis or as a whole visual identity.
useWhen: deliberate corruption used as decoration
notes: Chromatic aberration is listed as an alias rather than its own record; split it out at canonicalize if the demo differs.

name: Global navigation
definition: The links to the top tier of a site's structure, present on every page and unchanged wherever the reader currently is.
useWhen: the nav that is the same on every page

sources.title: The Difference Between Information Architecture and Navigation, NN/g

notes: Page anatomy vocabulary: the trio global, local and utility navigation is how IA people name the regions a layout has to provide.

name: Gloss
definition: A wet plastic finish made from a light gradient across the top half of a control, a highlight arc, and a darker lower half.
useWhen: the control looks like polished wet plastic

sources.title: GirlieMac: CSS3 Gradients: No Image Aqua Button

name: Glyph
definition: A single drawn shape in a font, which may be one character, a variant of one, or several characters fused together.
useWhen: talking about drawn shapes rather than characters

name: Goal gradient
definition: Effort rising as a visible goal gets closer, which is why interfaces show how little is left rather than how much has been done.
useWhen: the interface shows how close you are, not how far you came
notes: A psychology principle rather than a UI shape; kept because its interface expression (a nearly full meter) is demoable.

name: Golden ratio
definition: The proportion of roughly 1 to 1.618 used to divide a layout, so its parts relate to each other by a rule instead of by arbitrary numbers.
useWhen: picking proportions that are not arbitrary

sources.title: A designer's guide to the Golden Ratio, Creative Bloq

notes: Round one has rule-of-thirds but not its parent. The honest article says the maths is often applied after the fact, and shows the 38/62 split it implies.

name: Gooey effect
definition: Blurring a group of shapes and then crushing the blur back to a hard edge so overlapping elements merge into one liquid silhouette as they move apart and together.
useWhen: two moving shapes should read as one substance

sources.title: Animation Patterns: SVG metaball gooey filter with feColorMatrix

notes: The alpha-contrast half of the filter is unsupported in Safari and Firefox, so the fallback is a plain blur. Good candidate for a specimen that shows the filter chain in two steps.

name: Grade
definition: A variable font axis that thickens or thins strokes without changing any character's width, so text can get darker without reflowing.
useWhen: darkening text on a dark background without reflow

name: Gradient
definition: A fill that transitions between two or more colours across a shape, defined by colour stops and by the space the transition is interpolated in.
useWhen: a fill that changes colour across its own area

name: Gradient border
definition: An outline filled with a gradient rather than a single color, usually built from a conic or linear gradient behind a masked shape so the hue travels around the edge.
useWhen: an outline whose color changes along its length

sources.title: web.dev: Use conic gradients to create a cool border
Bram.us: Animating a CSS Gradient Border
Bejamas: Finding the best way to create animated gradient borders in CSS

notes: border-image with a gradient works but cannot be animated directly; the rotating version needs a registered @property angle or a pseudo-element.

name: Gradual engagement
definition: Replacing a sign-up form at the front door with a first useful action, so the reader experiences value before being asked for anything.
useWhen: the first screen does something instead of asking you to register

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Gradual Engagement instead of a hasty sign up

name: Grainy gradient
definition: A gradient with a fine noise layer over it, added to hide banding and give a flat background the texture of printed paper or film.
useWhen: a smooth background deliberately roughened with noise

sources.title: ibelick: Creating grainy backgrounds with CSS

notes: Merge candidate: a separate noise-texture entry would overlap almost entirely, so aliases carry it here.

name: Grid lanes
definition: The native masonry mechanism in CSS grid, where one axis keeps strict tracks and the other lets items stack into whichever lane has room.
useWhen: masonry without a library, straight from grid
notes: Masonry is already a site term; this is the mechanism and the newer name for it. The naming argument itself, item-flow versus grid-lanes, is part of the story worth telling.

name: Group label
definition: The one name that covers a set of controls, a question above its radio buttons or a heading above an address block, so each field is heard in context.
useWhen: individual field labels make no sense on their own
notes: Overlaps the component-category fieldset record: this one is about the name, that one about the box.

name: Grunge design
definition: A 1990s style of torn and photocopied texture, overlapped and cut type, off-grid layout, and dirty muted color, where legibility is traded for emotional pitch.
useWhen: distressed texture and type deliberately off-grid

sources.title: Sessions College: The grunge typography of David Carson
Mew Design Docs: Grunge graphic design, the raw distressed art of the 90s

notes: David Carson at Ray Gun is the reference; the digital revival keeps the texture and the cut type but usually restores a readable body copy.

name: Guest checkout
definition: Letting a buyer complete a purchase without creating an account, with the offer to save details moved to after the order is placed.
useWhen: buying without being made to create an account

name: Gutenberg diagram
definition: A model splitting evenly weighted pages into four quadrants, with the eye falling from the primary area at top left to the terminal area at bottom right.
useWhen: placing the last thing you want read
notes: Long tail gold: designers know the F and Z patterns and almost never know this one, which is the older parent of both.

name: Gutter
definition: The space between columns or tracks in a grid, distinct from the outer margin that separates the grid from the container edge.
useWhen: the space between columns, not around them
notes: In print, gutter also means the binding margin between facing pages and alley means the space between columns; the web collapsed the two. Worth the disambiguation paragraph.

name: Half-leading
definition: The empty space a browser splits evenly above and below a line of text when line height exceeds the font's own height, which is why text boxes never sit flush.
useWhen: explaining the mystery padding around a line of text

sources.title: Leading-Trim: The Future of Digital Typesetting

name: Halftone
definition: Rendering tone as a grid of dots that vary in size, borrowed from print and used to give flat interface art a comic or newsprint feel.
useWhen: tone made of print dots that grow and shrink
notes: Frequently confused with dithering; the discrimination is varying dot size versus interleaved fixed pixels.

name: Hand-drawn UI
definition: A style whose lines wobble as if sketched by hand, used to signal that a diagram or wireframe is provisional rather than finished.
useWhen: the sketchiness says this is not final yet
notes: Rough.js is the underlying renderer for both; add it as a system id at canonicalize.

name: Hanging indent
definition: A paragraph whose first line starts further left than the rest, so the following lines are indented under it.
useWhen: setting bibliographies, definitions, or list labels

name: Hanging punctuation
definition: Letting quotes, hyphens, and other light marks sit outside the text column so the edge of the text reads as straight to the eye.
useWhen: a quote mark makes the left edge look dented

sources.title: Hung Punctuation and Optical Margin Alignment (CreativePro)

notes: Merge candidate: optical margin alignment is InDesign's name for the same effect and should stay an alias, not a term.

name: Haptic feedback
definition: A brief physical vibration or tap produced by the device to confirm an interaction, mark a boundary, or signal success and failure.
useWhen: feedback the user feels rather than sees or hears

name: Has popup
definition: A hint on a trigger that says something will open and what kind of thing it will be, a menu, a listbox, a dialog, before the reader commits to pressing it.
useWhen: a button opens a menu and gives no warning

name: HCT
definition: Material's colour space of hue, chroma and tone, which borrows hue and chroma from CAM16 and lightness from CIELAB so tone alone predicts contrast.
useWhen: generating a Material palette where tone predicts contrast

sources.title: Material 3: how the color system works

notes: Tail gold: the reason Material can promise a contrast ratio from a tone number alone.

name: Heading
definition: A short line of type that names the section under it and, by its size and weight, says how far down the outline that section sits.
useWhen: naming a section and showing its depth at once
notes: Round one caught heading-hierarchy (the outline rule) and typographic-hierarchy (the scale) but not the thing itself. The article should hold the two apart: level is semantic, size is a choice, and they are allowed to disagree.

name: Heading hierarchy
definition: The nested outline formed by heading levels, navigated directly by assistive technology and broken by skipping a level or picking a level for its size.
useWhen: structuring a page so it can be skimmed by heading

name: Height animation
definition: Animating a container between collapsed and its content's natural size, long impossible because height auto did not interpolate and now opened up by interpolate-size and calc-size().
useWhen: a section must grow to fit content without a magic pixel value

sources.title: Chrome for Developers: animate to height: auto

notes: The motion half of the existing accordion site term; canonicalize should decide which of the two owns the collapse animation.

name: Help drawer
definition: Documentation opened beside the task rather than over it, keeping the form usable while the explanation is read and staying open across steps.
useWhen: help opens beside the form instead of on top of it

name: Hero
definition: The large opening block of a page carrying a headline, a supporting line, imagery, and the main call to action.
useWhen: the big opening block that sets the pitch
notes: "Jumbotron" was Bootstrap's name and was dropped in Bootstrap 5; record it as a historical alias.

name: Hex color
definition: A colour written as a hash followed by three, four, six or eight hexadecimal digits, the notation most handoffs still speak even when the source is OKLCH.
useWhen: the notation a colour is handed over in
notes: The 8-digit form (hex with alpha) is the part people actually search for.

name: Hidden but focusable
definition: An element hidden from assistive technology that is still in the tab sequence, so keyboard focus lands on something a screen reader refuses to describe.
useWhen: focus disappears into an offscreen or hidden panel

sources.title: W3C ACT: Element with aria-hidden has no content in sequential focus navigation
Deque: aria-hidden elements do not contain focusable elements

name: Hit slop
definition: Invisible padding that extends a control's activatable area beyond its drawn bounds, so a small icon can stay small and still be easy to hit.
useWhen: the tappable area is bigger than the visible control

sources.title: Smashing Magazine: Accessible target sizes cheatsheet

name: Hit testing
definition: Working out which element sits under a pointer, which decides who receives the event when shapes overlap or transparent areas are in the way.
useWhen: asking which element a click actually lands on

name: Hold to confirm
definition: Requiring a press to be held for a moment before a destructive action commits, with progress shown so the wait is understood as deliberate.
useWhen: a dangerous action guarded by a held press
notes: Contrast pair with the existing alert-dialog entry: both guard a destructive action, one with a dialog, one with time.

name: Holographic foil
definition: A finish that shifts hue with viewing angle, imitating foil, soap film, or a CD surface with banded rainbow gradients over a pale metallic ground.
useWhen: a surface whose color shifts as if it were foil

sources.title: Envato Tuts+: 100+ best holographic and iridescent textures
Effect Labs: CSS holographic effect, iridescent and chrome

notes: The convincing version needs the hue to respond to something, pointer position or scroll, since a static rainbow gradient reads as a gradient rather than as foil.

name: Holy grail layout
definition: A three column page with header and footer where the centre column is fluid, the two side columns are fixed, and all three appear equal height.
useWhen: the classic fixed, fluid, fixed three column page
notes: The name is historical: it was hard before flexbox and grid. Worth saying so in the article.

name: Home indicator
definition: The thin bar at the bottom of a gesture driven phone screen, reserved space that app content must not sit beneath.
useWhen: the reserved strip at the bottom of a modern phone

name: Honeypot field
definition: A form field hidden from people but visible to automated form fillers, used to reject submissions that fill it in without challenging anyone.
useWhen: the invisible field that only a bot would fill in
notes: Cross-cuts accessibility: a naive display:none honeypot is invisible to screen readers too, which is why the correct technique matters.

name: Hover
definition: A pointer resting over an element without pressing, a state that exists for mice and pens but has no true equivalent on touch.
useWhen: the pointer is over something but has not committed

name: Hover intent
definition: Waiting out a short delay or watching cursor direction before acting on a hover, so a pointer merely passing through does not open anything.
useWhen: telling a deliberate hover from one passing through

sources.title: Baymard: Provide a hover delay of 300 to 500 ms
NN/g: Timing guidelines for exposing hidden content
CSS-Tricks: Dropdown menus with more forgiving mouse movement paths

notes: Tail gold: the safe triangle and the diagonal problem are separate enough that canonicalize may want them as aliases here or as their own entries.

name: Hover lift
definition: A card or button that rises a few pixels and deepens its shadow while the pointer is over it, so the whole surface reads as lifted toward the reader.
useWhen: a whole surface should answer the pointer, not just its border

sources.title: Subframe: CSS card hover effect examples

notes: Round two: named in round one's residue list. Transform plus shadow only, never margin or top, so the row it sits in does not move (SPEC §5).

name: Hoverable, dismissible, persistent
definition: The three conditions content revealed on hover or focus must meet: reachable with the pointer, dismissible without moving focus, and not self-closing.
useWhen: judging whether a tooltip or flyout behaves

sources.title: WCAG 2.2: Content on Hover or Focus

notes: Tail gold: the trio is always cited together and has no single popular headword.

name: Hub and spoke
definition: A navigation shape where every task is reached from one home screen and returns to it, with no way to move sideways between tasks.
useWhen: every section is reached from home and returns there
notes: Cross-category: could be filed as layout. The original iOS home screen is the canonical example.

name: HUD panel
definition: A small dark translucent floating window of controls that hovers over content without taking it over, common in media and creative tools.
useWhen: a small dark floating palette over content

name: Hue
definition: The attribute that gives a colour its name, red or teal or violet, expressed as an angle around a colour wheel independent of how light or vivid it is.
useWhen: naming the colour itself, apart from its lightness or intensity

name: Hue shift
definition: Rotating hue deliberately along a ramp, warmer at the light end and cooler at the dark end, so a scale looks alive instead of like one colour fading out.
useWhen: steering hue across a ramp instead of holding it fixed

sources.title: Rampensau: palette generation with hue cycling

notes: Tail gold: names the trick behind ramps that look designed rather than generated.

name: Hyperreal 3D
definition: Rendered objects pushed past photographic realism, with physically based materials, sharp specular detail, and studio lighting, floated over an otherwise plain interface.
useWhen: a rendered hero object that outdoes a photograph

sources.title: wings.design: 3D and depth in UI, function versus aesthetic

notes: Opposite pole from low-poly on the same axis; usually delivered as a pre-rendered image or a WebGL scene rather than as CSS.

name: Hyphenation
definition: Breaking a word across two lines at a syllable boundary so lines fill more evenly, marked with a hyphen at the break.
useWhen: keeping narrow columns from tearing open

name: Hyphenation ladder
definition: Three or more consecutive lines ending in a hyphen, which builds a visible staircase down the right edge of a column.
useWhen: naming a stack of hyphens down a column edge

name: Icon
definition: A small graphic symbol standing for an action, object or idea, read at a glance and rarely safe to ship without a label.
useWhen: a symbol has to carry meaning in very little space
notes: The most implemented entry in The Component Gallery (45 examples) and still missing from round one. Distinct from icon-button, which is the control, and icon-font, which is the delivery mechanism.

name: Icon font
definition: A font whose glyphs are icons rather than letters, addressed by code point or by a ligature so an icon can be styled like text.
useWhen: icons delivered as type instead of as images

sources.title: SVG, Icon Fonts, and Accessibility (24 Accessibility)

notes: Could equally be filed as component; the mechanism is a font, so typography.

name: Icon morph
definition: An icon that animates between two meanings rather than cutting, such as a hamburger whose bars rotate into a close cross.
useWhen: one control carries two states and should show the change

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: Strong long-tail search intent ('hamburger to X animation'); relates to the existing hamburger-menu entry.

name: Image
definition: An embedded picture, sized and cropped by the layout around it, carrying the alternative text that stands in when it cannot be seen.
useWhen: a picture is content rather than decoration

name: Image comparison slider
definition: Two images stacked with a draggable divider that wipes between them, used to show a before and an after in one frame.
useWhen: showing before and after in one frame
notes: Almost no design system ships it and almost every product marketing page has one, which is exactly the gap this site fills.

name: Image well
definition: An editable image view that shows its current picture and accepts a replacement dragged or pasted straight into it.
useWhen: a picture is both the display and the drop target
notes: The macOS name for the profile picture control every web app builds and never names. Copy, paste and delete are expected to work on it.

name: Images of text
definition: Text baked into a raster image, which cannot be resized, restyled, selected, translated, or read by anything but the alt attribute someone remembered to write.
useWhen: arguing a headline should be text, not a picture of text

name: Imposter
definition: A layout primitive that positions one element centred over its container, overlapping whatever is beneath rather than taking a place in the flow.
useWhen: one element floated dead centre over the rest

name: Inert
definition: A state that removes a subtree from focus order, hit testing, and the accessibility tree at once, used to seal the background behind a dialog.
useWhen: making a whole region unreachable, not just invisible
notes: Clean contrast with the existing aria-hidden and focus-trap entries: inert does all three jobs at once.

name: Infinite canvas
definition: A workspace with no page edges, where content is placed anywhere in an unbounded plane and the viewport pans and zooms over it instead of scrolling a document.
useWhen: a board with no page, only a viewport over it
notes: The layout model behind Figma, Miro, tldraw and node editors. Round one has minimap and pan and zoom in other sweeps but never named the surface itself.

name: Infinite scroll
definition: A list that appends the next page of results automatically as the reader approaches the bottom, so the content never ends and no page controls appear.
useWhen: the feed loads more by itself as you near the bottom

sources.title: NN/g: Infinite Scrolling: When to Use It, When to Avoid It

notes: The accessibility complaint (unreachable footer) is the false-bottom term, kept separate.

name: Initial focus
definition: Where focus lands when a view, dialog, or page first appears, chosen deliberately rather than left on the body or dumped on the first close button.
useWhen: a dialog opens and nobody decided where focus goes

name: Ink trap
definition: A notch cut out of a letter's inside corners so spreading ink or blurring pixels do not fill the joint solid.
useWhen: naming the cut-out notches in a display typeface

name: Inline autocomplete
definition: Completing the reader's text inside the field itself, with the guessed remainder selected so the next keystroke replaces it.
useWhen: the field finishes your word inside the field

implementations.name: Editable Combobox With Both List and Inline Autocomplete

notes: Ghost text now also names the AI completion suggestion in editors; a naming collision worth an article.

name: Inline edit
definition: Text that reads as plain content until you click it, at which point it becomes an input in the same place with save and cancel.
useWhen: editing a value where it is displayed
notes: The layout shift problem is the interesting constraint: the input must occupy exactly the space the text did.

name: Input group
definition: A field welded to text, a button or a select at one or both ends, so the addon reads as part of the same control rather than as a neighbour.
useWhen: a unit, prefix or action belongs inside the field
notes: The interesting part for an article is the seam: focus ring, border collapse and hit area all have to treat the group as a single control.

name: Input mask
definition: A field that imposes a fixed shape as you type, inserting the slashes, spaces or brackets a phone number or card number needs.
useWhen: the field types its own punctuation for you
notes: Widely disliked by accessibility practitioners because it fights paste and assistive input; that argument is the article.

name: Input purpose
definition: Machine readable autocomplete tokens on personal fields, which let browsers autofill and let personalisation tools add familiar icons or wording.
useWhen: telling the browser what a field is actually for

name: Inspector
definition: A pane, usually on the trailing edge, that shows and edits the properties of whatever is currently selected.
useWhen: a panel whose contents follow the selection

name: Interaction color step
definition: The convention that hover, active and selected are the next steps along the same scale rather than separate colours, so states are derived from one ramp.
useWhen: hover and pressed derived from a scale, not picked
notes: Tail gold: the reason a ramp has twelve steps rather than nine. Contrasts with state-layer, which does the same job with opacity.

name: Interactive transition
definition: A transition whose progress is held by an ongoing gesture, so the reader can drag it partway, hesitate, and either complete it or send it back.
useWhen: a gesture should own the transition until it is released
notes: Cross-category with interaction; kept here because the term names how the transition is driven.

name: Interpolation
definition: The rule that produces the intermediate values between two endpoints, which is why some properties can animate smoothly and others can only switch.
useWhen: explaining why a property will or will not animate
notes: The discrete case is exactly what transition-behavior: allow-discrete exists to work around.

name: Interruptible animation
definition: Motion that can be caught, reversed, or redirected mid-flight from its current value, instead of finishing before it will accept a new input.
useWhen: a reader may act again before the motion finishes
notes: The strongest practical argument for springs over fixed durations, so it pairs with spring-animation.

name: Interstitial
definition: A full screen placed between two steps of a flow, carrying a message, an advert, or a warning that the reader must pass through to continue.
useWhen: a whole screen sits between you and where you were going

name: Intrinsic web design
definition: Building layouts from what the content needs, using grid, flexbox and intrinsic sizing together, instead of imposing a fixed column skeleton.
useWhen: naming the era after responsive web design
notes: Coined by Jen Simmons in 2018. Good tail term with a clear attributable origin.

name: Invalid state
definition: The programmatic mark that a field's value failed validation, paired with a pointer to the message that explains it.
useWhen: the field itself must report that it is wrong

name: Inverse color
definition: A surface and text pair flipped against the current theme, so a snackbar or tooltip reads as a foreign object that arrived from outside the page.
useWhen: an element deliberately styled opposite to the theme

implementations.name: Inverse surface, Inverse on surface, Inverse primary

name: Inverted colors
definition: A whole-screen colour inversion applied by the OS, which flips a design nobody tested upside down and turns every shadow into a highlight.
useWhen: the OS inverts your palette and shadows go wrong

name: Isometric illustration
definition: Art drawn on a fixed axonometric grid so depth reads without perspective, with parallel edges and no vanishing point.
useWhen: depth without perspective, on a fixed 30 degree grid

name: Italic
definition: A companion style with letterforms redrawn on a cursive model, not merely slanted, used for emphasis and titles.
useWhen: emphasis inside running text

name: Jank
definition: Visible stutter in motion caused by frames arriving late or not at all, so an animation that should be continuous reads as juddering.
useWhen: naming why smooth-looking motion feels wrong

sources.title: MDN: animation performance and frame rate
web.dev: jank busting for better rendering performance

name: Jiggle mode
definition: An editing state announced by making every rearrangeable item wobble in place, so the whole screen says it can be reordered.
useWhen: an editing mode should be announced by motion alone

sources.title: How-To Geek: what is jiggle mode on iPhone

notes: Pure long tail: Apple has no official name, the community word is the entry. Good candidate for the 'what is the word for' framing.

name: Juiciness
definition: Stacking far more feedback on an act than it needs, so one small input wobbles, pops and sings, and the interface feels alive under the hand.
useWhen: deliberately excessive feedback for one small act

sources.title: Game Developer: Is your game 'juicy' enough?

notes: From game development: the 'Juice it or Lose it' talk by Martin Jonasson and Petri Purho, and the phrase 'maximum output for minimum input'. Game vocabulary is already in scope on site (attract-mode, jiggle-mode, ten-foot-ui, diegetic-interface, fictional-user-interface). HONESTY DUTY: this is the word for what 'add some microinteractions' actually asks for, and the article must say plainly where juiciness is WRONG, namely an act performed forty times a day, and link prefers-reduced-motion.

name: Justified gallery
definition: A photo grid that scales and trims images so every row lands on one shared height with flush left and right edges, unlike masonry's ragged columns.
useWhen: photos of mixed shapes in tidy flush rows
notes: The contrast partner for masonry, which is already a site term: masonry keeps widths and varies heights, a justified gallery keeps heights and varies widths.

name: Justified text
definition: Text set so both edges of the column are flush, achieved by stretching or squeezing the spaces between words on each line.
useWhen: you want both edges of a column flush

name: Kanban board
definition: A row of vertical columns, each one a stage, holding cards that move sideways as work progresses.
useWhen: items that belong to exactly one stage at a time
notes: A swimlane is strictly the horizontal band across a board, not the vertical column; the two get swapped constantly and that confusion is worth the entry.

name: Kawaii UI
definition: A cute style of pastel fills, rounded everything, oversized eyes and blush marks, sticker and mascot characters, and hand-lettered or bubbly rounded type.
useWhen: cuteness carried by mascots, pastels, and round shapes

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions

notes: Japanese in origin and still the default register for consumer apps there; mascots do real work, standing in for empty states and errors.

name: Ken Burns effect
definition: A slow pan and zoom across a still image that gives it motion, named after the documentary filmmaker who made the technique famous.
useWhen: a static image needs life without becoming video

name: Key repeat
definition: A held key firing repeatedly after an initial delay, which is how arrow keys scroll and backspace deletes more than one character.
useWhen: holding a key keeps producing the action

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

name: Key sequence
definition: A shortcut typed as an ordered run of presses, where the first key opens a mode and the next chooses within it.
useWhen: shortcuts typed in order, like a prefix then a letter

name: Keyboard shortcut
definition: A key or key combination that runs a command directly, giving practised users a path that skips the menus and the pointer entirely.
useWhen: a command reachable by keys instead of controls

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

name: Keyboard shortcuts dialog
definition: The panel opened by pressing question mark that lists every shortcut in the application, grouped by area.
useWhen: the cheat sheet of every shortcut
notes: Gmail, GitHub, Linear and Slack all ship one behind the same question mark key, which is a strong convention with no agreed name.

name: Keyboard trap
definition: A place keyboard focus can enter but not leave by keyboard alone, stranding anyone who is not using a pointer.
useWhen: focus goes in and cannot be tabbed back out

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

notes: Merge risk with the existing focus-trap entry: focus trap is deliberate and correct in a dialog, keyboard trap is the accidental failure. The two should contrast, not merge.

name: Keyframe
definition: A point in an animation where a value is pinned, with the frames between generated by interpolating from one pinned point to the next.
useWhen: an animation needs waypoints, not just a start and end

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

name: Keyline
definition: An invisible line that content across a whole screen aligns to, such as the edge line every row starts at and the deeper line where text begins after an icon.
useWhen: the shared line every row's text starts on
notes: Material 1 vocabulary that outlived its spec: 16dp at the screen edge, 72dp where list text starts after an avatar. The word designers reach for when a list looks ragged.

name: Kinetic typography
definition: Type animated over time, where letters and words move, scale, stagger, or morph so the setting carries tone and emphasis that a static line cannot.
useWhen: the type itself performs rather than sits still

sources.title: SVGator: What is kinetic typography, a guide to text in motion
Linearity: Kinetic typography, the what, why and how
Kinetic Typography UX: principles, patterns, and getting started

notes: Cross-category: recorded as typography, surfaced by an aesthetic sweep, and defensible as motion too. Word or letter splitting plus stagger is the usual mechanism, so it also touches the stagger term.

name: Knob
definition: A round control turned by dragging in an arc, borrowed from hardware and mostly found in audio and creative tools.
useWhen: a dial you turn rather than a track you slide

name: Label association
definition: The programmatic link between a label and its field, made by for and id or by wrapping, which makes the label clickable and the field named.
useWhen: connecting the words to the input they name
notes: SPEC section 8 warns that a choreography cannot rely on a label's native activation, which makes this a careful demo.

name: Label in name
definition: The rule that a control's accessible name must contain its visible label text, so speaking the visible words works in voice control.
useWhen: aria-label and the visible text disagree

name: Landmark
definition: A named region role (banner, navigation, main, complementary, contentinfo, search) that lets assistive technology jump between the major parts of a page.
useWhen: naming the big regions so they can be jumped between

name: Language attribute
definition: The declared language of a document or a passage inside it, which picks the voice, the pronunciation rules, and the hyphenation a reader gets.
useWhen: a quoted passage is in another language than the page
notes: iframe: the page language lives on the root element of a document.

name: Large text threshold
definition: The size at which text counts as large for contrast purposes (about 18pt, or 14pt when bold) and its required ratio drops from 4.5:1 to 3:1.
useWhen: deciding which contrast number a heading owes
notes: Cross-category with typography.

name: Lasso selection
definition: Selecting by drawing a freehand outline around items, so the boundary can follow an irregular shape instead of a rectangle.
useWhen: selecting an irregular region by drawing around it

name: Lawn mower pattern
definition: A scanning shape for tables where the eye runs across one row, drops down and runs back the other way, mowing the cells in alternating directions.
useWhen: laying out a comparison table for scanning

sources.title: The Lawn Mower Eyetracking Pattern for Scanning Comparison Tables, NN/g

notes: Observed most on comparison tables and zigzag layouts. Pairs with zigzag-layout, which is the layout that provokes it.

name: Layer cake pattern
definition: A scanning shape where the eye reads headings and subheadings and skips the text between them, so the fixation map looks like stacked layers.
useWhen: predicting a skim that only reads headings

sources.title: Text Scanning Patterns: Eyetracking Evidence, NN/g
F-Shaped Pattern of Reading on the Web, NN/g

notes: One of NN/g's named scanning patterns. Round one took F, Z and Gutenberg only; this and its four siblings are the rest of the set, and the layout argument for good subheadings.

name: Layout grid
definition: The shared column, gutter and margin structure a team lays every screen against, so different people's pages line up with each other.
useWhen: the agreed skeleton every screen is built on

sources.title: Layout grid, U.S. Web Design System

name: Layout margins
definition: The reserved space between a container's edge and its content, sized by the system so content never touches the edge of the screen.
useWhen: the outer breathing room, set once by the system

name: Layout shift
definition: Content moving after it has already been painted, usually because something arriving late took space that was never reserved for it.
useWhen: the page jumped and you lost your place
notes: Directly echoes SPEC section 5's no incidental layout shift rule, so the site is already opinionated about it.

name: Layout shifter
definition: A responsive pattern where the arrangement genuinely differs per breakpoint rather than reflowing, so each size gets its own composition.
useWhen: sizes get different layouts, not the same one reflowed
notes: Easy to confuse with layout-shift (the CLS metric), which is unrelated. Worth an explicit contrast.

name: Layout thrashing
definition: Reading a geometric value after writing to the DOM in the same frame, forcing the browser to lay out synchronously over and over and stalling the animation that caused it.
useWhen: an animation stutters and the cause is the code, not the curve

sources.title: web.dev: avoid large, complex layouts and layout thrashing
Paul Irish: what forces layout / reflow

notes: Distinct from layout-shift: nothing moves that should not, the frames simply never arrive on time.

name: Lazy loading
definition: Deferring the fetch of an image, list section, or module until it is about to be needed, usually when it approaches the viewport.
useWhen: content is fetched only once it is nearly on screen

name: Lazy registration
definition: Letting someone use a product and accumulate state anonymously, and asking for an account only when that state needs to survive the session.
useWhen: you can start using it before making an account

name: Leaderboard
definition: A ranked list of participants by some score, with the reader's own position pinned into view even when it falls outside the visible range.
useWhen: a ranked table with your own row pinned into view

name: Legibility
definition: How easily one letter can be told apart from another, a property of the typeface's drawing rather than of how the text is set.
useWhen: judging the typeface, not the setting

name: Letterboxing
definition: Filling the mismatch between content shape and screen shape with bars: above and below for letterbox, at the sides for pillarbox.
useWhen: the bars that appear when ratios do not match
notes: Also the name for what a mobile OS does to an app that refuses to resize on a foldable or tablet, which is the modern UI sense.

name: Letterpress text
definition: A text effect that fakes stamping into the surface, using a one pixel light shadow below the glyphs and a slightly darker fill above it.
useWhen: type that looks pressed into the surface
notes: Cross-category candidate with typography; kept here because it is a finish, not a type decision.

name: Ligature
definition: A single glyph that replaces two or more letters whose shapes would otherwise collide, such as the f and i pair.
useWhen: two letters collide and the font fuses them
notes: Discretionary ligatures folded in as an alias rather than split out; revisit if the demo wants to show both.

name: light-dark()
definition: A CSS function that takes two colours and returns the one matching the page's current colour scheme, collapsing a theme's light and dark values into one declaration.
useWhen: writing both theme values inline instead of in a media query

name: Light dismiss
definition: Closing a transient surface by clicking outside it or pressing Escape, without a dedicated close control being used.
useWhen: clicking away is enough to close something
notes: The native popover attribute names this behaviour directly (auto versus manual); verify the MDN popover page before authoring.

name: Lightbox
definition: An overlay that shows one image or video large over a dimmed page, with next and previous controls and a dismiss.
useWhen: an image opened large over the dimmed page
notes: The name comes from a 2005 JavaScript library and stuck; almost no design system uses it, which is itself the story.

name: Lightness
definition: How light or dark a colour reads, from black at one end to white at the other, held separately from its hue and its colourfulness.
useWhen: stepping a colour lighter or darker without changing the hue
notes: Brightness, value, lightness and tone are four vocabularies for nearby ideas; disambiguation prose is the point of this entry.

name: Line clamp
definition: Cutting a block of text off after a fixed number of lines, with an ellipsis at the end of the last one.
useWhen: capping a card's description at three lines

name: Line drawing animation
definition: An SVG stroke that appears to draw itself by animating its dash offset along its own length, used for signatures, check marks and illustrated line art.
useWhen: a mark should look drawn rather than revealed

sources.title: CSS-Tricks: how SVG line animation works

notes: The dash trick is the whole term: stroke-dasharray as long as the path, then animate stroke-dashoffset to zero.

name: Line focus
definition: A reading aid that dims everything except one to five lines of text, so the eye has a single band to track and cannot skip or reread a line by accident.
useWhen: long prose has to be readable line by line

sources.title: Microsoft Support: Use Immersive Reader in Microsoft Edge

name: linear() easing
definition: An easing written as a list of sampled stops rather than a curve, which lets CSS express springs and bounces that no cubic bezier can describe.
useWhen: a curve is not expressible as one bezier

sources.title: Chrome for Developers: create complex animation curves with linear()
Smashing Magazine: the path to awesome CSS easing with linear()

name: Lining figures
definition: Numerals all drawn to cap height so they line up evenly with capitals and with each other.
useWhen: numbers next to capitals or in interface chrome

sources.title: OpenType at Work: Figure Styles (Type Network)

name: Link purpose
definition: Whether a link's own text says where it goes, the reason a list of read more and click here links fails when read out of context.
useWhen: judging link text pulled out of its sentence

name: Liquid Glass
definition: Apple's 2025 material where controls float as a translucent layer that refracts what is behind them and reshapes fluidly as content moves underneath.
useWhen: controls are a glass layer that bends the content behind
notes: Announced 9 June 2025 across iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe, tvOS 26, visionOS 26, watchOS 26. The HIG page fetch returned only a title (JS rendered), so the URL resolves but its wording was not read this sweep.

name: List detail
definition: A browsable list paired with a pane showing the selected item in full, collapsing to one screen at a time when the window is narrow.
useWhen: browse a list, read one item, keep both in view
notes: "Master detail" is the older name and still the most searched; it is being retired for the same reasons master/slave was.

name: List virtualization
definition: Rendering only the rows currently in view and a small buffer around them, while spacers preserve the scrollbar of the full list.
useWhen: a huge list renders only the rows you can see
notes: Breaks find-in-page and anchor links, which is the usual reason a reader goes looking for the word.

name: Listbox
definition: An always visible list of options you choose from with the keyboard or pointer, without a popup or a text field.
useWhen: the options are on screen already, not behind a popup
notes: The role name most people meet only through error messages, which makes it a good dictionary entry.

name: Live activity
definition: A persistent, updating view of something in progress, shown in system places like a lock screen so a reader can follow it without opening the app.
useWhen: a task in progress must be followed outside the app
notes: Defined against the push notification: not one interruption but a few hours of state, and interactive. The food delivery tracker is the canonical example.

name: Live region
definition: A container marked so assistive technology reads changes inside it without moving focus, used for messages that appear after an action.
useWhen: something must be spoken without stealing focus
notes: Absorbs the search query 'screen reader announcement', which is a head phrase but not a separate concept.

name: Load more
definition: A button at the end of a list that fetches and appends the next batch only when pressed, keeping the reader in control of how much arrives.
useWhen: the next batch waits behind a button instead of arriving on its own

sources.title: NN/g: Alternatives to Pagination on Product-Listing Pages

name: Local navigation
definition: Links contextual to where the reader is, showing the siblings and children of the current page rather than the whole site.
useWhen: nav that changes with the section you are in

sources.title: Local Navigation Is a Valuable Orientation and Wayfinding Aid, NN/g

notes: Usually the thing in the sidebar. Distinguish from a table of contents, which is within one page.

name: Logical properties
definition: Layout properties named by flow direction (inline start, block end) rather than by screen edge, so a layout mirrors itself in other writing modes.
useWhen: spacing that must flip for right to left text

name: Logo cloud
definition: A row or grid of customer logos used as social proof, usually flattened to one colour so no brand dominates.
useWhen: proof by association, laid out as a strip of marks

name: Long description
definition: An extended text alternative for a chart, diagram, or map, linked or referenced because a short alt string cannot carry the content.
useWhen: the image is data and one line will not do

name: Long press
definition: A press held in place for a moment before release, used to reveal secondary actions, enter a rearrange mode, or open a contextual menu.
useWhen: holding a touch to reach the secondary action
notes: Long press is the touch counterpart of secondary click; worth a contrastWith edge to context-menu (already on site).

name: Long shadow
definition: A flat era decoration where an icon casts a single hard shadow at 45 degrees that runs far past the shape before fading out.
useWhen: one hard 45 degree shadow running off the icon

sources.title: NN/g: Flat Design: Its Origins, Its Problems, and Why Flat 2.0 Is Better for Users

notes: NN/g cites it as flat 2.0 gone wrong: decorative depth that carries no information.

name: Lorem ipsum
definition: Scrambled pseudo-Latin placeholder text used so a layout can be judged on its shape and texture before the real copy exists.
useWhen: filling a layout before the copy is written
notes: Greeking is the broader practice; lorem ipsum is the specific text and the far more common search query.

name: Lottie
definition: A JSON format for vector animations exported from design tools and played natively on the web and mobile, so complex motion ships without video.
useWhen: designed animation must ship as an asset, not as code

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: A format rather than a design concept; drop it if the taxonomy excludes tooling. demo: none because there is nothing to illustrate without shipping the runtime.

name: Low poly
definition: A 3D style that keeps the polygon count low enough to see, so surfaces read as faceted triangles under flat shading instead of smooth curves.
useWhen: deliberately faceted 3D art with visible triangles

sources.title: Aesthetics of Design: Low Poly Aesthetic
Sessions College: What is the deal with low poly art?

notes: Started as a rendering budget in games and became a look; flat shading, not the triangle count alone, is what makes it read as a style.

name: Magazine layout
definition: An editorial composition with mixed column widths, one dominant lead story and smaller supporting items arranged around it.
useWhen: an editorial page with one clear lead and ranked rest

name: Magic link
definition: Signing in by clicking a single-use link emailed on request, with no password, and a screen that waits and offers to resend while the mail arrives.
useWhen: you sign in by clicking a link sent to your email
notes: The waiting screen with a resend timer is the demoable half of the term.

name: Magic tap
definition: A screen reader gesture that fires the one action a screen is most likely about, answering the call or pausing the track, without the reader hunting for the control.
useWhen: a screen has one obvious action worth a shortcut

sources.title: Apple: Supporting Accessibility (View Controller Programming Guide)

name: Magnetic button
definition: A control that leans toward the cursor as it approaches, translating a fraction of the distance to its centre so it reads as attracted rather than merely hovered.
useWhen: a hero control should feel alive before it is clicked

sources.title: Init HTML: magnetic hover effect, cursor-attracted buttons

notes: Distinct from hover lift: the displacement tracks pointer position, so it needs pointermove plus a spring back to rest when the pointer leaves.

name: Marching ants
definition: The animated dashed outline that circles a selection, moving continuously so the boundary reads as active rather than drawn.
useWhen: the crawling dashed border around a selection

sources.title: Computer Hope: What is a marquee?

notes: Cross-category: filed as motion since the animation is the term, but discovered through selection vocabulary.

name: Marking menu
definition: A radial menu that can be answered before it appears: waiting shows the menu, while a confident stroke in the item's direction selects it outright.
useWhen: an expert stroke that skips showing the menu

sources.title: Buxton: User learning and performance with marking menus

name: Marking pattern
definition: A scanning shape where the eye holds one spot on the screen while content scrolls past underneath it, most common on phones.
useWhen: reasoning about where eyes rest while scrolling

sources.title: F-Shaped Pattern of Reading on the Web, NN/g

notes: Do not confuse with the marking menu, a separate gesture control already captured in the component sweep.

name: Marquee
definition: Text or logos that scroll continuously across a strip, either as a decorative ticker or because a label is too long for its box.
useWhen: content is wider than its box and must still be read

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: The deprecated <marquee> element is worth a disambiguation note in the article body.

name: Material 3 Expressive
definition: Google's 2025 update to Material 3, with bolder shapes, larger type, spring based motion physics, and a wider set of dynamic color variants.
useWhen: Material turned up: big shapes, springy motion

sources.title: Google blog: Material 3 Expressive redesign for Android and Wear OS

notes: Announced May 2025, shipped on Pixel with Android 16 in September 2025.

name: Material You
definition: Google's personalization layer where the system derives an app's entire color scheme from the user's wallpaper, so every app shifts together.
useWhen: the palette comes from the user's wallpaper
