notes: Overlaps the color category; recorded as aesthetic because Material You names a whole design language, not just a palette. Variants documented: Tonal Spot (Android 12), Neutral, Vibrant, Expressive (Android 13).

name: Maximalism
definition: A style that fills the screen on purpose with layered color, pattern, and type, treating abundance rather than restraint as the message.
useWhen: abundance is the point, not a failure of editing

sources.title: Envato: Minimalism vs. Maximalism: Battle of the Divisive Design Styles
Twine: Minimalism vs Maximalism: The Pros and Cons for Web Design

name: Measure
definition: The width of a column of text, judged in characters per line, with roughly 45 to 75 treated as the comfortable range for reading.
useWhen: deciding how wide a paragraph is allowed to get

sources.title: Choose a comfortable measure (Elements of Typographic Style Applied to the Web)

name: Media controls
definition: The cluster of play, pause, skip, volume and fullscreen controls attached to a player, which usually hides itself while playing.
useWhen: the control bar of a video or audio player

name: Media object
definition: The pairing of a fixed size image or avatar on one side with a heading and text that fills the rest, repeated everywhere in interfaces.
useWhen: avatar or thumbnail beside a block of text

sources.title: The media object saves hundreds of lines of code, Nicole Sullivan
The Media Object, A Bunch of Ways, CSS-Tricks

notes: Named by Nicole Sullivan in 2010 as the flagship example of OOCSS. Attributable origin, which makes a good article.

name: Mega menu
definition: A large navigation panel that drops from a top level item and shows many links at once, grouped into columns with headings.
useWhen: a nav panel too big to be a simple list

name: Memphis design
definition: The 1980s Memphis Group look of clashing pastels, squiggles, confetti dots, and terrazzo shapes scattered across a layout.
useWhen: squiggles and confetti shapes on clashing pastels
notes: Must be disambiguated from Corporate Memphis, which only borrows the name.

name: Mention autocomplete
definition: Typing a trigger character inside a text field to open a filtered list of people or objects, inserting the chosen one as a linked token.
useWhen: typing @ opens a list of people to insert
notes: Distinguished from slash-command by what selection does: a mention inserts text, a slash command runs something.

name: Menu bar
definition: A permanent horizontal row of menu titles (File, Edit, View) whose menus open on click and then follow the pointer along the row.
useWhen: the desktop row of File, Edit, View menus

sources.title: ARIA APG: Menu and Menubar pattern

notes: Its keyboard model (arrow keys move between menus, one tab stop for the whole bar) is the reason it is a pattern rather than a row of buttons.

name: Menu bar extra
definition: A small application controlled item living in the system menu bar or tray, usually an icon that opens a compact panel of status and controls.
useWhen: an app's icon living in the system bar or tray
notes: Windows calls the region the notification area but everyone says system tray, which is a nice misnomer note.

name: Mesh gradient
definition: A soft multi-point blend built from colours placed on a grid and smoothed between them, giving the blurred, cloudlike backgrounds a linear gradient cannot.
useWhen: a soft multi-point colour blend, not a straight ramp
notes: Tail gold: a very common visual with no name most designers can produce on demand.

name: Metered paywall
definition: A paywall that grants a fixed number of free items per period and counts down publicly, so the barrier arrives only after the reader is invested.
useWhen: you get three free articles a month and a counter says so
notes: The fade-to-white teaser above it is a separate visual device, sometimes called a content fade or gradient fade.

name: Metro
definition: Microsoft's typography led design language of flat colored tiles, large light headings, and motion used in place of chrome, shadow, and texture.
useWhen: flat colored tiles and oversized light headings
notes: Historically important as the trigger for flat design, but no authoritative live source captured this sweep. Verify against Microsoft or Wikipedia before authoring.

name: Mica
definition: Fluent's opaque app background material, subtly tinted with the user's desktop wallpaper color and going neutral when the window loses focus.
useWhen: an opaque window background tinted by the wallpaper

sources.title: Microsoft Learn: Materials used in Windows apps

notes: Shares the wallpaper-personalization idea with Material You, from the opposite vendor. Good contrastWith pair with acrylic (opaque versus transient).

name: Microinteraction
definition: A small self-contained loop of trigger, rule, feedback, and result, such as a toggle that flips, buzzes, and settles into its new state.
useWhen: one tiny complete interaction, trigger to feedback
notes: Cross-category candidate with motion; the motion sweep may also propose it.

name: Microsurvey
definition: A one or two question survey placed inside the product at the moment being asked about, answered in place rather than on a separate page.
useWhen: a one-question survey inside the thing it asks about

name: Mid-century modern
definition: A 1950s and 60s style of muted mustard, teal, and burnt orange, tapered organic shapes, textured paper grounds, and friendly geometric sans type.
useWhen: muted 50s palette with tapered organic shapes

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions

notes: The optimistic half of the same era that raygun gothic and atompunk draw on, which is why it keeps appearing next to retro-futurism.

name: Middle click
definition: A press of the scroll wheel button, conventionally used to open a link in a new tab, close a tab, or start autoscrolling.
useWhen: the wheel press, not the left or right button

name: Mini cart
definition: A compact view of the basket opened from the cart icon, confirming what was just added and offering checkout without leaving the current page.
useWhen: the small basket panel that opens from the cart icon
notes: drawer already exists as the component; this is the commerce reading of it.

name: Minimalism
definition: A style that reduces an interface to one typeface, one accent color, and generous empty space, letting whitespace rather than ornament carry hierarchy.
useWhen: hierarchy carried by space, not by decoration

sources.title: Zoviz: Minimalist vs Maximalist Web Design

name: Minimap
definition: A shrunken overview of a long document or canvas beside the scrollbar, with a box showing which part is currently on screen.
useWhen: a zoomed out map of a long document or canvas
notes: Named by editors (VS Code, Sublime) and canvas tools (Figma, Miro) rather than by design systems.

name: Misdirection
definition: Using contrast, size, and position to pull attention to the option the business prefers while the other option is present but visually demoted.
useWhen: the choice you want is there but styled to be missed

name: Mixed state checkbox
definition: A checkbox showing a third, indeterminate state when only some of the boxes it governs are checked.
useWhen: a parent box stands over a partly checked group
notes: Cross-category: reads as a component to most people; recorded here because the third state exists for the semantics.

name: Mobile first
definition: Designing and writing the narrow layout first and adding rules as space is gained, so the small screen is the default rather than the fallback.
useWhen: which end of the range you start designing from

name: Modal presentation
definition: The slide-up-over transition that puts a sheet or dialog in front of the current screen while what is behind recedes, the platform motion for entering a modal context.
useWhen: a task takes over the screen and must be dismissible
notes: Captured from uiterms.com in round one. Push transition, parallax and spring easing from that same capture were already recorded, so this was the only new one.

name: Model selector
definition: The control in an assistant interface that picks which model answers, usually a menu carrying a short description of each option.
useWhen: choosing which model answers the request
notes: New vocabulary, still settling. Worth an entry precisely because the naming is being decided now.

name: Modifier key
definition: A key held to change what another input means, so the same click or keystroke can copy instead of move, or add instead of replace.
useWhen: a held key changes what the next input does

name: Modular grid
definition: A grid with both columns and rows, dividing the page into equal modules that content can span in either direction.
useWhen: content that needs to span rows as well as columns
notes: Contrast set worth building: manuscript, column, modular, hierarchical, baseline. The classic grid taxonomy.

name: Modular scale
definition: A type scale generated by multiplying a base size by a fixed ratio, so every step is proportionally related to the one before it.
useWhen: generating sizes from a ratio instead of picking them

sources.title: What the Font are Vertical Rhythm and Modular Scale?

name: Momentum scrolling
definition: Content that keeps moving after the finger lifts, decelerating as though it had mass, so one flick can travel a long way.
useWhen: scrolling that coasts after the gesture ends

sources.title: MDN: Basic concepts of scroll snap

name: Monochromatic palette
definition: A scheme drawn from one hue at many lightness and saturation levels, so hierarchy comes from contrast alone rather than from colour difference.
useWhen: one hue carrying the whole interface

sources.title: The Ultimate Color Glossary For UI Designers

name: Monospace
definition: A typeface in which every character occupies the same horizontal width, so characters stack into columns down the page.
useWhen: code, terminals, or anything that must line up in columns

name: Morph transition
definition: A transition where a shape or icon is interpolated into a different shape rather than swapped, so the two states read as one object changing.
useWhen: two states are the same object in different forms

name: Morphing control
definition: One control that changes what it says and does according to state, showing play when paused and pause when playing rather than offering both.
useWhen: one button that becomes the next action each time

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Multifunctional Controls instead of more parts

notes: Accessibility trap worth naming: a morphing label breaks the promise that a control's name describes what it does.

name: Mostly fluid
definition: A responsive pattern where a multi column grid stretches with the viewport up to a maximum width, then centres, stacking only on the smallest screens.
useWhen: one grid that just widens, then caps
notes: One of Luke Wroblewski's five multi-device layout patterns (tiny tweaks, mostly fluid, column drop, layout shifter, off canvas). Consider a single parent entry with five children.

name: Motion actuation
definition: Triggering a function by moving the device itself, such as shake to undo, which needs a plain control alternative and an off switch.
useWhen: the gesture is a shake or tilt of the device

name: Motion blur
definition: Blurring an element along its direction of travel so fast movement reads as speed instead of teleporting, borrowed from film and rare but real in interfaces.
useWhen: something moves fast enough that a sharp frame looks wrong

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: Expensive on the web: filter: blur() is not a compositor-only property, which is half of why the term is rarer here than in film.

name: Motion path
definition: A defined path an element travels along, with its distance and rotation along that path animated instead of its x and y positions.
useWhen: an element should follow a specific route
notes: MDN notes the property was called motion-path in early drafts, which is exactly the naming confusion an entry can settle.

name: Motion token
definition: A named duration or easing value published by a design system, so timings are chosen from a set rather than typed per component.
useWhen: timings should be system decisions, not per-component ones

sources.title: Material Design 3: easing and duration tokens

notes: Overlaps the existing duration and easing entries; keep as the entry about naming and reuse, not about the values.

name: Mouse gesture
definition: A command issued by the shape of a pointer stroke, usually with a button held, so a movement stands in for a menu choice.
useWhen: a drawn stroke that means a command

name: Multi column layout
definition: An application shell with three or more vertical regions, typically navigation, a list, and a reading pane, as in a mail client.
useWhen: three regions at once: navigate, list, read
notes: Clashes with the CSS multi-column module (column-count), which is a different thing. Disambiguate in the article.

name: Multi select
definition: A select that accepts several values at once, usually showing the chosen ones as removable tokens inside the field.
useWhen: one field, several answers
notes: Note the interaction file already carries multi-select as the selection gesture (shift click, ctrl click). Merge step must keep these apart or rename one.

name: Multi-touch
definition: Input from more than one simultaneous contact point, letting a surface distinguish two-finger scrolling, pinching, rotating and larger finger counts.
useWhen: naming input that depends on more than one finger at once
notes: Hard to demonstrate honestly with a single ghost cursor, so demo is none rather than a faked animation.

name: Multi-window mode
definition: A windowing mode where two or more apps share one screen, side by side, stacked, or as freeform windows, so every app must survive being any size.
useWhen: the app is only part of the screen
notes: The reason window-size-class exists: the window, not the device, is what a layout responds to. Apple's Stage Manager is the same idea, unverified this sweep.

name: Multimodal interface
definition: An interface that accepts and answers in more than one channel at once, letting a person speak, type, touch, or point and pick whichever suits the moment.
useWhen: voice, touch, and screen share one interaction

sources.title: NN/g: Voice First, the future of interaction?
UXmatters: Voice first versus the multimodal user interfaces of the future

notes: Cross-category: recorded as pattern, surfaced by an aesthetic sweep of a catalog that lists voice-first multimodal as a style. Voice-first is the stricter claim, that voice leads and the screen assists.

name: Nagging
definition: Interrupting a task again and again with the same request, so that agreeing becomes the cheapest way to be left alone.
useWhen: the same prompt keeps returning until you give in

name: Name, role, value
definition: The three things every control has to expose to assistive technology: what it is called, what kind of thing it is, and what state it is currently in.
useWhen: auditing whether a custom control is really a control

name: Named color
definition: One of the CSS keywords such as tomato or rebeccapurple that map to fixed sRGB values, a fossil vocabulary still useful for prototypes and debugging.
useWhen: the keyword colours built into CSS

name: Named grid areas
definition: Naming regions of a grid and drawing the layout as rows of those names, so items are placed by name instead of by line number.
useWhen: placing items by name instead of by number
notes: MDN itself calls it the ascii-art method, which is the phrase most designers recognise.

name: Named instance
definition: A specific point in a variable font's design space that the designer has given a style name, so it can be picked like an ordinary weight.
useWhen: picking a named style out of a variable font

name: Navigation menu
definition: A menu of destinations rather than commands, where opening an item moves you somewhere instead of running an action.
useWhen: a menu whose items are places, not commands
notes: The accessibility point that earns the entry: a nav menu is a list of links in a nav landmark, not a role=menu, and treating it as a menu breaks it.

name: Navigation rail
definition: A narrow vertical strip of top level destinations at the side of a screen, used at medium widths where a bottom bar is wasteful and a drawer is too heavy.
useWhen: top level navigation on a medium width window
notes: Cross category: this is a component, found through the layout sweep because it is defined by the window width it belongs to. The component sweep may also produce it.

name: Neo-skeuomorphism
definition: The current return of depth and material to interfaces, using restrained texture, shadow, and highlight instead of literal leather, metal, and felt.
useWhen: depth is back, but abstracted rather than literal

sources.title: Userology: Flat Design is Dead: The Rise of Neo-Skeuomorphism in 2026

notes: Trend-piece vocabulary rather than a settled term; keep as a stub unless the usage holds.

name: Neon glow
definition: A saturated color surrounded by layered soft shadows of the same hue, so type or a border reads as a lit tube against a dark surface.
useWhen: type or borders that look lit rather than filled
notes: Built from stacked text-shadow or box-shadow at increasing blur radii; bloom is the same idea in rendering vocabulary.

name: Nested interactive
definition: A focusable control placed inside another control, such as a button inside a link or a checkbox inside a row that is itself clickable, which leaves an unreachable tab stop.
useWhen: a whole card is clickable and so is its button

aliases.name: interactive controls must not be nested

sources.title: Deque: Interactive controls must not be nested

name: Neubrutalism
definition: A loud style built from thick black outlines, saturated flat color, square corners, and hard offset shadows with zero blur.
useWhen: black outline plus a hard unblurred shadow

sources.title: NN/g: Neobrutalism: Definition and Best Practices

notes: Spelling is genuinely split: NN/g writes neobrutalism, the neubrutalism.com guide writes neubrutalism. Both spellings must resolve.

name: Neutral palette
definition: The greys an interface is mostly made of, ramped from page background to body text, which carry the structure while the accent carries the attention.
useWhen: the greys that most of the interface is actually made of

name: New Wave design
definition: The postmodern break from Swiss order: stair-stepped rules, diagonal and letter-spaced type, weights mixed inside a word, and text reversed out of bars.
useWhen: the Swiss grid kept but deliberately violated

sources.title: Hue and Eye: New Wave graphic design explained

notes: The missing middle between swiss-style and memphis-design: same tools, opposite intent. Weingart taught at Basel, which is why it is called Swiss punk.

name: No results state
definition: What a search or filtered list shows when nothing matched, naming the query, explaining why, and offering a way to loosen the constraints.
useWhen: the screen shown when a search matches nothing
notes: empty-state and zero-state already exist on the site. This is the distinct no-results reading; if the merge step folds it in, keep no results and zero results as aliases there.

name: Non-breaking space
definition: A space that renders normally but forbids a line break, gluing two words together so they never end up on separate lines.
useWhen: keeping a number and its unit on one line

name: Non-text contrast
definition: The requirement that controls, focus indicators and meaningful graphics reach 3:1 against what is next to them, which is the rule that governs borders and icons.
useWhen: contrast for controls and icons rather than text
notes: Cross-category: accessibility. Kept separate from contrast-ratio because the 3:1 threshold for controls is what people get wrong.

name: Notification center
definition: A panel collecting notifications that were missed or kept, usually opened from a bell with an unread count.
useWhen: the panel behind the bell icon
notes: The counterpart to toast: toasts are the ones you may miss, this is where they go.

name: Notification digest
definition: Collecting many similar alerts into one summary rather than delivering each, so the count rises but the number of interruptions does not.
useWhen: many alerts arrive as one grouped summary
notes: Android says group and summary notification; Apple says notification summary. Both names are live.

name: Nudge
definition: Moving or changing a value by one small fixed step with an arrow key, with a modifier switching to a larger step.
useWhen: moving something by exact steps with the keyboard

sources.title: Figma Learn: Adjust alignment, rotation, position, and dimensions

name: Object fit
definition: How a picture or video is resized inside a box whose shape it does not match: stretched to fill, letterboxed to fit whole, or cropped to cover every edge.
useWhen: choosing between cropping and letterboxing
notes: The everyday cover versus contain decision, and the term that ties letterboxing and pillarboxing to a real property. Pairs with object-position, which chooses what the crop keeps.

name: Oblique
definition: An upright typeface slanted to the right without redrawing its letters, which is why it lacks the cursive forms a true italic has.
useWhen: distinguishing a slanted roman from a real italic

name: Obstruction
definition: Putting deliberate hurdles in front of an action the business does not want taken, so the effort itself does the discouraging.
useWhen: the path exists but is made exhausting on purpose
notes: Not all added friction is deceptive: type-to-confirm is deliberate friction in the reader's favour, which makes a good contrast pair.

name: Off canvas
definition: Keeping secondary regions parked outside the viewport and sliding them in on demand, instead of stacking them below the main content.
useWhen: secondary panels parked off screen until called
notes: Close to drawer (already on the site). Off canvas is the layout strategy, drawer is the component; keep as contrastWith.

name: Offline indicator
definition: A persistent notice that the product has lost its connection, saying what still works, what is queued, and when the last sync happened.
useWhen: the bar telling you the app is working offline
notes: Pairs with optimistic-ui (already on site): optimistic UI is what fills the gap this indicator explains.

name: OKLCH
definition: A colour notation of lightness, chroma and hue built on Oklab, where changing the hue leaves the perceived lightness alone and equal steps look equal.
useWhen: writing colour so that equal numeric steps look equal

name: Oldstyle figures
definition: Numerals with varying heights, some rising and some dropping below the baseline, so numbers blend into lowercase running text.
useWhen: numbers inside a sentence, not in a table

sources.title: OpenType at Work: Figure Styles (Type Network)

name: On-color
definition: A colour defined by what it sits on, such as on-primary or on-surface, so every fill ships with the foreground guaranteed to be readable against it.
useWhen: the foreground colour that ships paired with a fill

implementations.name: On primary, On surface, On error

notes: Tail gold: the 'on' prefix is opaque to newcomers and is exactly the kind of word this site exists to answer.

name: Onboarding checklist
definition: A persistent list of setup tasks with completion state and a progress meter, kept available so the reader can return to unfinished steps.
useWhen: a setup list you can leave and come back to

sources.title: GOV.UK Design System: Complete multiple tasks

notes: GOV.UK renamed Task list pages to Complete multiple tasks and split out a Task list component; both names are live in the wild.

name: Onboarding tour
definition: A short sequence of pointers layered over a live interface, each naming one control, advanced by the reader and skippable at any point.
useWhen: a stepped overlay walks you around a live screen

name: One thing per page
definition: Asking a single question on each screen of a form so the reader never chooses which field to answer first and errors point somewhere unambiguous.
useWhen: each form screen asks exactly one question
notes: GOV.UK files it as Question pages; the phrase one thing per page is the community headword.

name: One-time code login
definition: Signing in by typing a short code sent to a second channel, keeping the reader inside the app rather than sending them out to a mail client.
useWhen: you type a six digit code sent by mail or text
notes: The segmented code input is a component (pin input, one-time code field); this record is the flow around it.

name: Opacity
definition: How much of what is behind an element shows through it, applied to the whole element and its children at once rather than to a single colour value.
useWhen: fading an entire element and everything inside it
notes: Merge candidate with alpha-channel; the useful entry is the contrast between them, so both records should survive as a contrastWith pair.

name: OpenType features
definition: Optional glyph substitutions and spacing rules packed inside a font file, addressed by four-letter tags and switched on from CSS.
useWhen: reaching for a font capability that is off by default

name: Optical alignment
definition: Nudging an element off its measured position so it looks aligned, correcting for shapes whose bounding box lies about their visual centre.
useWhen: it measures right but still looks wrong
notes: Excellent demo candidate: a play button in a circle, mathematically centred versus optically centred.

name: Optical kerning
definition: Letting software space letter pairs by looking at their shapes, instead of using the pair values the type designer built into the font.
useWhen: a font's own spacing is unreliable at display size
notes: Kerning already exists on the site; this is the metric vs optical distinction, which is a separate question and a separate search.

name: Optical size
definition: A font adjusting its own drawing for the size it is set at, thickening strokes and opening spacing for small text and refining both for large.
useWhen: type that should be redrawn, not just scaled

implementations.name: SF Pro Text and SF Pro Display switching

name: Orbit
definition: Rotating a camera around a fixed point by dragging, so the scene appears to turn while the subject stays centered.
useWhen: dragging to turn a 3D view around its subject

sources.title: Apple Developer: Explore game input in visionOS

name: Orbit animation
definition: One element circling another on a continuous path, used for logo constellations and loading states where the revolving is the ornament.
useWhen: elements should revolve around a fixed centre
notes: Slug is orbit-animation because interaction.json already owns 'orbit' for the three-finger camera gesture.

name: Order summary
definition: The persistent panel beside a checkout listing items, quantities, and every cost line, kept visible so nothing about the total arrives as a surprise.
useWhen: the panel beside checkout that itemises what you will pay

name: Orientation lock
definition: Restricting a screen to portrait or landscape, which strands anyone whose device is fixed in a mount or a wheelchair arm in the orientation the design refused.
useWhen: a layout only works one way up

name: Origin-aware animation
definition: Scaling or fading a panel out of the control that opened it by putting its transform origin on that anchor, so the panel reads as belonging to its trigger.
useWhen: a menu should look like it came from its button
notes: The reason a popover placed by a positioning library still needs its origin set: placement alone does not tell the motion where it came from.

name: Ornament
definition: A small panel of controls that floats just outside a window edge in visionOS, staying with the window without covering its contents.
useWhen: controls must stay reachable without eating the content

sources.title: Create with Swift: Creating Ornaments in visionOS

notes: Spatial vocabulary with no web equivalent, which is exactly what makes it worth defining. On visionOS tab bars and toolbars become ornaments by default.

name: Orphan
definition: A first line of a paragraph left alone at the bottom of a column or page, with the rest of the paragraph carried over.
useWhen: naming a first line left behind at the bottom of a column

name: Outline color
definition: The role that draws boundaries, split into a stronger value for edges that must be seen and a weaker one for dividers that only need to hint at structure.
useWhen: the colour of borders and dividers as a named role

implementations.name: steps 6 to 8, borders and focus rings

name: Overscan safe area
definition: The inset a television layout keeps clear of the screen edge, about five percent, because sets crop the outer frame and anything near it disappears.
useWhen: laying out for a screen that crops its own edges

sources.title: Layouts in the Leanback UI toolkit, Android Developers

notes: Broadcast vocabulary that survived into TV app design: 48dp by 27dp on a 960 by 540 layout. Sibling of safe-area on phones and display-cutout.

name: Overscroll
definition: Scrolling input that continues after a scroller has reached its limit, which platforms answer with a bounce, a glow, or a handoff to the parent.
useWhen: input keeps scrolling past the end of the content

name: Overshoot
definition: The part of a motion that carries past its final value before coming back, the visual signature of an underdamped spring or a back easing curve.
useWhen: motion should read as having weight and momentum

implementations.name: cubic-bezier() with a control point outside 0 to 1

notes: Frequently confused with bounce; overshoot passes the target once, bounce oscillates around it.

name: Overview plus detail
definition: A layout that shows a compressed overview and a detailed view at the same time in separate regions, so the reader keeps their place while inspecting one part.
useWhen: a map or minimap kept beside the detail

sources.title: A Review of Overview+Detail, Zooming, and Focus+Context Interfaces, Cockburn, Karlson and Bederson

notes: The formal name for the code editor minimap, the map inset and the page thumbnails rail. Its contrast partner is focus-plus-context.

name: Owned element
definition: A child the accessibility tree is told to adopt from elsewhere in the DOM, used when the visual nesting a role requires is impossible in the markup.
useWhen: a listbox and its options cannot be nested in markup
notes: Support is patchy and it is easy to build a tree nobody can navigate, so canonicalize may want the cautionary framing.

name: Page break
definition: Where content is cut to continue in the next fragment, a printed page, a column or a region, and the rules that stop a heading being stranded at the cut.
useWhen: controlling where printed or column content splits
notes: The layout side of the widow and orphan terms the typography sweep already has. Print stylesheets are the case nobody tests until someone prints an invoice.

name: Page curl
definition: A page turn that lifts and bends the leaf away from the spine as the finger drags it, the most literal transition a reader can be given.
useWhen: turning a page should read as paper rather than as a slide

sources.title: MacRumors: re-enable the classic page turning animation in Apple Books
Creating a page curl transition in SwiftUI

notes: Apple Books offers Curl, Slide and None, which is the clearest evidence the word names a choice rather than a decoration. Effectively absent from the web, so a specimen would be an approximation.

name: Page header
definition: The band at the top of a screen carrying the page title, its context, and the actions that apply to the page as a whole.
useWhen: the title band that owns the page's own actions
notes: Contrast with app-bar (already on the site): the app bar belongs to the app, the page header belongs to this page.

name: Page title
definition: The document title, the first thing a screen reader speaks and the only label a reader has when picking between tabs, windows, and history entries.
useWhen: the label a page carries outside its own viewport
notes: iframe: the subject is the document title, which only exists at document scope.

name: Page transition
definition: Motion that covers a navigation between two whole pages or routes, replacing the hard cut a document load would otherwise produce.
useWhen: navigation between routes should feel continuous
notes: iframe because the subject is document scope: a real navigation inside the specimen document.

name: Pagination
definition: The numbered row of page links under a long result set, with previous and next controls and usually an ellipsis where numbers are skipped.
useWhen: results split into numbered pages

name: Pan
definition: Moving the viewport across content in any direction while keeping contact, so the content feels anchored to the finger or cursor.
useWhen: moving the view over content rather than the content itself

name: Pancake stack
definition: A three row page where the header and footer take only the height they need and the middle row absorbs every remaining pixel, even when the content is short.
useWhen: header, body, footer with the body taking the slack
notes: From Una Kravets' ten one line layouts. The vocabulary designers actually use for the problem sticky-footer used to solve with hacks.

name: Pane
definition: A layout container that holds one destination's content inside a window, either fixed or flexible in width, combined with other panes to fill the space.
useWhen: naming one region of a multi region window
notes: Material 3 names four kinds: fixed, flexible, floating, semi permanent. Distinguish from panel, which many systems use loosely for any boxed region.

name: Pangram
definition: A sentence that uses every letter of the alphabet at least once, used to show a whole character set in one line.
useWhen: you need one line that shows every letter

name: Parallax
definition: Moving layers at different rates against the same input, so the slower layers read as farther away and the scene gains depth.
useWhen: depth should come from relative speed, not shadow
notes: One of the motions most often disabled under Reduce Motion, which makes it a good pair with the reduced-motion entry.

name: Parenting
definition: Tying one element's motion to another's so moving or scaling the parent carries the child with it, which is how a group of parts reads as one object instead of several.
useWhen: several elements must move as one because one of them leads

sources.title: UX Magazine: creating usability with motion, the UX in Motion Manifesto
Issara Willenskomer: the UX in Motion Manifesto

notes: One of the twelve UX in Motion principles. accessibility.json already uses 'reparenting' for the unrelated DOM-order sense, which canonicalize should keep apart.

name: Passkey
definition: Signing in with a device-held credential unlocked by the reader's own biometric or screen lock, so the interface asks for a face or fingerprint, not a secret.
useWhen: signing in with a fingerprint instead of a password
notes: demo none: the interesting part is an operating system dialog that cannot be reproduced honestly in a page.

name: Password strength meter
definition: A gauge that scores a password while it is typed and names what would improve it, replacing a list of rules with continuous feedback.
useWhen: the bar that rates a password as you type it

name: Pause, stop, hide
definition: A visible control for content that moves, blinks, scrolls, or updates on its own, so a reader can stop it before reading around it.
useWhen: something animates or refreshes without being asked

name: Paywall
definition: A barrier that stops access to content or a feature until the reader pays, placed either before anything is shown or partway into the content.
useWhen: the point where content stops until you pay

name: Perceptual duration
definition: How long a spring appears to take, measured to the point the movement stops being visible rather than to its mathematical rest, the figure to quote against a timed animation.
useWhen: a spring must be compared with a duration
notes: The word that makes a spring reviewable: without it a designer cannot answer 'how long is this'.

name: Perceptual uniformity
definition: The property of a colour space where equal numeric distances look like equal visual differences, which is what makes a generated ramp step evenly.
useWhen: explaining why an HSL ramp looks uneven and an OKLCH one does not

name: Permission priming
definition: Explaining why access is needed in the product's own dialog first, and only firing the operating system prompt once the reader has said yes to that.
useWhen: your own dialog asks before the real system prompt does
notes: Genuine long-tail gold: three competing names for one well-understood behaviour.

name: Petite caps
definition: Capitals drawn to exactly x-height, shorter than small caps, so they sit flush with the lowercase around them.
useWhen: you need caps that match x-height exactly

name: Picture in picture
definition: A small always on top window that keeps video or navigation visible in a corner while the reader works in another app or scrolls another page.
useWhen: keeping video visible while doing something else
notes: Cross category: could sit with components. Captured here because it is a window mode, and because the web now has a Document Picture-in-Picture API.

name: Pilcrow
definition: The paragraph mark, a reversed P with a doubled stem, used to show where a paragraph begins or as a hover anchor beside a heading.
useWhen: naming the paragraph symbol in an editor

name: Pinch to zoom
definition: Two fingers moving apart or together on a surface to scale content up or down, with the scale tracking the distance between them.
useWhen: two fingers changing the scale of what is on screen

sources.title: Material Design: Gestures (pinch open and closed)

name: Pixel art UI
definition: An interface drawn on a visible pixel grid, with bitmap type, hard aliased edges, and icons kept at their original low resolution.
useWhen: the pixels are meant to be visible

sources.title: Sage: Retro Web Design: When Pixel Art Belongs on Your Site

notes: The load-bearing CSS is image-rendering: pixelated plus an integer scale factor.

name: Placeholder as label
definition: The antipattern of using placeholder text as a field's only label, which vanishes on typing and usually fails both contrast and naming.
useWhen: naming why a placeholder-only field is broken

name: Plain language
definition: Writing interface copy at the reading level of the people using it, with short sentences, familiar words, and the point first, rather than at the level of the org chart.
useWhen: the copy is correct but nobody can act on it

name: Playhead
definition: The marker showing the current position in a timeline or track, which travels during playback and can be dragged to move it.
useWhen: the marker showing where playback is
notes: Video editing vocabulary that most web people never learn even though they use it daily.

name: Point size
definition: The nominal size of type, measured in points, which describes the body the letters are drawn on rather than the height of any letter.
useWhen: explaining why 16pt in two fonts looks different

name: Pointer cancellation
definition: Activating a control on pointer release rather than press, so someone who lands on the wrong target can slide off and abort.
useWhen: letting a mis-press be taken back before release

name: Pointer capture
definition: Redirecting all events for one pointer to a chosen element, so a drag keeps reaching the control it started on even when it wanders off.
useWhen: a drag must keep its grip after leaving the element

name: Pointer gestures
definition: Path based or multi finger gestures such as pinch, swipe, and draw, which need a single pointer equivalent to stay operable.
useWhen: a pinch or swipe is the only way in

name: Pointer lock
definition: Hiding the cursor and reading only its movement deltas, so input keeps flowing past the edges of the screen instead of stopping at them.
useWhen: input is relative movement, not a screen position
notes: Needs a real user gesture and a browser permission prompt, so it cannot be demonstrated in attract mode.

name: Politeness level
definition: The urgency setting on a live region: polite waits for a pause in speech, assertive interrupts whatever is being read.
useWhen: choosing whether an update may interrupt speech

name: Pop art style
definition: A comic and advertising style of flat primary color, heavy black outlines, printed dot shading, speech balloons, and bold condensed capitals.
useWhen: comic outlines, flat primaries, and printed dots

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions
Inkbot Design: 20 iconic graphic design styles

notes: Shares its dot shading with halftone and its heavy outlines with neubrutalism, so canonicalize should decide whether it survives as its own entry.

name: Pop in
definition: An entrance that scales slightly past full size before settling, so the element arrives with a small snap instead of simply being there.
useWhen: an arriving element should feel eager rather than merely present
notes: Overlaps entrance-animation and overshoot; kept because 'pop in' is what people ask for by name. Merge candidate.

name: Popover arrow
definition: The small triangle joining a popover or tooltip to the thing it belongs to, which flips and slides as the popover repositions.
useWhen: the little triangle pointing at the trigger
notes: Everyone ships one, everyone calls it Arrow in code, and nobody documents the word. Perfect long tail entry; Floating UI's arrow middleware is the reference behaviour.

name: Positive tabindex
definition: Using tabindex values above zero to force an order, which yanks those elements to the front of the whole page sequence and is almost always a bug.
useWhen: someone proposes tabindex="1" to fix an order
notes: Antipattern term. Verify the MDN URL before publishing: the global-attributes path moved with the Reference reshuffle.

name: POUR
definition: The four principles WCAG is built on, perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust, used as a shorthand for sorting an accessibility problem into a bucket.
useWhen: classifying what kind of barrier you are looking at
notes: Vocabulary rather than an interface part; demo: none unless canonicalize finds a way to show it.

name: Predictive back
definition: A back gesture that reveals the destination underneath while the finger is still down, so the swipe can be finished or abandoned once the reader has seen where it goes.
useWhen: a back swipe should show its destination before it commits
notes: The platform's own name for a gesture-driven interruptible transition, which is why it is worth recording next to interactive-transition rather than folded into it.

name: Increased contrast
definition: A user preference for more contrast than a theme's default, honoured by strengthening borders, text, and state colours rather than by shifting hues.
useWhen: the system asks for a higher contrast version

sources.title: MDN: Using media queries for accessibility

name: Reduced motion
definition: A user preference asking interfaces to cut non-essential animation, honoured by shortening, cross fading, or removing movement rather than by doing nothing.
useWhen: the reader has asked the system for less movement
notes: Cross-category: arguably belongs to motion. Recorded here because the preference and its media query are accessibility vocabulary.

name: Preselected opt-in
definition: Arriving at a choice with the answer that benefits the business already ticked, so consent is collected from everyone who does not notice.
useWhen: the marketing box is already ticked when you get there
notes: Sharpest contrast pair on the site: smart-defaults and preselected-opt-in are the same mechanic judged by whose interest the default serves.

name: Presence indicator
definition: The small coloured dot on an avatar reporting whether a person is available, away, busy or offline.
useWhen: the green dot on someone's picture
notes: Colour alone carries the meaning here, which puts it straight into the use-of-color accessibility discussion.

name: Presentation role
definition: Stripping an element of its semantics while leaving it on screen, so a table used for layout or a list used for spacing stops being announced as one.
useWhen: markup you needed for layout is lying about meaning
notes: Distinct from aria-hidden: presentation keeps the element and its content readable, it only drops the role.

name: Presentational children
definition: The rule that some roles flatten everything inside them into their own label, which is why an icon and a span inside a button are never announced separately.
useWhen: markup inside a control vanishes from the a11y tree

name: Pressed state
definition: The look a control takes while it is actually being held down, confirming that the press was received before the action runs.
useWhen: the moment a control is under the finger

name: Pressure sensitivity
definition: Reading how hard a pen or finger presses, plus tilt and twist, so stroke weight and behaviour vary with the shape of the contact.
useWhen: how hard or how tilted the input is matters

name: Prime mark
definition: The slanted tick used for feet, inches, minutes, and seconds, which is a different character from either a straight quote or a curly one.
useWhen: writing feet and inches, not quoting anyone

name: Primitive color token
definition: A raw palette value named for what it is, like blue-500, sitting under the semantic layer that names colours for what they do.
useWhen: the raw palette value beneath a semantic name

sources.title: Color token naming: primitive, semantic and component layers

notes: Component-level tokens are a third tier; may deserve a separate entry outside the color category.

name: Priority plus navigation
definition: A horizontal menu that keeps as many items visible as fit and moves the rest into a More control, recalculating whenever the available width changes.
useWhen: the nav shows what fits and hides the rest behind More
notes: Coined by Michael Scharnagl, popularised by Brad Frost. overflow-menu already exists on the site as the component; this is the responsive strategy that fills it.

name: Privacy zuckering
definition: Steering people into sharing more about themselves than they meant to, by making the permissive choice the easy one and the private choice several clicks deep.
useWhen: the settings are arranged so sharing is the easy answer

sources.title: Deceptive Design: Types of deceptive pattern

notes: Named after Mark Zuckerberg; still in Brignull's original twelve but absorbed into other categories on the current types index. Verify before publishing.

name: Progress ring
definition: A circular progress indicator that fills around a ring, often with the percentage in the middle.
useWhen: progress drawn as a filling circle
notes: Frequently confused with the spinner, which reports that something is happening rather than how much is done.

name: Progressive blur
definition: A blur whose strength ramps across a region instead of applying evenly, so content fades into softness toward an edge rather than stopping at a hard line.
useWhen: content should dissolve into blur, not meet an edge

sources.title: Devs Love Coffee: Making Apple progressive blur on the web

notes: Built today by stacking backdrop-filter layers under mask-image gradients; a CSS proposal to give blur() a from and to pair would replace the stack.

name: Progressive image loading
definition: Showing a cheap stand-in for an image, a blur, a dominant colour, or a low resolution copy, and swapping in the full file once it arrives.
useWhen: a blurred or coloured block stands in until the photo loads
notes: Contrast with skeleton-screen (already on site): skeletons stand in for layout, LQIP stands in for one image.

name: Progressive profiling
definition: Collecting profile details a few at a time across separate visits, instead of demanding the whole record in one long form at registration.
useWhen: the product asks for one more detail each time you return

name: Progressive reduction
definition: Simplifying a control as the same person uses it more, dropping the label once the icon has been learned and restoring it after a long absence.
useWhen: the label falls away once you have used it enough

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Progressive Reduction instead of being static

notes: Coined at Dan Birman and Allan Grinshtein's LayerVault; more discussed than shipped, which is itself worth saying.

name: Prompt input
definition: The composer at the bottom of an assistant interface: a growing text area with attachment, model and send controls attached to it.
useWhen: the box you type an assistant request into
notes: Auto growing height without shifting the messages above it is the layout constraint that makes it a good specimen.

name: Pronunciation
definition: How a synthetic voice says a word, and the hints an author can give when the default reading turns a product name, a units string, or a homograph into nonsense.
useWhen: the screen reader mangles a name or a number
notes: Audible only, so a visual demo can at best show the markup and a transcript of what is spoken.

name: Property filter
definition: A search field that builds structured queries from tokens, letting a reader filter by named properties with operators rather than free text.
useWhen: filtering by named fields inside one search box
notes: GitHub's issue search and Linear's filter bar are the two examples everyone recognises.

name: Proximity
definition: The grouping principle that elements placed close together read as related, which is why spacing decides perceived structure more reliably than borders do.
useWhen: arguing that spacing, not lines, makes groups

sources.title: Proximity Principle in Visual Design, NN/g

notes: The classic failure case makes a good demo: a label sitting nearer the wrong field than its own.

name: Psychedelic style
definition: A 1960s poster style of vibrating complementary color, warped and interlocking lettering that fills its own shape, kaleidoscopic symmetry, and liquid distortion.
useWhen: vibrating color and lettering warped to fill a shape

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions

notes: Legibility is traded for texture on purpose, which puts it next to anti-design when it is used on a live interface.

name: Pull quote
definition: A phrase lifted out of an article and set large as a graphic element, to draw a browsing reader into the text.
useWhen: advertising a line of the article to a scanner

sources.title: How to Attract Attention With Pull Quotes (CreativePro)

name: Pull to refresh
definition: Dragging a list downward past its top edge to trigger a reload, with a spinner that appears in the space the drag opens up.
useWhen: tugging a list down to fetch new items
notes: Credited to Loren Brichter's Tweetie; worth a history note in the article.

name: Push notification
definition: A system delivered message shown outside the app, on a lock screen or in a notification list, that has to earn the interruption it costs.
useWhen: something needs saying while the app is closed
notes: Distinct from toast, which lives inside the app and cannot interrupt anything. The consent prompt in front of it is why permission-priming exists.

name: Push transition
definition: A navigation transition where the new view slides in and pushes the old one off, and reversing it pops back, encoding depth in a stack.
useWhen: navigating deeper into a stack and back out

name: QR code
definition: A square matrix barcode rendered in the interface to hand a link or credential to a phone camera.
useWhen: handing a link to a phone by camera

name: Quasimode
definition: A temporary mode held open by the user, such as a key kept down, so it cannot be forgotten and ends the moment the hold ends.
useWhen: a mode that lasts only while you hold it
notes: Raskin's term. Explains why holding Space to pan is safer than a pan tool you can forget you are in.

name: Quick return header
definition: A header that slides out of the way while the reader scrolls down and returns immediately on the first upward scroll, without waiting for the top of the page.
useWhen: the bar hides going down and comes back the moment you scroll up

sources.title: Bram.us: hide a header when scrolling down, show it again when scrolling up

notes: iframe demo: the subject is the document scroller and a position:sticky header measured against it.

name: Quick settings tile
definition: A one tap button or toggle an app contributes to the system control surface, so one feature can be reached without opening the app.
useWhen: one app feature deserves a place in system controls

sources.title: Android: Create custom Quick Settings tiles

notes: Named after the Android term on purpose: Apple calls these Controls, which collides head on with the generic sense of control. Symbol, title and optional value is the whole anatomy.

name: Quick view
definition: Opening a summary of an item over the list it came from, so the reader can inspect it and return without losing scroll position or filters.
useWhen: peeking at an item without leaving the list
notes: hover-card already exists; quick view is the deliberate open, not the hover.

name: Radial menu
definition: A menu whose items sit around the point of invocation, so a choice is made by direction and distance rather than by reading a list.
useWhen: a menu chosen by direction from where you pressed
notes: Cross-category: a component, but it is an interaction technique first. Contrasts with the existing context-menu entry.

name: Rag
definition: The uneven edge left by unjustified text, and the thing typographers tune so that edge makes no distracting shapes down the side of a paragraph.
useWhen: critiquing the uneven edge of a paragraph

name: Rage click
definition: A burst of repeated clicks on one spot, the shape frustration takes when a control answers nothing, and the analytics signal that goes looking for it.
useWhen: the repeated clicking that reports a dead control
notes: Digital-experience-analytics vocabulary (Fullstory, Hotjar, Microsoft Clarity, Pendo). Vendors commonly say three or more clicks in a short window, but Fullstory publishes no threshold, so do NOT state a number as universal. DISCRIMINATION: ghost-click and dead-zone are CAUSES, this is the observed behaviour, and the article must say which is which.

name: Raised cap
definition: An oversized opening letter that sits on the first line's baseline and rises above the text, rather than sinking into it.
useWhen: the big opening letter rises instead of sinking
notes: relatedSlugs mentions initial-letter, which is currently an alias of drop-cap rather than a term; resolve in canonicalize.

name: RAM technique
definition: A grid that decides its own column count from a minimum item width, so the same one line rule works at every screen size without a single breakpoint.
useWhen: a grid that reflows with no breakpoints at all

sources.title: RAM (Repeat, Auto, Minmax), web.dev layout patterns

notes: auto-fit collapses empty tracks, auto-fill keeps them: that difference is the whole demo, and it is the one thing people get wrong.

name: Range select
definition: Choosing a contiguous run of items by marking one end and holding Shift while marking the other, selecting everything between them.
useWhen: selecting everything between two items at once

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

name: Range slider
definition: A slider with two handles on one track that sets a lower and an upper bound, so the selection is an interval rather than a point.
useWhen: the reader picks a from and a to on one track

name: Rating prompt
definition: An in-product request to rate or review, usually timed to a moment of success and often filtered so only positive responses reach the public store.
useWhen: the app asks how you like it right after something went well
notes: Review gating (routing unhappy answers to private feedback) is against both app store policies, worth saying in the article.

name: Reaction picker
definition: A small row of emoji that appears on hover or long press so a message can be answered without a reply.
useWhen: answering a message with one emoji

name: Read aloud
definition: Speaking page text with synthetic voice for readers who are not blind, with word highlighting as it goes, which is a reading aid rather than a screen reader.
useWhen: distinguishing text to speech from a screen reader

sources.title: Microsoft Support: Use Immersive Reader in Microsoft Edge

name: Read receipt
definition: A per-message marker reporting how far a message got, sent, delivered, or read, drawn as ticks, labels, or the recipient's avatar.
useWhen: the ticks that say sent, delivered, and read
notes: The double tick and its colour are conventions with no standard, so the term is understood but the drawing is not.

name: Readability
definition: How comfortably a body of text can be read at length, a property of the setting: size, measure, leading, and contrast.
useWhen: judging the setting, not the typeface
notes: Legibility and readability are the classic mixed-up pair; they should contrastWith each other.

name: Reader mode
definition: A browser view that throws away your layout and rebuilds the article as plain text the reader can restyle, which is a verdict on how readable the original was.
useWhen: checking what survives when the design is stripped

sources.title: Microsoft Support: Use Immersive Reader and reading mode in Microsoft Edge

notes: Depends entirely on semantic markup, so the demo can show a page that reader mode empties.

name: Reading flow
definition: A CSS property that repoints reading and tab order at the visual arrangement of a flex or grid container, instead of leaving both stuck in source order.
useWhen: a visual reorder has left tab order zigzagging
notes: Experimental and Chromium-only as of this sweep, which makes it a good tail term rather than guidance.

name: Reading order
definition: The order content is exposed in the DOM, which drives both speech output and tab order, and which visual reordering can silently contradict.
useWhen: the visual order and the source order disagree

name: Reading progress
definition: A bar tied to scroll position that shows how much of an article remains, usually pinned to the top edge and filling as the reader descends.
useWhen: the thin bar showing how far through the article you are
notes: iframe demo: the subject is scroll-driven animation over the document scroller. scroll-spy already exists and should carry a contrastWith edge.

name: Reduced transparency
definition: A user preference asking for opaque surfaces instead of blur and translucency, honoured by swapping frosted layers for solid fills.
useWhen: frosted panels have to become solid on request

sources.title: MDN: Using media queries for accessibility

notes: Direct counterpart to the existing glassmorphism entry: the preference that turns the frost off.

name: Redundant entry
definition: The rule against asking for the same information twice in one process, unless it is re-entered for a real reason such as confirmation.
useWhen: a wizard asks for the address a second time

name: Reflow
definition: The requirement that content works in one column at 320 CSS pixels wide without two dimensional scrolling, which is 400 percent zoom on a desktop.
useWhen: checking a layout at heavy zoom, not just on phones
notes: iframe: the subject is the document viewport and its scroller, which a shadow root cannot stand in for.

name: Relative color syntax
definition: CSS notation that builds a new colour from an existing one by naming an origin colour with from and then adjusting individual channels.
useWhen: deriving a colour by editing one channel of another

name: Relative luminance
definition: The brightness of a colour measured on a 0 to 1 scale after each channel is linearised, which is the input every WCAG contrast calculation actually uses.
useWhen: explaining why two colours of equal saturation contrast differently
notes: Tail. The reason yellow and blue at the same HSL lightness score wildly different contrast.

name: Relative timestamp
definition: A time printed as a distance from now, two hours ago or in three days, updating itself and holding the exact time in its tooltip.
useWhen: printing a time as how long ago it was
notes: Intl.RelativeTimeFormat is the platform answer and deserves an MDN row after a probe. The Mantine row is a weak match and should probably be dropped.

name: Required field indicator
definition: How a form says a field cannot be left empty, in the label text, in the announced name, and not by an asterisk whose meaning is explained somewhere else.
useWhen: deciding how to mark required versus optional fields

name: Resize handle
definition: The small corner grip that lets you drag an element or window bigger and smaller, drawn as diagonal ridges on a textarea or window corner.
useWhen: the corner grip that resizes a box
notes: Windows accessibility calls it size grip, which is the most precise name anyone uses. The MDN row needs a probe for the resize property page.

name: Resize text
definition: Text must scale to at least 200 percent without loss of content or function, which rules out fixed pixel heights around wrapping copy.
useWhen: the reader has enlarged text, not the whole page

aliases.name: text-only zoom vs full page zoom

name: Responsive upscaling
definition: Designing what a layout does with the space it gains on very wide screens, rather than only what it drops as screens narrow.
useWhen: the layout has more room than it knows what to do with

sources.title: Responsive Upscaling: 11 Ideas for Large-Screen E-Commerce Design, Baymard

notes: A Baymard coinage, so canonicalize should judge whether it has escaped one vendor. It names the neglected half of responsive design: everything above the widest breakpoint.

name: Responsive web design
definition: One layout that adapts to any screen through fluid grids, flexible images and media queries, rather than a separate site built for each class of device.
useWhen: the umbrella term for one adapting layout

sources.title: Responsive Web Design, A List Apart

notes: Ethan Marcotte, 2010, named three ingredients: fluid grids, flexible images, media queries. Round one captured the parts but not the umbrella word. Contrast with adaptive-layout, which swaps whole layouts at fixed sizes.

name: Retro film aesthetic
definition: A treatment that makes digital imagery look shot on film, adding grain, halation, light leaks, faded contrast, dust, and sometimes a corner date stamp.
useWhen: photography faked to look developed rather than rendered

sources.title: Wix: The biggest web design trends of 2026 (vintage photography and texture)

notes: Overlaps grainy-gradient, which covers noise over a flat fill; this record is the photographic treatment. Merge candidate.

name: Retro-futurism
definition: A style that pictures the future the way an earlier decade pictured it, so the technology on screen is advanced but the type, color, and hardware belong to the past.
useWhen: a future imagined by an older decade, not by this one
notes: Umbrella term; its dated subgenres (raygun gothic, atompunk, space age, cassette futurism, Y2K futurism) are separate names, not synonyms.

name: Retro web design
definition: A style that rebuilds the early desktop web on purpose: beveled window chrome, pixel and system type, garish color, and animated banners.
useWhen: the page imitates a 90s desktop or an early website

sources.title: Superdesign: Retro Web Design: CSS Recipe, Live Examples and Trend Data
Setproduct: Retro and brutalist UI design, a 2026 field guide

notes: 98.css recreates Windows 98; system.css recreates Apple System 6 (1984 to 1991).

name: Reveal animation
definition: Motion that uncovers content already in place, usually by growing a clip or mask outward from a point rather than moving the content itself.
useWhen: content should be uncovered rather than moved in

name: Review cursor
definition: A second cursor a screen reader user can move over the screen to read text without moving the system focus, so inspecting a region does not disturb the app.
useWhen: a reader inspects content without leaving the field

name: Ribbon
definition: A tall tabbed toolbar that replaces menus, grouping commands into labelled sections with the important ones drawn larger.
useWhen: the tall tabbed command strip in Office style apps
notes: Microsoft's 2007 answer to menu overload, and still the reference for command dense desktop apps.

name: Rich text editor
definition: An editing surface that shows formatting as it will appear rather than as markup, so what the writer sees is close to what readers get.
useWhen: authors need formatting without learning a markup language

sources.title: The Component Gallery: Rich text editor

notes: The editor itself, as opposed to rich-text-toolbar (the controls) and bubble-toolbar (the selection popover), both of which already exist and should relate up to this one.

name: Rich text toolbar
definition: The strip of formatting controls above or beside an editor, whose buttons report their state from wherever the caret sits.
useWhen: the formatting strip over a text editor
notes: Merge candidate with toolbar. Keep separate only if the article is really about pressed state reflecting the selection.

name: Ripple
definition: A circular wash that spreads from the point of contact to acknowledge a touch, Material's way of tying feedback to where the finger landed.
useWhen: touch feedback that spreads from the contact point
notes: Cross-category: filed as motion. State layer is Material's current term and may deserve a separate colour entry.

name: Risograph style
definition: A print-inspired look of two or three flat spot colors that misregister slightly and show grain, imitating a riso duplicator.
useWhen: flat spot colors that overprint and slip out of register
notes: No authoritative UI-side source found this sweep; the term is well established in illustration and increasingly used for web backgrounds. Verify before promoting past stub.

name: River
definition: An accidental channel of white space running down a paragraph where word spaces on consecutive lines happen to line up.
useWhen: naming the white streak running down a paragraph

name: Roach motel
definition: Making entry into a commitment take one click and exit take a phone call, a chat queue, or a buried page, so the asymmetry keeps people subscribed.
useWhen: easy to sign up, deliberately hard to leave
notes: deceptive.design renamed it Hard to cancel; roach motel remains the searched term, which is exactly the kind of gap this site should close.

name: Role description
definition: An author supplied name for a widget's role, spoken in place of the stock role name, which overrides the platform wording and misleads easily.
useWhen: renaming what a widget calls itself out loud

name: Rotate gesture
definition: Two fingers turning around a common center to rotate the object or view beneath them, the angle tracking the fingers as they orbit.
useWhen: turning content with two fingers rather than a handle

name: Rotor
definition: VoiceOver's dial for choosing what a swipe or flick moves between: headings, links, landmarks, form controls, or characters.
useWhen: naming the VoiceOver dial that picks a navigation unit

sources.title: Apple Support: Use the VoiceOver rotor on Mac

name: Route announcement
definition: Telling assistive technology that a client side navigation happened, by moving focus to the new heading or posting the new title to a live region.
useWhen: the URL changed but the page never reloaded

sources.title: Dave Rupert: Accessible page navigation in single page apps

notes: iframe: the subject is the document title and the document's focus, so it needs its own document.

name: Roving tabindex
definition: A focus technique where only one item in a group is in the tab order and arrow keys move that position, so Tab enters and leaves the whole group once.
useWhen: a group of controls that Tab treats as one stop

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

notes: Cross-category candidate with accessibility; the accessibility sweep may also propose it. aria-activedescendant is the sibling technique and could be its own tail entry.

name: RTL mirroring
definition: Flipping a layout horizontally for right to left languages, moving navigation and progression to the other side while leaving some elements unmirrored.
useWhen: shipping the same screen in Arabic or Hebrew
notes: The interesting content is what does not mirror: clocks, media playback controls, and numbers.

name: Ruby annotation
definition: Small guide text set beside or above a run of base text, most often to give the pronunciation of East Asian characters.
useWhen: annotating characters with their pronunciation

name: Rule builder
definition: Assembling a condition from dropdowns and values, joined by and or or, so a non-programmer can express a query without writing one.
useWhen: building an if-this-then-that condition from dropdowns

name: Rule of thirds
definition: Dividing a frame into nine equal cells with two lines each way and placing the important elements on the lines or their intersections.
useWhen: placing a focal point off centre on purpose

name: Runt
definition: A single word left alone on the last line of a paragraph or heading.
useWhen: naming the lone word on a heading's last line

sources.title: An end to typographic widows on the web (Clagnut)

notes: Casually called a widow by most web designers; strong disambiguation entry against widow and orphan.

name: Safe area
definition: The part of the screen guaranteed clear of notches, system bars and rounded corners, where interactive content can safely sit.
useWhen: the region a control can occupy without being clipped

sources.title: Using safe-area-inset to build mobile-safe layouts, Polypane

name: Sans-serif
definition: A typeface drawn without finishing strokes on the ends of its stems, which is the default register of most interface type.
useWhen: naming type without finishing strokes
notes: Classification families (grotesque, neo-grotesque, humanist, geometric, slab) are a possible sub-cluster if the taxonomy wants them.

name: Saturation
definition: How far a colour is from grey on a scale where 100 percent is the pure hue and 0 percent is neutral, as modelled by HSL and its relatives.
useWhen: describing how vivid or washed out a colour looks
notes: Merge candidate with chroma; they are not the same measure and the distinction is worth a contrastWith edge.

name: Save for later
definition: Moving an item out of the active list into a parked list that stays associated with the reader, without deleting it or committing to it.
useWhen: parking an item without buying or discarding it

name: Scaffold
definition: The frame that positions an app's persistent regions, its bars, panes and body, so each screen drops content into named slots instead of inventing its own arrangement.
useWhen: the named slots a screen's parts drop into
notes: Overlaps app-shell: a scaffold is the slotted frame a toolkit hands you, an app shell is the part of a running app that never reloads. Flutter's Scaffold widget is the same word, unverified this sweep.

name: Scanlines
definition: Thin repeating dark lines laid over an interface to imitate the raster of a cathode ray tube screen, often with a slight curve and flicker.
useWhen: the screen is dressed as an old CRT monitor
notes: Classic long-tail query: people search for the word for the lines over a retro screen.

name: Scarcity indicator
definition: A label reporting how little of something is left, in stock, in seats, or in time, placed beside the action it is meant to accelerate.
useWhen: only two left in stock, printed next to the buy button
notes: Honest when the number is real; the fabricated version is recorded separately as fake-scarcity.

name: Scope bar
definition: The row of category buttons directly under a search field that narrows what the query searches, such as All, Mail, Files.
useWhen: buttons under a search box that limit its reach
notes: Apple vocabulary that never crossed to the web, though the thing itself is everywhere in search results pages.

name: Screen curtain
definition: A screen reader mode that switches the display off entirely while navigation keeps working, used for privacy and by sighted testers to check an audio-only run.
useWhen: testing whether a flow works with the screen dark

sources.title: Apple Support: Use Screen Curtain with VoiceOver

notes: Not renderable as a specimen; a candidate for a term with no demo, or a staged illustration.

name: Screen magnification
definition: Blowing part of the screen up many times over, so a reader sees a keyhole of the layout at a time and anything far from the action is effectively off screen.
useWhen: a toast at the corner will never be seen
notes: Explains why feedback belongs near the control that caused it rather than in a screen corner.

name: Screen reader
definition: Software that speaks or brailles the accessibility tree and supplies its own keyboard commands for moving through a page.
useWhen: naming the software that reads an interface aloud

name: Scrim
definition: A translucent or gradient layer laid over imagery or behind a dialog, dimming what is beneath so text on top clears contrast or so focus moves forward.
useWhen: darkening what is behind so the layer above stays readable
notes: Tail gold. Classic 'what is the word for the dark gradient behind the caption on a photo'.

name: Scroll anchoring
definition: Keeping the reader's position fixed when content loads or resizes above it, by adjusting scroll offset so the visible text does not jump.
useWhen: content loads above and the view must not jump
notes: MDN has a dedicated overflow-anchor page that was not fetched this sweep; verify before authoring.

name: Scroll chaining
definition: When an inner scroller reaches its end and the gesture continues, the scroll passes to the page behind it unless that handoff is blocked.
useWhen: an inner scroll spills over into the page behind

name: Scroll container
definition: The element that actually scrolls its overflowing content, distinct from the page, and the box the browser calls the scrollport.
useWhen: identifying which box is doing the scrolling
notes: Genuine tail gold: "scrollport" is the spec word almost nobody knows, and "which thing is scrolling" is a daily debugging question.

name: Scroll hijacking
definition: Overriding the browser's scrolling so a wheel turn advances a scripted sequence instead of moving the page by the distance the reader asked for.
useWhen: the page takes over what one scroll of the wheel does
notes: Almost always used pejoratively; contrast with scroll-snap, which constrains scrolling without stealing it.

name: Scroll-linked animation
definition: An animation whose progress is bound to scroll position rather than to time, so scrolling back rewinds it exactly.
useWhen: the reader's scroll should drive the animation frame by frame
notes: The precise contrast with scroll-triggered-animation is the reason both entries exist.

name: Scroll lock
definition: Freezing the page behind an open overlay so a wheel or swipe moves the overlay's own content and never the document underneath.
useWhen: the page must hold still while an overlay is open
notes: Subject is the document scroller, so this is a genuine iframe case. Pairs with modal-dialog, already on the site.

name: Scroll pinning
definition: Holding a section fixed in place while the page keeps scrolling, spending scroll distance on an animation instead of on movement.
useWhen: a section should hold still while its content advances
notes: Cross-category with layout (position: sticky); recorded here because the searched concept is the scroll-motion technique.

name: Scroll snap
definition: Snap positions declared on a scroll container so scrolling settles on a chosen item edge instead of stopping wherever momentum runs out.
useWhen: scrolling that must land on an item, not between two

name: Scroll-triggered animation
definition: An animation that scroll position only starts, after which it runs on its own clock and does not rewind when the reader scrolls back up.
useWhen: scrolling should start the motion, not steer it

sources.title: Chrome for Developers: CSS scroll-triggered animations are coming

notes: Usually built on IntersectionObserver, which is worth an alias but probably belongs to a different category's sweep.

name: Scrollbar
definition: The bar beside a scrollable region whose thumb shows both how much content there is and where in it you are.
useWhen: the bar that shows and sets scroll position
notes: color.json already holds scrollbar-color. The overlay vs classic distinction (does it take layout space) is the discrimination worth writing.

name: Scrollbar color
definition: The thumb and track colours of a scrollbar, which a page can set explicitly or leave to the declared colour scheme so the browser draws its own dark variant.
useWhen: matching the scrollbar to a dark or branded theme
notes: Marked iframe: the honest subject is the document scroller, though a scrolling sub-element demo could stay inline.

name: Scrollytelling
definition: A narrative layout where a pinned graphic stays fixed while text scrolls past it, each step changing what the graphic shows.
useWhen: one visual that changes as the story scrolls past
notes: Cross category: pattern or motion is arguably the better home. Recorded here because the mechanism is a sticky layout region.

name: Scrubber
definition: The seek control of a media player: a track showing elapsed and buffered time with a playhead you drag to move through it.
useWhen: the bar you drag to move through a video
notes: interaction.json already holds scrubbing as the gesture; this is the control it acts on.

name: Scrubbing
definition: Dragging a playhead along a timeline to move through media by hand, previewing frames as the position changes rather than waiting for playback.
useWhen: dragging through time to find a moment

name: Scrubby slider
definition: A numeric field whose label can be dragged sideways to change the value, giving a slider's feel without a slider taking up room.
useWhen: dragging a label to change the number beside it

sources.title: John Nack on Adobe: Scrubby sliders and more

notes: Strong tail term: people search for it as the Figma or Photoshop drag-the-label thing without knowing a name.

name: Secondary click
definition: The alternate pointer press, usually the right button or a two-finger tap, reserved for opening contextual actions rather than activating.
useWhen: the press that asks for options instead of acting
notes: context-menu already exists on the site; secondary click is the input that opens it, worth a seeAlso rather than a merge.

name: Seed color
