definition: The single input colour an algorithm expands into a whole scheme, so a palette becomes something derived from one decision rather than picked swatch by swatch.
useWhen: one colour in, a whole palette out

sources.title: Material 3: how the color system works

name: Select all across pages
definition: Offering to extend a selection from the visible page to every matching row, after a header checkbox has selected only what is on screen.
useWhen: select all offers to also take the rows you cannot see
notes: Gmail popularised the two-stage version; no design system seems to have a documented name for it.

name: Selection card
definition: A radio or checkbox dressed as a card, where the whole tile is the target and the control itself is small or absent.
useWhen: choosing between options drawn as big tiles

name: Selection color
definition: The highlight painted behind text a reader has selected, which a page can restyle and thereby break the contrast the operating system had guaranteed.
useWhen: styling the highlight behind selected text

name: Selection follows focus
definition: A widget where moving focus also selects, so arrowing through tabs or a listbox changes the selection immediately rather than on a second press.
useWhen: arrowing changes the choice, not just the highlight

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

notes: Contrast pair with the existing tabs entry, where automatic versus manual activation is the visible consequence.

name: Selection handle
definition: The draggable grip at each end of a touch text selection, used to widen or narrow the range a finger cannot adjust precisely.
useWhen: adjusting a touch selection by its endpoints

sources.title: iOS HIG: Gestures (touch and hold in text)

name: Semantic HTML
definition: Reaching for the element that already means what you mean, so name, role, keyboard behaviour, and platform conventions arrive for free instead of being rebuilt.
useWhen: choosing between a native element and a rebuilt one

name: Semantic zoom
definition: Switching between two views of the same content, a zoomed out view of group headings and a zoomed in view of individual items, instead of scaling pixels.
useWhen: zooming out to headings, not to smaller text
notes: A Windows 8 idea worth reviving as vocabulary: it names what a jump list, a year view in a calendar and a map's label thinning all do.

name: Sensory characteristics
definition: Instructions that lean on shape, size, position, or sound alone, such as the round button on the right, which fail when those cues are not perceived.
useWhen: copy points at a control by shape or position

name: Sentence case
definition: Capitalizing only the first word of a label or heading, plus any proper nouns, as you would in an ordinary sentence.
useWhen: Google-style UI copy and anything meant to be read

sources.title: Title case vs sentence case in UI

name: Sequential palette
definition: A data palette that runs light to dark in one direction, encoding an ordered quantity so that darker always means more.
useWhen: colour encoding an ordered quantity
notes: Data visualisation vocabulary; close cousin of the existing color-ramp entry but ordered by value, not by UI job.

name: Serif
definition: The small finishing stroke at the end of a letter's stem, and by extension the class of typefaces that have them.
useWhen: naming the little feet on the ends of strokes

name: Set size and position
definition: Telling assistive technology how big a list really is and where an item sits in it, so a windowed or paginated list still announces "item 6 of 16".
useWhen: only twenty rows of ten thousand are in the DOM

name: Shade
definition: A colour with black mixed in, darker than the original hue and typically used for pressed states, borders and dark theme surfaces.
useWhen: a darker version of a colour made by adding black
notes: Casual usage calls every ramp step a 'shade'; the entry should note the strict versus loose sense.

name: Shake
definition: A short lateral wobble used to reject an input, borrowed from the head shake and read as no rather than as an error message.
useWhen: an input is refused and should be felt, not just read

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

name: Shake to undo
definition: Physically shaking a device to trigger undo or redo, an accelerometer gesture Apple defines system wide for reversing a recent edit.
useWhen: undo triggered by motion rather than a control

name: Share sheet
definition: The system panel of destinations and actions for sending the current item elsewhere, populated by whatever apps are installed.
useWhen: the system panel for sending something onward
notes: Apple's formal name is activity view, which nobody says. The Web Share API brings the same sheet to the browser and deserves an implementation row after a probe.

name: Shared axis
definition: Material's transition where outgoing and incoming views slide and fade along the same x, y, or z axis, so direction encodes the navigational relationship.
useWhen: two views sit next to each other in a sequence or hierarchy

name: Sidebar
definition: A persistent vertical region alongside the main content holding navigation or secondary controls, often collapsible on narrow screens.
useWhen: navigation that lives beside the content, not above it
notes: Every Layout uses "Sidebar" for a narrower idea (a fixed width element beside a fluid one that wraps without a media query). Worth a disambiguation paragraph rather than a second record.

name: Sidenote
definition: A note placed in the outer margin beside the line it belongs to, rather than collected at the foot of the page.
useWhen: an aside that must stay level with its sentence
notes: relatedSlugs mentions pull-quote, which this sweep did not record; the typography sweep is the natural owner of that one.

name: Sign language interpretation
definition: A signed track alongside video, presented as an inset or a companion stream, for readers whose first language is a sign language rather than the written caption text.
useWhen: captions are not the reader first language

name: Signature pad
definition: A drawing area that captures a handwritten signature by pointer or touch, with a clear control and a baseline to sign on.
useWhen: capturing a handwritten signature
notes: Needs a keyboard alternative to be usable at all, which is the interesting half of the entry.

name: Signifier
definition: The visible cue that advertises an affordance, such as a grip texture, an underline, or a shadow that says this can be pressed.
useWhen: the cue that tells you an action is possible
notes: Norman's distinction: affordance is the possibility, signifier is the advertisement of it. Strong contrastWith pair.

name: Site footer
definition: The closing region of a site holding secondary navigation, legal links, and contact details that do not deserve top level placement.
useWhen: everything that must exist but must not compete

name: Situational disability
definition: A barrier that comes from the moment rather than the body, one arm holding a baby, sunlight on a screen, a noisy train, and that makes the audience for access everyone.
useWhen: widening who a barrier actually affects

name: 60-30-10 rule
definition: A proportion guideline that gives about 60 percent of a layout to a dominant colour, 30 percent to a secondary, and 10 percent to an accent.
useWhen: deciding how much of each colour to use, not which colours
notes: Tail gold: names the question 'how much of each colour', which no token system answers.

name: Skeuomorphism
definition: A style that makes interface elements imitate real objects and materials, using leather, metal, paper, and glossy highlights so their purpose reads as familiar.
useWhen: the control is dressed as the physical object it replaces

sources.title: NN/g: Flat Design: Its Origins, Its Problems, and Why Flat 2.0 Is Better for Users

notes: The reference pole for the whole category: half the other entries are defined against it.

name: Slash command
definition: Typing a forward slash in a composer to open a menu of actions, where choosing one runs it rather than inserting the words into the message.
useWhen: typing / in the message box opens a command menu

name: Slide to confirm
definition: A control that commits only once its thumb is dragged the length of its track, so the effort of the gesture is the guard against doing it by accident.
useWhen: making one irreversible action need a deliberate drag
notes: The completing sibling of hold-to-confirm and type-to-confirm, both published: link and contrast BOTH. MANDATORY honesty duty: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 requires a non-dragging alternative for this exact control, so the article must link the site's own dragging-alternative and the demo must not pretend the drag is the only way in.

name: Slide transition
definition: A transition where content translates in or out along one axis, using direction to say whether the user moved forward, back, up, or down.
useWhen: the change has a direction the reader should feel

name: Sliding indicator
definition: A single underline or pill that travels between tabs to mark the selection instead of each tab drawing its own, so the move itself says which way the selection went.
useWhen: selection should move between items rather than blink between them

sources.title: CSS-Tricks: creating an animated menu indicator with CSS selectors

notes: The motion half of the existing segmented-control and tabs site terms; the kit's <sp-segmented> already carries the state this would animate.

name: Small caps
definition: Capital letters drawn at roughly lowercase height, with weight adjusted to match, so an abbreviation does not shout inside running text.
useWhen: setting acronyms inside body text without shouting

name: Smart app banner
definition: A strip pinned to the top of a mobile web page urging the reader to open or install the native app instead, with an install or open action.
useWhen: the strip on a mobile site pushing you into the app
notes: The full-screen version is penalised by search engines as an intrusive interstitial, which is part of the term's story.

name: Smart defaults
definition: Prefilling a choice with the answer most people in this situation want, so the common case needs no work and every other case is still reachable.
useWhen: the form arrives already answered the way you would have

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Smart Defaults instead of asking to do extra work

name: Smart guides
definition: Alignment lines that appear only while dragging, showing which edges or centers the moving object currently lines up with.
useWhen: the guide lines that appear mid-drag
notes: Borderline layout, but the guides only exist during an interaction, so filed here.

name: Smart quotes
definition: The curved opening and closing quotation marks a typeface actually draws, as opposed to the straight vertical marks inherited from typewriters.
useWhen: your quotes look like typewriter ticks

sources.title: The Definitive Guide to Quotes, Apostrophes, and Primes

name: Smooth scrolling
definition: Animating a programmatic jump so the page travels to its destination instead of cutting there, which keeps an anchor link or a back-to-top button from losing the reader's place.
useWhen: a jump would leave the reader unsure where they landed
notes: demo: iframe because the subject is a document scroller, which is exactly the case SPEC allows the expensive isolation mode for. Do not confuse with the smoothed custom scrolling that earns the name scroll hijacking (recorded in interaction.json).

name: Snapping
definition: Pulling a dragged object into exact alignment once it comes within a small distance of a grid, guide, or another object's edge.
useWhen: a drag jumps into alignment near a guide

name: Sneak into basket
definition: Adding an item the buyer never chose, an insurance, a donation, a warranty, into the cart through a preselected control found earlier in the flow.
useWhen: something you never picked is in your basket

name: Social login
definition: Signing in by delegating identity to an existing account elsewhere, presented as a row of provider buttons above or instead of a password form.
useWhen: the row of continue with Google and Apple buttons
notes: The NASCAR problem (too many provider buttons) is the usual reason people search for this term.

name: Social proof
definition: Showing what other people did or said next to a decision, as counts, reviews, logos, or live activity, so the reader can borrow their judgement.
useWhen: the interface shows what others chose to steady your choice

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Social Proof instead of talking about yourself

name: Soft delete
definition: Removing an item from view but keeping it recoverable in a trash or archive for a period, so deletion is reversible without a confirmation step.
useWhen: deleted things go to a bin you can dig them out of

name: Soft hyphen
definition: An invisible character placed inside a word that marks where a hyphen may appear if the word has to break, and stays hidden otherwise.
useWhen: telling the browser where a long word may break

name: Solarpunk
definition: An optimistic ecological future style of daylight palettes, plant growth over structure, stained glass color, art nouveau curves, and visible solar and wind technology.
useWhen: a hopeful green future rather than a dystopian one
notes: Defined against cyberpunk on purpose: same technology, opposite politics and palette.

name: Sonification
definition: Turning data into sound, mapping a series to pitch or rhythm, so a chart can be heard as a shape rather than described one value at a time.
useWhen: a chart has to be perceivable without sight

sources.title: University of Washington: Making data visualizations accessible

name: Sort state
definition: The announced direction of the one column a table is currently sorted by, carried on that column header alone rather than on every sortable header.
useWhen: a sorted column shows an arrow but says nothing

name: Spacer
definition: A deliberate empty element between regions: the gap between two panes that carries the drag handle when they resize, or the flexible filler that pushes toolbar items apart.
useWhen: the empty element that does the spacing
notes: Two senses worth naming: Material 3's gap between panes, and the flexible spacer element in toolbars, SwiftUI stacks and Figma auto layout.

name: Spacing scale
definition: The fixed, named set of spacing values a system allows, so gaps come from a shortlist instead of being invented per screen.
useWhen: why the gap is 12 and not 13

name: Spanned layout
definition: How an app arranges itself when one window is stretched across two displays, either keeping content clear of the seam or splitting the layout exactly at it.
useWhen: one app stretched across two screens

sources.title: Surface Duo device modes, Microsoft Learn

notes: Sibling of device-posture, which round one captured: posture is the shape of the hinge, spanning is what the layout does about it. The web version is the viewport segments API.

name: Sparkline
definition: A tiny chart with no axes or labels, drawn inline at text size to show the shape of a trend beside the number it belongs to.
useWhen: a trend line small enough to sit inline
notes: Coined by Edward Tufte, which gives the article a genuine provenance to cite.

name: Spatial navigation
definition: Moving focus by direction rather than by sequence, so arrow keys, a D-pad, or a TV remote jump to the nearest control up, down, left, or right.
useWhen: the input is a remote or a game pad, not a keyboard

name: Spatial UI
definition: Interface designed to sit in three dimensional space, where panels use a system glass material and depth rather than color carries hierarchy.
useWhen: the interface floats in the room, not on a screen

sources.title: WWDC23: Design for spatial user interfaces
Create with Swift: Ensuring interface legibility and contrast in visionOS

notes: Marked demo: none because a flat specimen cannot honestly show a spatial subject. Reconsider if a parallax mock is judged fair.

name: Specular highlight
definition: The bright reflection drawn on a surface to say it is glossy, placed where a light source would strike a curved object.
useWhen: the bright spot that makes a surface read as shiny
notes: Deep tail: the word for the small bright arc, distinct from the whole gloss treatment. Apple's Liquid Glass documentation uses the term for its edge reflections.

name: Speed dial
definition: A floating action button that fans out into three to six smaller related actions when pressed or hovered.
useWhen: one prominent button that unfolds into a few actions
notes: MUI kept the name after Material 2 dropped it, so the word now lives mostly in React vocabulary.

name: Split-flap animation
definition: A digit or letter changing by flipping through the characters between the old value and the new one, imitating the mechanical boards of airports and flip clocks.
useWhen: a changing value should read as mechanical rather than digital

sources.title: Design engineering: a split-flap display component

notes: Distinct from count-up: the value does not interpolate, it steps through every character in between, which is why it pairs with stepped-animation.

name: Split screen layout
definition: A page cut into two equal full height halves, each carrying its own message or path, with no hierarchy between them.
useWhen: two equally weighted choices on one page
notes: Distinct from split-view: this is a marketing composition, not a selection driven pane pair. Contrast pair worth keeping.

name: Split view
definition: A layout of two or more side by side panes where a choice in the leading pane decides what the trailing pane shows.
useWhen: two panes where one drives the other
notes: Merge candidate with list-detail. Keep separate: split view is the container mechanism (resizable panes, collapse behaviour), list-detail is the content relationship.

name: Splitter
definition: The draggable bar between two panes that changes how much room each one gets, keyboard operable as a slider between limits.
useWhen: the draggable bar between two resizable panes
notes: The APG keyboard model (arrow keys resize, Enter collapses) is the part nobody implements and the reason this entry earns its place.

name: Spotlight hover
definition: A soft radial glow centred on the pointer's position inside a card, lighting its surface and border as the cursor moves and going dark when the cursor leaves.
useWhen: a card should light up under the pointer rather than change colour

sources.title: Frontend Masters: how to build a glowing hover effect that follows the pointer
Cruip: how to create a spotlight card hover effect with Tailwind CSS

notes: Mechanically a pair of CSS custom properties updated on pointermove, which is why it is motion rather than colour: nothing is restyled, a gradient is repositioned.

name: Spotted pattern
definition: A scanning shape where the eye jumps to isolated words scattered down the page, hunting a keyword, a link or a number rather than reading anything.
useWhen: predicting a keyword hunt rather than reading

sources.title: Text Scanning Patterns: Eyetracking Evidence, NN/g

notes: The scanning pattern that justifies bolding keywords and formatting numerals distinctly.

name: Spring animation
definition: Motion driven by a simulated spring (mass, stiffness, damping) instead of a fixed duration, so the element settles rather than stopping on a schedule.
useWhen: motion should react to how it was interrupted, not a timer

sources.title: Spring Animations in Pure CSS with linear()
Chrome for Developers: the linear() easing function

notes: Head-adjacent but the searched word is usually 'spring animation'. Stiffness, damping ratio and mass are sub-vocabulary; damping is recorded separately, stiffness folded in here.

name: Spring loading
definition: Hovering a dragged item over a container until it opens, so a drag can travel through nested destinations without being dropped and restarted.
useWhen: a drag opens what it hovers so it can go deeper

sources.title: MacPaw: What is spring loading on Mac

name: Squash and stretch
definition: Deforming an element along its direction of travel so it reads as having mass and flexibility, usually as a press squash or a launch stretch.
useWhen: a control should feel physical when pressed or launched

sources.title: IxDF: UI Animation, applying Disney's 12 principles to UI

name: Squircle
definition: A rounded square whose corners curve continuously into the sides instead of meeting a circular arc, the shape behind iOS app icons.
useWhen: corners that blend in rather than snap to an arc
notes: Tail gold and highly searched. CSS corner-shape: squircle was landing in browsers around 2025; verify support and the exact property name before authoring.

name: sRGB
definition: The default colour space of the web, the one hex codes and plain rgb() values live in, and the baseline every wider gamut is described relative to.
useWhen: the assumed colour space behind a hex code

name: Stack
definition: A layout primitive that puts one consistent gap between every child in a vertical run, so spacing lives with the parent instead of each item.
useWhen: one rule for the space between everything vertical

name: Stacking cards
definition: A run of sections that each stick at the top of the viewport as the next one slides over it, so scrolling deals the page like a deck rather than passing it by.
useWhen: sequential sections should pile up instead of scrolling away

sources.title: CSS-Tricks: stacked cards with sticky positioning

notes: demo: iframe because the subject is the document scroller and a run of sticky sections needs the page's own scroll, not a nested one.

name: Stacking context
definition: A self contained depth ordering created by certain properties, inside which z-index only competes locally and can never escape to the level above.
useWhen: why a huge z-index still sits behind something

sources.title: CSS Flexible Box Layout Module Level 1

notes: The z-index: 9999 that does nothing is one of the most searched layout problems there is, and this is the word that explains it.

name: Stat
definition: A single number shown large with a label and often a change indicator, the unit a dashboard is built from.
useWhen: one number shown big with its label

name: State layer
definition: A translucent sheet of the content colour laid over a control at a fixed opacity per state, so hover, focus and pressed are one rule instead of three palettes.
useWhen: one overlay opacity expressing hover, focus and pressed
notes: Tail gold and very demoable: one swatch, four states, opacity readout.

name: Static color
definition: A colour deliberately excluded from theming because it sits on something that never changes, such as a label over a photo or a fixed brand mark.
useWhen: a colour that must not flip with the theme
notes: Material has the parallel idea in its fixed colour roles (primary fixed, on primary fixed).

name: Status bar
definition: A thin strip along the edge of a window or screen that reports state and offers only minor actions, never the primary ones.
useWhen: an edge strip that reports rather than commands
notes: Two senses: the OS status bar on phones (clock, battery) and the app status bar in desktop tools. Both belong in one entry.

name: Status color
definition: The small fixed set of colours a product reserves for outcome, typically success, warning, danger and info, so meaning is consistent wherever it appears.
useWhen: colours that report an outcome rather than a brand
notes: Merge candidate with the existing semantic-color stub; status colour is the narrower, outcome-only sense.

name: Status message
definition: A change in content that reports progress, result, or state and must be announced without taking focus, such as a count of search results.
useWhen: reporting an outcome the reader did not navigate to

name: Steampunk
definition: A Victorian industrial style of brass, riveted plate, wood, and leather, with gauges, cogs, and valve controls standing in for ordinary interface widgets.
useWhen: brass gauges and cogs instead of plain controls

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions
My Steampunk Style: What is retro-futurism?

notes: The clearest surviving case of full skeuomorphism in themes and games; dieselpunk is folded in as an alias but is a later decade.

name: Stepped animation
definition: Motion that jumps between a fixed number of discrete positions instead of interpolating, the mechanic behind sprite sheets, ticking clock hands and segmented spinners.
useWhen: the movement should tick rather than glide
notes: The counterexample that makes easing legible: an animation with no in-betweens at all.

name: Steps left
definition: Telling the reader where they are in a multi-step task and how many steps are still to come, so the end of the task is visible from the start.
useWhen: the flow says step 2 of 5

name: Sticky add to cart
definition: A condensed product bar that pins itself to an edge once the real buy button has scrolled away, keeping price and purchase always reachable.
useWhen: the buy bar that sticks once the real button scrolls off
notes: iframe demo: it is defined by its relationship to the document scroller.

name: Sticky footer
definition: A footer held against the bottom of the viewport when the page is short, and pushed below the content when the page is long.
useWhen: a footer that will not float in the middle of a short page
notes: Commonly confused with a fixed footer that always overlays the page. The distinction is the whole entry.

name: Sticky header
definition: A header that scrolls away with the page until it reaches the top edge, then stays fixed there while the rest keeps moving.
useWhen: a header that pins itself once it hits the top

implementations.name: position: sticky and the stuck state

notes: The "stuck" state now has a CSS query for it (scroll-state), which makes a nice demo beat.

name: Sticky hover
definition: A hover style that stays applied on a touch device after a tap, because there is no pointer to leave and clear the state.
useWhen: a tapped control stays looking hovered

name: Sticky sidebar
definition: A side column that scrolls with the page and then holds in place once its top reaches the viewport edge, releasing at the end of its container.
useWhen: a side column that follows you down a long article

name: Stories
definition: A sequence of full-screen cards that advance on a timer, paused by holding, skipped by tapping the edges, and gone after a fixed lifetime.
useWhen: the timed full-screen cards you tap through
notes: The segmented progress bar along the top is a component-level term of its own and may deserve a separate entry.

name: Streak
definition: A count of consecutive periods in which the reader did the thing, displayed prominently and lost if a period is missed.
useWhen: the running count of consecutive days you kept going
notes: Loss aversion made visible; the streak freeze is the mitigation and is itself a named sub-pattern.

name: Streaming announcement
definition: How a screen reader is told about text that arrives token by token, holding the region quiet while it streams and speaking once when the answer is complete.
useWhen: a reply types itself in and floods the announcer

sources.title: Harvard User Research Center: Review of generative AI chatbots accessibility

notes: Emerging vocabulary, and one of the few places where aria-busy earns its keep.

name: Strikethrough
definition: A rule drawn through the middle of text to mark it as removed, superseded, or no longer the current price.
useWhen: showing text that no longer applies

name: Structured format
definition: Splitting one value across several small fields with fixed shapes, which teaches the expected format but costs the reader extra focus moves.
useWhen: one value split across several little boxes
notes: Alias "segmented input" ceded to published pin-input 2026-08-20 (the OTP boxes are what that lookup means); this record keeps the split-field pattern sense.

name: Stylistic set
definition: A numbered bundle of alternate glyphs inside a font, switched on as a group to change the look of certain letters.
useWhen: switching a font's single-storey a on

sources.title: Syntax for OpenType features in CSS (Adobe Fonts)
A Practical Guide to Alternate Characters (Pangram Pangram)

name: Subgrid
definition: A nested grid that borrows its parent's tracks instead of defining its own, so contents of separate children still line up with each other.
useWhen: card internals that must align across sibling cards
notes: Best demo on the site's list: three cards with different length titles, aligned buttons with and without subgrid.

name: Submenu
definition: A menu that opens sideways from a menu item, marked by a trailing arrow, and stays open while the pointer travels diagonally toward it.
useWhen: a menu that opens out of another menu
notes: The diagonal safe triangle is the detail worth demonstrating and it is already close to interaction.json's hover-intent.

name: Superfamily
definition: A type system whose serif, sans, and sometimes mono members share one skeleton, so they pair by construction rather than by taste.
useWhen: picking two typefaces that are guaranteed to agree

name: Superscript
definition: Small raised characters used for footnote markers, ordinals, and exponents, ideally drawn by the font rather than shrunk by software.
useWhen: footnote markers, ordinals, and exponents

name: Supporting pane
definition: A secondary pane holding content that only makes sense next to the main pane, placed beside it on wide windows and below it on narrow ones.
useWhen: helper content that cannot stand on its own

name: Surface color
definition: The colour of a plane that content sits on, defined as a set of stacked levels so a card on a page and a sheet on a card are told apart by value.
useWhen: naming the plane content sits on, not the page background

name: Surface tint
definition: A wash of the primary colour blended into a surface in proportion to its elevation, so height reads as a colour shift rather than only as a shadow.
useWhen: elevation shown by tinting a surface rather than by shadow

name: Swash
definition: A letter drawn with an ornamental flourish, usually an extended entry or exit stroke on an italic capital.
useWhen: naming the decorative tail on a fancy capital

name: Swatch
definition: A small block of flat colour shown as a sample, used in pickers and documentation to stand in for a value the reader cannot otherwise see.
useWhen: a small block standing in for a colour value

name: Swipe
definition: A quick directional drag of a finger across the screen, faster and coarser than a drag, usually without a specific on-screen target.
useWhen: a fast directional stroke, not a controlled drag

name: Swipe actions
definition: Buttons hidden behind a list row that a partial sideways swipe reveals, so destructive or common actions live under the item itself.
useWhen: actions parked behind a row until it is swiped

sources.title: LogRocket: Designing swipe-to-delete and swipe-to-reveal interactions

name: Swipe deck
definition: A stack of cards judged one at a time, each thrown left or right to record a binary decision and reveal the next card underneath.
useWhen: a stack of cards you swipe left or right to judge
notes: No design system documents it; the vernacular name is the product that popularised it.

name: Swipe to dismiss
definition: Flinging an item off the edge of the screen to remove it, with the item tracking the finger and snapping back if the throw is too short.
useWhen: throwing a card or notification off the screen to clear it

sources.title: NN/g: Using Swipe to Trigger Contextual Actions

name: Swiss style
definition: The Swiss modernist system of a strict grid, flush left sans serif type, asymmetric layout, and objective photography, still the base of clean UI layout.
useWhen: grid, Helvetica, and nothing decorative
notes: Ancestor of the 12-column grid and of most design system layout thinking.

name: Switch access
definition: Operating a device with one or two switches, where a scanning cursor steps through targets in turn and a press selects the highlighted one.
useWhen: input is a single button and time, not a pointer

name: Switcher
definition: A layout primitive that flips between a row and a column at a threshold it works out from its own width, with no media query involved.
useWhen: side by side until it does not fit, then stacked

name: Symbol support
definition: Marking a control with a concept code so a reader who uses an augmentative symbol set sees their own familiar picture in place of your icon and wording.
useWhen: the words and icons themselves are the barrier
notes: Cognitive accessibility vocabulary, still a draft spec, but the only name for the idea.

name: Synthwave
definition: A neon 1980s look built on sunset gradients, glowing perspective grids, and chrome type, close to vaporwave but sincere rather than ironic.
useWhen: neon grid and sunset 80s futurism, played straight

sources.title: Digital Heroes: Vaporwave Retro Brand Design 2026

notes: Merge candidate with vaporwave if the taxonomy wants one entry; the irony versus sincerity split is the only real discriminator.

name: System color keyword
definition: A CSS keyword such as Canvas, CanvasText or LinkText that resolves to a colour chosen by the operating system rather than by the page.
useWhen: styling with the colours the OS itself picked

sources.title: Windows High Contrast Mode and CSS custom properties

name: System font
definition: The typeface the operating system uses for its own interface, requested by keyword so each platform supplies its native face.
useWhen: you want the app to look native and load nothing

name: Tab stop
definition: One position in the tab sequence: a place the Tab key can reach, counted once even when the widget it belongs to holds many focusable parts.
useWhen: counting how many Tab presses a widget costs

name: Tabbable
definition: Reachable by the Tab key, as opposed to merely focusable: an element with tabindex of -1 can take focus from script but never from Tab.
useWhen: distinguishing script focus from Tab reachability

sources.title: Eric Eggert: Two different kinds of focusable UI elements

notes: Tail gold: the distinction people reach for and cannot name. Headword could also be 'Focusable but not tabbable'.

name: Header association
definition: The markup that ties a data cell to its row and column headers, so a cell read on its own still says what it is.
useWhen: a table cell must announce which column it is in

name: Tabular figures
definition: Numerals drawn to identical widths so digits stack into columns, and so a changing number does not shift the text around it.
useWhen: numbers in a table, a timer, or a live counter

sources.title: OpenType at Work: Figure Styles (Type Network)

notes: Proportional figures are the contrasting setting; worth an alias row or its own stub.

name: Tag input
definition: A field that turns each entry into a removable tag sitting inside the field, with the caret waiting after the last one.
useWhen: a reader types an open ended set of short values
notes: Blueprint composes this with a dropdown to make MultiSelect, which is the right way round: the tag field is the primitive. Backspace deleting the last tag is the behaviour readers come looking for.

name: Tap
definition: A single press and lift of one finger on a touch surface, the touch equivalent of a click, used to activate a control or select an item.
useWhen: the touch gesture that activates something
notes: Material calls the mechanic touch and the outcome activate; Apple calls it tap.

name: Tap delay
definition: The pause a touch browser once held before dispatching a click, kept open in case a second tap arrived and turned the gesture into a zoom.
useWhen: naming the historic lag between tap and response

sources.title: Chrome for Developers: 300ms tap delay, gone away

name: Target spacing
definition: The exception that lets an undersized control pass when no other target falls inside a 24 pixel circle centred on it, trading size for clearance.
useWhen: small controls that cannot grow but can be separated

name: Tearsheet
definition: A tall modal anchored to the bottom of the viewport that holds a multi step creation flow, stackable when one flow opens another.
useWhen: a full height modal for a creation flow
notes: IBM-only vocabulary borrowed from print advertising. Worth recording precisely because it is the kind of word people meet once and cannot place.

name: Terminal aesthetic
definition: A look borrowed from the command line: monospace type on a fixed character grid, a block cursor, and green or amber text on black.
useWhen: the UI dressed as a command line

sources.title: Setproduct: Retro and brutalist UI design, a 2026 field guide

name: Terrazzo
definition: A background pattern of small irregular chips scattered on a plain field, copied from poured stone flooring and used flat and multicolored behind interface content.
useWhen: a speckled chip pattern used as a background fill

sources.title: Creative Market: Design Trend Report: Terrazzo

notes: Named in the memphis-design definition already; kept separate because it is used on its own as a pattern fill with no other Memphis cues.

name: Text balancing
definition: Choosing line breaks so a short block of text has lines of roughly equal length instead of a long first line and a stub second one.
useWhen: a two line heading breaks badly

sources.title: When to use text-wrap: balance vs pretty (LogRocket)

notes: balance and pretty solve different problems (even lines vs no stranded last word); canonicalize may want to split them.

name: Text box trim
definition: Cutting the leftover space above and below a line of text so the box hugs the cap height and baseline instead of the font's full ascent and descent.
useWhen: you want a label's box to match the letters, not the font
notes: Strong tail term; the property was renamed from leading-trim, so both spellings are live search queries.

name: Text columns
definition: Flowing one block of running text into several columns that fill and balance automatically, with an optional rule drawn between them.
useWhen: one passage of text split into columns
notes: Name collision to resolve in canonicalize: round one's multi-column-layout means side by side panes, this is one passage flowing into columns. Column boxes, column rules and spanning elements are the spec's words.

name: Text spacing
definition: The requirement that a reader can increase line height, letter spacing, word spacing, and paragraph spacing without any content being lost or clipped.
useWhen: proving a layout survives reader-set spacing
notes: CROSS-CATEGORY: filed under accessibility, surfaced by the typography sweep. Merge with the accessibility file's version if it enumerates one.

name: The fold
definition: The bottom edge of the first screenful, above which content is seen without any scrolling and below which it must be earned.
useWhen: arguing about what must be visible before a scroll
notes: Borrowed from newspapers. The interesting article is the disagreement: NN/g measures more attention above it, but there is no single fold across devices.

name: Throttle
definition: Capping how often a continuous stream of input is acted on, so a response fires at a steady rate instead of on every event.
useWhen: limiting how often a continuous input is answered
notes: Merge candidate with debounce; keep separate only if the article can hold the distinction clearly.

name: Thumb zone
definition: The arc of a phone screen a thumb reaches comfortably in a one handed grip, with harder to reach bands above and across from it.
useWhen: placing primary actions within easy reach on phones

sources.title: The Thumb Zone: Designing For Mobile Users, Smashing Magazine

notes: Coined by Steven Hoober from 2013 field observation. Could be filed under pattern or interaction; layout is where the decision actually gets made.

name: Thumbnail
definition: A small stand-in image for a larger one, cropped rather than letterboxed so a row of them lines up.
useWhen: a small preview image of a bigger one
notes: Collides with thumb the slider handle, which is worth one line of disambiguation.

name: Tick marks
definition: The small notches printed along a slider track that show the discrete stops the handle can land on.
useWhen: naming the notches printed along a slider
notes: Material 3 renamed these stop indicators in the expressive update, which is worth recording as a live naming change.

name: 3D tilt
definition: Rotating a card in perspective toward the pointer so it appears to tip in three dimensions, often with a moving highlight to sell the depth.
useWhen: a card should read as a physical object under the pointer
notes: Slug avoids 'tilt' because interaction.json uses that word for the device gesture. Perspective and transform-origin are folded in here rather than recorded as separate atoms.

name: Time picker
definition: A control for choosing a time of day, either as a dial you tap around or as hour and minute lists.
useWhen: choosing a clock time

name: Timeline
definition: A vertical or horizontal line of dated events, each pinned to the line by a marker and reading in order.
useWhen: events in order along a line
notes: Collides with the media editing sense of timeline (the track editor), which is worth disambiguating in the article.

name: Timeout warning
definition: A warning before a session or form expires with a simple way to extend it, so a slower reader does not lose their work silently.
useWhen: a session is about to expire under the reader
notes: Cross-category: could equally be a pattern entry.

name: Tint
definition: A colour with white mixed in, lighter than the original hue and used for faint fills, hover washes and subtle backgrounds.
useWhen: a lighter version of a colour made by adding white
notes: Apple overloads 'tint colour' to mean the app accent colour, which is a genuine naming dispute worth calling out.

name: Tinted neutral
definition: A grey with a trace of the brand hue mixed in, so backgrounds and borders belong to the palette instead of reading as a separate, colder system.
useWhen: greys that quietly carry the brand hue
notes: Tail gold: readers search 'why does my grey look dirty next to my blue'.

name: Tiny tweaks
definition: The lightest responsive pattern: a single column design that only adjusts type size, image size and margins as the screen changes.
useWhen: one column that only nudges type and margins
notes: The fifth of Luke Wroblewski's five multi-device layout patterns. Round one captured mostly fluid, column drop, layout shifter and off canvas but missed this one.

name: Title bar
definition: The strip along the top of a window carrying its title and window controls, and the region you drag to move the window.
useWhen: the draggable strip at the top of a window
notes: Relevant to the web again through the Window Controls Overlay API for installed web apps, which is worth a probe.

name: Title case
definition: Capitalizing the first letter of each significant word in a heading or label, leaving short articles and prepositions lowercase.
useWhen: Apple-style headings, buttons, and menu labels

name: Tittle
definition: The dot above a lowercase i or j.
useWhen: you need the word for the dot on an i

name: Tofu
definition: The empty rectangle a font renders when it has no glyph for a character, named for the block of bean curd it resembles.
useWhen: naming the empty box where a character should be

name: Toggle button
definition: A button that stays pressed, reporting an on or off state through aria-pressed rather than firing and returning.
useWhen: a button that stays down once you press it
notes: The bold button in a text toolbar is the canonical example. Contrast with switch, which changes a setting immediately and reads as on or off.

name: Top layer
definition: The layer above everything else in a document where fullscreen elements, modal dialogs and popovers render, escaping every ancestor's clipping and stacking order.
useWhen: explaining why a dialog is not trapped by overflow
notes: The answer to the oldest z-index bug: a dialog inside overflow: hidden. Each top layer element also gets its own ::backdrop.

name: Touch target
definition: The activatable area of a control, which needs a minimum size and spacing so a fingertip can hit it without catching its neighbours.
useWhen: sizing what the finger must hit, not what is drawn

sources.title: Smashing Magazine: Accessible target sizes cheatsheet

notes: Sits on the interaction and accessibility border; recorded here because the word is used about input, not about assistive tech.

name: Touch target size
definition: The minimum area a control must offer a finger or imprecise pointer, measured on the activation region rather than the painted glyph.
useWhen: sizing something for a fingertip, not a cursor

name: Track
definition: The groove a slider thumb or scrollbar travels along, usually drawn as filled before the handle and empty after it.
useWhen: naming the groove a handle slides in
notes: Old toolkits call it the trough (GTK, Tk), which is a nice piece of history for the article.

name: Transcript
definition: A full text version of time based media, readable without playing it and searchable by both people and machines.
useWhen: offering the whole of a video or podcast as text

sources.title: WebAIM: Captions, Transcripts, and Audio Descriptions

name: Transfer list
definition: Two side by side lists with arrow buttons between them, used to move items from available to chosen and back.
useWhen: picking a subset by moving items between two lists
notes: Enterprise vocabulary. Oracle and Salesforce ship it as pick list, PrimeReact as PickList, which is worth a probe later.

name: Tree select
definition: A select whose popup is a tree, so options can be chosen at any depth with parents collapsing over their children.
useWhen: picking from a tree inside a field

name: Tree grid
definition: A table whose rows nest and expand like a tree, so hierarchy and columns of data coexist in one grid.
useWhen: a table whose rows contain child rows

name: Tree view
definition: A nested list where branches expand and collapse in place, navigated with arrow keys as a single tab stop.
useWhen: nested items that expand in place
notes: AppKit calls it an outline view, which is worth a line in the article.

name: Triadic color scheme
definition: A palette of three hues spaced evenly around the colour wheel, vivid by construction and usually applied with one hue dominant.
useWhen: three hues balanced evenly around the wheel

name: Trick wording
definition: Phrasing a choice so its plain reading is the opposite of its effect, typically through double negatives or a label that describes the wrong outcome.
useWhen: untick this box to not stop receiving emails

name: True black theme
definition: A dark palette whose background is pure black rather than near black, which switches OLED pixels off entirely but makes elements look like they float in a void.
useWhen: a dark theme at pure black for OLED, not near black
notes: Tail. Names the argument about #000000 versus #121212 that every dark theme discussion reaches.

name: Truncation
definition: Cutting text that does not fit and marking the cut, usually with an ellipsis, so the reader knows something was removed.
useWhen: text has to fit a box it does not fit

name: Tween
definition: A single animation from one value to another over a duration, named for the in-between frames a computer fills in.
useWhen: naming one animation as a unit you can play or reverse

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: Contrasts with spring: a tween is bounded by a duration, a spring by its physics.

name: 12 column grid
definition: The web's default column count, chosen because twelve divides cleanly into halves, thirds, quarters and sixths.
useWhen: why almost every layout grid has twelve columns

name: Type scale
definition: The fixed set of text sizes a design allows, chosen so sizes relate to each other rather than being picked one at a time.
useWhen: deciding what sizes are allowed to exist at all

name: Type specimen
definition: A display of a typeface's characters, sizes, and styles made to show what the face can do rather than to communicate the text itself.
useWhen: showing off a typeface rather than using it

name: Type to confirm
definition: Guarding a destructive action by making the reader type the name of the thing being destroyed before the confirm button becomes usable.
useWhen: you must type the repo name to delete it
notes: GitHub popularised it; Cloudscape documents it as delete with text confirmation.

name: Typeahead
definition: Offering suggestions that update on every keystroke, drawn from a live query, so the reader picks a result rather than finishing the phrase.
useWhen: suggestions appear and change as you type
notes: combobox is already on the site as the component; typeahead is the behaviour, and the two need a disambiguation article.

name: Typeface
definition: The designed set of letterforms itself, as distinct from a font, which is one particular file or instance you actually use.
useWhen: distinguishing the design from the file

sources.title: Family, type family, or font family (Google Fonts Knowledge)

notes: Typeface vs font is the classic disambiguation entry; keep them as one term with the other as an alias.

name: Typewriter effect
definition: Revealing text one character at a time, as if it were being typed, usually with a blinking caret trailing the last letter.
useWhen: text should arrive as if being written right now

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

notes: Has picked up a second life as the way streamed model output is rendered, which is a useful contemporary note.

name: Typing indicator
definition: The three bouncing dots shown while someone is composing a reply, or while an assistant is preparing one.
useWhen: showing that a reply is being composed
notes: MUI draws a useful distinction: a typing indicator means a human is composing, a streaming indicator means a model is generating.

name: Typographic color
definition: The overall lightness or darkness a block of text produces when you stop reading it and look at it as a grey texture.
useWhen: judging a paragraph as texture rather than words
notes: Cross-category trap: the word color here has nothing to do with the color category. Worth a contrastWith into semantic-color.

name: Typographic hierarchy
definition: The ordering of text by visual weight so a reader can tell at a glance what is a title, what is body, and what is a caption.
useWhen: making importance readable without reading

implementations.name: Type roles: display, headline, title, body, label

name: Typography token
definition: A named bundle of type values (family, size, weight, line height, tracking) that a design system hands out instead of raw numbers.
useWhen: naming a text style so it can be reused and themed
notes: Sits at the border of typography and a future design-token cluster; merge candidate with any generic design-token entry.

name: Underline
definition: A rule drawn under text, on the web the default marker for a link, ideally set to skip the descenders it would otherwise cross.
useWhen: marking a link without relying on color alone

name: Undo
definition: Letting an action run immediately and offering to reverse it afterwards, instead of stopping to ask whether the reader really meant it.
useWhen: the action happens first and offers a way back

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Undos instead of prompting for confirmation

name: Universal navigation
definition: A slim bar that links a subsite back to its parent organisation's other sites, sitting above the subsite's own global navigation.
useWhen: connecting a subsite back to the parent org

sources.title: Universal Navigation: Connecting Subsites to Main Sites, NN/g

notes: Very common on university, government and large enterprise sites, and almost never named by the people building them.

name: Unsaved changes guard
definition: Warning the reader that edits will be lost before a navigation or close is allowed to proceed, and offering to save or discard first.
useWhen: leaving a form asks whether to discard your edits

name: Use of color
definition: The rule that colour must never be the only carrier of meaning, so a red field also needs an icon, wording, or shape change.
useWhen: the only difference between two states is hue

implementations.name: Use of color and color blindness

name: Utility bar
definition: A persistent bar docked to the bottom of an application holding small tools that open into panels without leaving the current page.
useWhen: tools docked along the bottom of the app
notes: Salesforce vocabulary. The chat windows docked along the bottom of Gmail and Facebook are the same idea under no name at all.

name: Utility navigation
definition: The strip of secondary tools and account actions, sign in, search, language, cart, kept apart from the links that describe the site's content.
useWhen: the small links above or beside the main nav

sources.title: Utility Navigation: What It Is and How to Design It, NN/g

notes: The utility bar record in the component sweep is the same word for the component; this record is the page region. Canonicalize should decide which keeps the name.

name: Vaporwave
definition: A retro internet look of magenta and cyan gradients, grid horizons, Japanese type, statuary, and 90s desktop chrome used ironically.
useWhen: 90s mall and desktop imagery reused with irony

sources.title: Shutterstock: What Is the Vaporwave Aesthetic

name: Variable font
definition: One font file that contains a continuous design space, so any weight, width, or other axis value between the extremes can be requested.
useWhen: you need many weights without many files

name: Variation axis
definition: One dimension a variable font can move along, named by a four-letter tag: lowercase for the five registered axes, uppercase for custom ones.
useWhen: naming a single dial inside a variable font

name: Velocity skew
definition: Skewing or stretching content in proportion to how fast the page is scrolling and easing it back to square when the scroll stops, so speed shows up in the shape of the content.
useWhen: scroll speed itself should be visible

sources.title: GSAP forums: skew on scroll velocity

notes: Squash and stretch applied to a scroller: the same animation principle, driven by input velocity rather than a curve.

name: Verbosity
definition: How much a screen reader says about each thing it reaches, a user setting that decides whether your carefully written description is heard at all.
useWhen: arguing about how much detail a label should carry

name: Vernacular web
definition: The amateur homepage look of the GeoCities era: tiled backgrounds, sparkle GIFs, under construction signs, midi music, and hit counters.
useWhen: the hand-made amateur homepage look
notes: The phrase comes from Olia Lialina's essay A Vernacular Web; that attribution was not verified this sweep and should be checked before publishing.

name: Vertical rhythm
definition: Spacing every block of text by multiples of one line height so the page keeps an even beat from top to bottom.
useWhen: spacing paragraphs and headings by one consistent unit

sources.title: What the Font are Vertical Rhythm and Modular Scale?

name: Vertical writing mode
definition: Setting lines to run top to bottom in columns rather than left to right, as traditional Chinese, Japanese, and Korean typography does.
useWhen: typesetting CJK text in columns

name: VHS aesthetic
definition: A look that imitates a worn videotape: tracking bands, smeared color bleeding past edges, interlace comb artifacts, and burned-in timecode or REC overlays.
useWhen: artifacts of magnetic tape used as decoration
notes: Distinct from scanlines (CRT raster) and from glitch (digital failure): the artifacts here are magnetic and horizontal.

name: Vibrancy
definition: Apple's treatment where foreground colour samples the blurred content behind a material, so labels on a translucent panel shift with whatever they cover.
useWhen: foreground colour that reacts to the blur behind it

sources.title: Apple HIG: Dark Mode (vibrancy and materials)

notes: Related to the existing glassmorphism entry; vibrancy is the platform mechanism, glassmorphism is the aesthetic.

name: Video player
definition: A framed video with the controls needed to play, seek, mute and caption it, sized so the controls never crowd the picture.
useWhen: video is the content and the reader controls playback
notes: media-controls already covers the control bar in isolation; this is the framed player around it, which is where poster frames, aspect ratio and caption placement live.

name: View progress timeline
definition: A scroll timeline measured by one element's passage through the scrollport, with named ranges for entering, being contained, covering, and exiting.
useWhen: the animation should track one element, not the whole page
notes: Also carries the word 'scrollport', which may deserve its own layout-category entry.

name: Viewport
definition: The visible rectangle of a page inside the browser window, excluding the browser's own bars, and the unit basis for vh and vw.
useWhen: the visible window, not the whole document
notes: The layout versus visual viewport split, and the small, large and dynamic viewport units, are the interesting part.

name: Virtual keyboard
definition: The on screen keyboard a device raises for a field, whose key set the field itself chooses by declaring what kind of value it wants.
useWhen: the field type decides which keys a reader is given
notes: The design decision is upstream in the field: an email keyboard with an @ key, a numeric pad for a code. Also the thing that eats half the viewport and moves the submit button.

name: Visual balance
definition: The distribution of visual weight across a composition, reached by mirroring elements, by setting one large element against several small ones, or by radiating from a centre.
useWhen: saying why a layout feels tippy or settled

sources.title: Design Principles: Compositional, Symmetrical And Asymmetrical Balance, Smashing Magazine

notes: Visual weight is folded in as an alias but may deserve splitting out: it is the property, balance is the arrangement.

name: Visual hierarchy
definition: The ordering of elements by visual weight, size, contrast, position and spacing, so a reader learns what matters most without being told.
useWhen: deciding what a reader should notice first
notes: Cross category: recorded here because layout is one of its main levers, but aesthetic or pattern may be the better home. Merge candidate with whatever the aesthetic sweep produces.

name: Voice control
definition: Operating an interface by speaking control names or numbered overlays, which makes the visible wording of a control its address.
useWhen: the reader clicks by saying the button's name

name: Watermark
definition: Repeating faint text or a mark tiled across content to claim it or to mark it as a draft or a preview.
useWhen: faint repeated text laid over content

name: Waveform
definition: An audio track drawn as a row of amplitude bars, used both to show what is in the file and as the surface you scrub along.
useWhen: audio drawn as bars you can scrub

name: Web font
definition: A font file downloaded by the page rather than taken from the reader's device, declared in CSS and delivered like any other asset.
useWhen: type the page ships rather than borrows

name: Welcome mat
definition: A full width introduction shown on first entry to a feature, listing what is new or what to set up, with a way to skip it for good.
useWhen: a first run introduction to a whole feature
notes: Salesforce named it and Open UI's matrix picked the name up, which is the only reason it has any currency outside Salesforce.

name: Wheel picker
definition: A spinning drum of values that snaps to the item under a fixed selection line, the iOS way of choosing from a short list.
useWhen: the iOS drum you spin to pick a value
notes: Strong tail candidate and a good demo: scroll snap plus a fixed selection band is the whole thing.

name: Whitespace
definition: The empty area between and around elements, treated as an active design material rather than as leftover space.
useWhen: the empty space doing the grouping work
notes: Whitespace need not be white; that misreading is worth a line in the article.

name: Wide gamut
definition: Colour beyond what sRGB can express, addressed in CSS through spaces such as display-p3 and rec2020 and shown only on displays that reach that far.
useWhen: reaching for colours sRGB cannot express

sources.title: Wide Gamut Color in CSS with Display-P3

notes: Radix notes alpha blending differs in P3 from sRGB, which is a good disambiguation hook.

name: Widget
definition: A small, glanceable view of an app placed on a system surface such as a home screen or desktop, sized in fixed slots rather than freely.
useWhen: app content is useful without opening the app
notes: Worth disambiguating in the article: ARIA also calls any composite control a widget, which is a different word wearing the same spelling.

name: Widow
definition: A short last line of a paragraph, often a single word, stranded at the top of the next column or page.
useWhen: naming a stranded last line at the top of a column

sources.title: An end to typographic widows on the web (Clagnut)

notes: Widow and orphan are defined in opposite directions by different sources; the entry has to say so.

name: Window controls
definition: The cluster of close, minimise and zoom controls in a window's title bar, three coloured dots on macOS and three glyphs on Windows.
useWhen: the close, minimise and maximise cluster
notes: Note the platform split in the third button: macOS calls it zoom, Windows calls it maximize, and they do not do the same thing.

name: Window size class
definition: A named bucket for how much width an app window has (compact, medium, expanded), used instead of raw device categories.
useWhen: reasoning about window width, not device type
notes: The point of the term is that a phone in split screen is compact and a tablet in split screen may also be compact; device is the wrong unit.

name: Windows Aero
definition: The Windows Vista and 7 look built on translucent glass window frames, soft outer glows, reflections, and animated window transitions.
useWhen: see-through window chrome from the Vista and 7 era
notes: Named separately from Frutiger Aero: Aero is the Microsoft product design language, Frutiger Aero the wider cultural aesthetic it belongs to.

name: Wipe
definition: A transition where a moving edge or mask travels across the frame, replacing what was there with what comes next.
useWhen: a reveal should have a visible leading edge

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

name: Wizard
definition: A flow broken into ordered steps with back and next controls, where each step validates before the next one is allowed.
useWhen: a long task split into ordered steps
notes: Arguably a pattern rather than a component. Recorded here because most systems ship it as a component; the merge step may reassign it.

name: Word break
definition: Whether a long unbroken string is allowed to split mid-word rather than overflow its container, and where that split may happen.
useWhen: a long URL or token is bursting out of its box

name: Word spacing
definition: The width of the gaps between words, which justification stretches and which, set too wide, opens rivers down a paragraph.
useWhen: the gaps between words, not between letters

name: X-height
definition: The height of a lowercase x in a typeface, measured from the baseline, which is what makes two fonts at the same point size look different sizes.
useWhen: explaining why two fonts at the same size look different

name: Y2K aesthetic
definition: The turn of the millennium look of chrome type, bubble shapes, translucent plastic, and lens flares, revived as a web and app style.
useWhen: chrome, bubbles, and translucent plastic futurism

name: Yellow fade technique
definition: Washing a just-changed element in colour and letting it fade back out, so a change made without a page reload is still noticed where it happened.
useWhen: showing which thing on the page just changed

sources.title: Signal vs. Noise: Web Interface Design Tip: The Yellow Fade Technique

notes: 37signals, 2004, for Basecamp: the canonical answer to 'the page did not reload, so what changed?'. The site has NO term for this at all today (no highlight-fade, no value-flash, no flash-on-update anywhere). HONESTY DUTY: the colour is not the point and the article must say so, and a fade that is the ONLY signal of a change fails WCAG 1.4.1, so link use-of-color.

name: Yo-yo loop
definition: A repeating animation that plays forward then backward instead of jumping back to the start, so a loop has no visible seam.
useWhen: a loop must repeat without a snap back to frame one

name: Z pattern
definition: The scanning shape on sparse pages: across the top, diagonally down to the lower left, then across the bottom to the final call to action.
useWhen: laying out a sparse page with one clear action

name: Zebra striping
definition: Alternating row backgrounds in a table so the eye can track a single row across many columns.
useWhen: shading every other row of a table
notes: Could reasonably be filed under aesthetic or accessibility rather than component; recorded here because it only exists inside tables.

name: Zero UI
definition: A paradigm where the screen stops being the interface and the interaction happens through voice, gesture, presence, or sensors, so the system responds without anything to look at.
useWhen: the interaction has no screen to design

sources.title: Designer Daily: The invisible interface, an introduction to designing for Zero UI
Microsoft Advertising: Zero UI, the invisible interface revolution
UX Planet: Zero UI, how to design invisible interfaces

notes: Cross-category: recorded as pattern, surfaced by an aesthetic sweep from a style catalog that files it as a look. Nothing to demo on a web page, hence demo none.

name: Zero-width space
definition: An invisible character that takes no width and adds a legal break point, letting a long string wrap without showing a hyphen.
useWhen: breaking a long identifier with no visible mark

name: Zigzag layout
definition: Alternating rows that flip which side the image and the text sit on, so the eye zigzags down a list of features.
useWhen: a run of feature blocks that would otherwise read as a list

name: Zoom transition
definition: A presentation that scales a tapped element up into the full view it opens, so the destination appears to come from the thing that was touched.
useWhen: the destination should visibly come from what was tapped
notes: Merge candidate with container-transform and shared-element-transition; kept because the platform word people search is 'zoom transition'.

name: Miller columns
definition: A browsing layout of side-by-side columns where selecting an item in one column fills the next with its children, keeping the whole path visible.
useWhen: browsing a deep hierarchy with the path kept visible

name: Blockquote
definition: A passage quoted from another source and set off from the running text as its own block, carrying the attribution with it.
useWhen: quoting a source at paragraph length
sweptFrom: canonicalize 2026-08-15: split from pull-quote per component.gallery distinction

name: Abbreviation
definition: A shortened form of a word or phrase, from Dr. to NASA, with its own typographic conventions and an expansion assistive tech can speak.
useWhen: shortened forms need setting, marking up, or expanding
sweptFrom: user wishlist 2026-08-15, shaped in canonicalize follow-up

name: Pixel density
definition: How many physical pixels a display packs into an inch, and the reason a CSS pixel is a unit of measure rather than a dot on the screen.
useWhen: raster crispness, 2x assets, or dpi/ppi confusion is on the table
sweptFrom: user wishlist 2026-08-15, shaped in canonicalize follow-up

name: Chamfer
definition: A corner cut flat at an angle instead of rounded, the sharp-edged sibling of border-radius that reads industrial, military, or sci-fi.
useWhen: corners should read machined rather than soft
sweptFrom: user wishlist 2026-08-15, shaped in canonicalize follow-up
article must disambiguate the existing bevel term (3D edge) from corner-shape: bevel (flat cut)

name: Interface metaphor
definition: Explaining a system by dressing it as something the user already knows: the desktop, the trash can, the folder, the shopping cart.
useWhen: a familiar concept is carrying the explanation of an unfamiliar system

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group: Metaphors in UX

sweptFrom: user wishlist 2026-08-15, shaped in canonicalize follow-up
reshaped from "figures of speech"; the idiom/localization half belongs to plain-language

name: Axis
definition: The ruled edge of a chart that maps position to value: scale, ticks, and labels that make the marks readable as numbers.
useWhen: discussing tick density, label rotation, or what scale a chart hangs on

sources.title: Fundamentals of Data Visualization: Coordinate systems and axes

notes: Gridlines and tick marks live in this article rather than as their own terms (a resting gridline is a hairline; the stage cannot ring one anyway).

name: Chart legend
definition: The key beside a chart that decodes series colors and symbols into names, and the first thing direct labeling tries to delete.
useWhen: naming the color key of a chart, not a fieldset caption
notes: Bare "legend" belongs to fieldset (authored alias); both articles owe a disambiguation sentence. Contrast with direct-labeling is the teaching.

name: Reference line
definition: A line drawn at a meaningful value across a chart: a target, a threshold, an average, a before-and-after moment.
useWhen: a chart needs a benchmark the eye can compare marks against
notes: HAIRLINE LAW applies: a 1px line at rest is invisible to the stage, so the specimen draws it at 2px or asserts its label.

name: Chart annotation
definition: A note pinned onto the data itself: a callout, arrow, or highlighted span that tells the reader what to see in the chart.
useWhen: the takeaway should be written on the chart, not left to the caption
notes: Disambiguate from accessibility-annotation (handoff spec notes) and ruby-annotation (typography); "annotation" stays unclaimed as a bare alias.

name: Error bar
definition: Whiskers on a mark showing the range a value could plausibly take, so a chart does not imply precision it does not have.
useWhen: a chart states an estimate and honesty requires showing the spread

sources.title: Fundamentals of Data Visualization: Visualizing uncertainty

notes: The umbrella (uncertainty display) lives in this article; gradations and bands are variants, not separate terms.

name: Truncated axis
definition: Starting a value axis above zero so differences look bigger than they are; honest for lines and dots, a lie for bars.
useWhen: judging whether cutting the y-axis exaggerates or clarifies

sources.title: Fundamentals of Data Visualization: Proportional ink

notes: Prime data-pose specimen: mount at the honest zero baseline, offer the deceptive cut as a captioned counter-example state, like dark-pattern’s checkout. Bare "baseline" belongs to typography.

name: Dual axis
definition: Two value axes sharing one plot so two series can be compared, and a free knob for manufacturing whatever correlation you like.
useWhen: someone proposes a second y-axis and the scales question needs asking

sources.title: Datawrapper: Why not to use two axes

notes: Same honesty machinery as truncated-axis; the two are round-mates when authored.

name: Direct labeling
definition: Writing series names next to the data instead of in a legend, trading a lookup for a glance.
useWhen: few series and room at the line ends make the legend deletable

sources.title: Fundamentals of Data Visualization: Redundant coding

notes: Contrast pair with chart-legend; author together and cross-link one sentence each way.

name: Brushing
definition: Dragging a selection across one chart to highlight the same records in every linked view.
useWhen: coordinated views should answer a selection made in any one of them
notes: The drag is player-performable (law 4); linked views make a natural two-panel specimen.

name: Small multiples
definition: The same small chart repeated in a grid, once per category, so comparison happens by eye movement instead of overplotting.
useWhen: one chart would need too many series to stay readable
notes: Alias fence: "facets"/"faceting" belong to faceted-filter.

name: Chart aspect ratio
definition: How wide a chart is for its height, which sets the slopes of its lines; banking to 45 degrees keeps rates of change readable.
useWhen: a line chart reads too steep or too flat for the story it tells
notes: Alias fence: bare "aspect ratio" belongs to aspect-ratio-box.

name: Chartjunk
definition: Tufte’s word for ink that decorates a chart without carrying data: 3D bevels, gradient fills, mascots, gridline thickets.
useWhen: a chart’s decoration is fighting its data
notes: Contrast pair with data-ink-ratio (the vice and the measure); author together. A before/after strip is the natural specimen.

name: Data-ink ratio
definition: Tufte’s measure of chart economy: the share of ink that would be missed if erased, with everything else a candidate for deletion.
useWhen: deciding what a chart can lose before it loses meaning

name: Chart description
definition: The text alternative for a chart: a summary of the takeaway plus access to the underlying values, not a recital of the pixels.
useWhen: a chart needs to work for readers who cannot see it
notes: Bare "alt text" belongs to alt-text and "long description" to long-description; this is the chart-shaped practice above both.

name: CMYK
definition: The subtractive print color model: cyan, magenta, and yellow inks plus a key black, mixing by absorbing light, with a gamut narrower than any screen's.
useWhen: designing for ink on paper instead of light on glass
notes: Screen designers meet it at print handoff: the out-of-gamut warning in a color picker is usually a CMYK boundary. 'Subtractive color' is left unclaimed in case an additive/subtractive pair term is ever wanted.

name: Natural language interface
definition: An interface whose input is ordinary language, typed or spoken: the user states an intent in their own words and the system parses it, instead of picking from controls.
useWhen: the input is a sentence, not a selection
notes: 'Conversational interface' is deliberately not claimed as an alias: the chat-shaped, turn-taking pattern is its own possible term, while this is the input paradigm, one-shot included (a search box that accepts intent is an NLI with no conversation).

name: Scroll edge fade
definition: A gradient mask at the edge of a scroll container that fades clipped content out, hinting that more lies past the edge without drawing a control.
useWhen: showing a list continues past its clipped edge

sources.title: Lea Verou: Pure CSS scrolling shadows with background-attachment local

notes: 'Scroll shadow', the shadow-painted variant of the same affordance, is left unclaimed: likely an alias at authoring time, possibly a variantOf if the author finds the usage distinct. The marquee specimen already paints edge fades as scenery.

name: 10-foot UI
definition: The register for screens read from a couch: focus-driven navigation with a remote, oversized type and cards, horizontal rails, and safe margins for TV overscan.
useWhen: the screen is across the room and the input is a remote
notes: Shaped from the wishlist's 'Game/Console UI': the game half is already covered (diegetic-interface, fictional-user-interface, hud-panel), and 'console UI' is claimed by terminal-aesthetic as the other console, so the uncovered sense is the TV register. Never take 'console UI' as an alias. Slug spells the number out after sixty-thirty-ten-rule's precedent.

name: Signed distance field
definition: A texture storing each pixel's distance to a shape's edge rather than its color, so glyphs and icons rendered from it stay crisp at any scale on the GPU.
useWhen: text or icons must scale sharply inside a GPU pipeline

sources.title: Chris Green (Valve), SIGGRAPH 2007: Improved alpha-tested magnification for vector textures

notes: Filed under typography because UI meets SDFs at text rendering (game UI, canvas, WebGL); the raymarching and generative senses are wider but not this site’s angle. Demo thought: the same glyph as a bitmap and as an SDF on one zoom ride. Not the gooey effect: that is usually the SVG blur plus alpha-contrast trick, though a smooth-minimum union of SDFs is the shader-land way to the same goo, so the two are cousins under implicit surfaces.

name: Identicon
definition: A generated default avatar derived deterministically from an identifier, so the same account always gets the same abstract pattern without uploading anything.
useWhen: an account needs a face before the user provides one
notes: Don Park coined it in 2007 for IP-hash patterns; GitHub made the 5x5 symmetric-pixel form famous. The seeded determinism is a gift to the specimen: identical on every identify run by construction, and the demo can show the same handle always drawing the same face. Generative art that is pure interface, which is what earned it a record where raymarching was rejected.

name: Vignette
definition: A gradual darkening toward the edges of an image that pulls the eye to the centre, borrowed from lens falloff and applied deliberately for focus and mood.
useWhen: the edges of an image quietly dimmed to hold focus
notes: The article should draw the scrim boundary: a scrim is functional (text protection, usually one-sided), a vignette is compositional (focus and mood, radially symmetric); UI heroes often carry both and call the pair a vignette.

name: Particle background
definition: An ambient decorative background of many small moving agents: drifting dots, linked constellations, flocks, or starfields animating behind the page content.
useWhen: the backdrop is alive with drifting points

sources.title: particles.js: a lightweight library for particles
Craig Reynolds: Boids, background and update

notes: The umbrella artifact for the agent-driven background; algorithm names ride as aliases after gooey-effect precedent, and boids (Reynolds 1986: separation, alignment, cohesion) gets its paragraph here per the raymarching rule. The interface content is real: prefers-reduced-motion is load-bearing (a full-viewport ambient field is the canonical vestibular offender), it spends CPU and battery while the page is idle, and text over a moving field has no stable contrast ground. Digital rain is deliberately not an alias: it reads as its own icon in the terminal and cyberpunk family.

name: Transparency checkerboard
definition: The grey and white checker grid a design tool paints behind transparent regions, a convention so universal that the pattern itself now reads as meaning alpha.
useWhen: showing that a region is transparent rather than white
notes: The alpha-indicating tool convention, not the aesthetic motif: chequerboard floors stay prose inside vaporwave and acid-graphics, and the alternating content rows are zigzag-layout (which now carries the "checkerboard layout" alias).

name: Press-drag-release
definition: Operating a menu in one gesture: pressing the trigger opens it, dragging moves through the items while the button stays down, and releasing over an item commits it.
useWhen: a menu or select should answer one continuous press as well as two clicks

aliases.name: press to open, release to select

notes: The original Macintosh menu-tracking behavior: before Mac OS 8 it was the ONLY way menus worked, and the OS 8 addition of the two-click mode was named "sticky menus", which the article uses as the named contrast rather than an alias. Modern natives keep both paths live (macOS selects and menus, iOS long-press context menus with slide-to-select); Radix Select famously reimplemented it for the web. The up-event commit is what WCAG 2.5.2 pointer cancellation blesses: sliding off and releasing is the escape hatch. Fences: marking-menu keeps the radial gesture-as-command sense; long-press is the touch trigger, not the tracking. HIG source verified on URL resolution only (JS-rendered). Demo is performable today: a drag step from the trigger through the open menu to an item IS the gesture, and the two-click sticky path contrasts it in the same specimen; the demo wires pointerdown-open plus pointerup-commit with the law-22 capture guard.
